title: Two approaches, one question
description: Two alternatives align around the same question, then matched attributes connect across a center divider. One authored difference receives a final underline without declaring an automatic winner.
creativeDirection: Within six seconds, two labeled halves slide apart to reveal a shared question in the center. Matching attribute pairs enter on the same horizontal baselines, their center brackets draw simultaneously, and the nominated contrast expands into a single readable comparison band. Both alternatives remain visible during the resolved hold before the shared exit envelope.
goodFor: Compare two approaches against the same criteria
Explain centralized versus distributed responsibility
Contrast two definitions before choosing terminology
Compare who supplies operations, maintenance, and hosting for the same software
Compare vendor-side and device-side responsibility without erasing either side
intent: Make the difference between two alternatives easy to see on equal terms.

inputs.name: question
inputs.default: How is a fictional draft reviewed?
inputs.description: The shared question answered by both alternatives.
inputs.constraints: 1..60 characters

inputs.name: alternatives
inputs.description: The left and right alternatives in display order.
inputs.constraints: Exactly 2 items; unique IDs <= 20 characters; labels 1..24 characters

inputs.name: criteria
inputs.description: Authored pairs of qualitative attributes, aligned by criterion.
inputs.constraints: 1..3 items; unique IDs <= 20 characters; labels <= 20 characters; each side <= 34 characters

inputs.name: focusCriterionId
inputs.description: The criterion that receives the final expanded contrast band.
inputs.constraints: Must equal a criteria ID

inputs.name: comparisonLabel
inputs.description: Caption beneath the resolved comparison.
inputs.constraints: 0..48 characters

inputs.name: showPairBrackets
inputs.description: Show matching brackets that tie each left and right attribute to its criterion.
inputs.constraints: boolean

bindingExample.shortSourceText: In a fictional writing club, solo review uses a self-check while pair review adds a shared discussion.

inputBindings.question: How is a fictional draft reviewed?

distinction: Unlike stagger-cards, the action is the synchronized alignment and expansion of matched differences. Unlike bar-race, it compares supplied qualitative attributes without ranking or invented numeric scores.
limits: Exactly two alternatives and at most three criteria keep both sides readable in six seconds.
Equal panel areas express equal editorial attention, not equal effectiveness, cost, or prevalence.
The nominated contrast is supplied by the author and is not inferred from the text.
Free access to source code is not zero operating cost. Comparison labels must account for the supplied hosting and maintenance responsibilities without inventing monetary amounts.
Moving computation to a user device changes the resource owner. It does not establish zero total cost, zero energy, or that one option is universally cheaper.
verificationFocus: Changing the focused criterion moves the comparison emphasis to that row while both alternatives and every other criterion remain visible.

sourceRefs.locator: pages 29-30, Open source offering / self-hosting mitigation
sourceRefs.rationale: The plan distinguishes access to software from the resources and operational work required to run it.
The strategy attributes savings to moving processing away from the vendor cloud, which does not eliminate device-side costs.

title: Capability by capability
description: A compact table reveals explicit capability states one line at a time, then holds an authored row or column focus. Supported, unavailable, conditional, and unknown states remain visually distinct.
creativeDirection: A table skeleton and option headings settle first. A narrow horizontal rule advances through the capability rows, resolving all cells in each row together so the audience compares like with like. The final focus opens a bracket around one selected column or row while every other cell remains legible, followed by the common opaque exit.
goodFor: Compare feature support across a small set of alternatives
Explain what each plan includes
Separate conditional support from unknown information
Compare task needs with an explicitly supplied capability set
Explain fit across affordability, usability, and lifecycle coverage
Show whether affordability and defined quality requirements are both met in an authored example
Compare local and network-dependent operations
Show unknown or planned capability support honestly
intent: Compare alternatives using the same explicit list of capabilities.

inputs.name: options
inputs.description: Column definitions for fictional alternatives.
inputs.constraints: 2..3 items; unique IDs <= 20 characters; labels 1..18 characters

inputs.name: capabilities
inputs.description: Rows and their explicit states, including optional qualification notes.
inputs.constraints: 2..5 rows; unique row IDs <= 20 characters; labels <= 22 characters; exactly one cell per option ID; notes <= 18 characters

inputs.name: stateLabels
inputs.description: Editable visible legend text for all four semantic states.
inputs.constraints: Each label 1..14 characters

inputs.name: focus
inputs.description: An editorial focus after the full comparison is visible.
inputs.constraints: For row or column, ID must exist in the corresponding collection; for none, ID must be empty

inputs.name: showNotes
inputs.description: Display authored cell notes next to the state glyphs.
inputs.constraints: boolean

inputs.name: caption
inputs.description: The context caption shown above the matrix.
inputs.constraints: 0..48 characters

bindingExample.shortSourceText: The fictional pocket and desk kits both contain a pencil, but their ruler and refill options differ.

distinction: The grid carries a two-dimensional comparison contract and four explicit cell meanings. It is neither a cohort dot-matrix nor source-to-destination schema-mapping, and its choreography compares each line item across all alternatives.
limits: Cells are categorical statements, not performance scores or quantities.
Unknown must never be rendered as absent, and conditional cells require meaningful source qualifications.
At most three options and five rows fit the intended six-second overview.
A capability state is a supplied statement about a specific context and version. Do not infer market-wide absence, universal superiority, or current competitor support from a strategic comparison.
Qualitative affordability requires a stated audience and context; included features are not proof that a plan is affordable to every team.
A quality row needs an explicit criterion and source. Included affordability and quality cells do not prove that every organization can afford the tool or that it is safe.
Unavailable, conditional and unknown must stay distinct. Planned capability is not currently supported.
verificationFocus: Included, absent, conditional and unknown cells have four distinct marks. Unknown never appears as absent. Switching row or column focus changes only the designated emphasis, not capability values. Source-derived variant: Use independent states for local querying, remote invitation and optional synchronization; an offline flag must not convert every row into supported.

sourceRefs.locator: pages 3-5, The Market / The Problem / Solution
sourceRefs.rationale: The strategy frames the problem as a mismatch between organizational needs and available tool capability, complexity, and cost.
A comparison table evaluates audience, scale, usability, functions, and self-serve access.
The source rejects a mandatory choice between affordable access and dependable tools.
Local operations and remote server procedures have different availability.

title: Choose the replacement
description: An initially proposed option fails a stated criterion, moves aside, and hands the same position to a selected replacement. The rejected option stays visible with its authored reason.
creativeDirection: A proposed label settles into a central selection slot beneath a criterion. A small strike crosses its selection marker, then the option slides into a left-side rejected position as its reason appears. The replacement enters the vacated slot from the right, receives a selection bracket, and holds with its rationale and the original choice still readable before the shared fade.
goodFor: Explain why an initial approach was discarded
Introduce a replacement tool or technique
Show a choice changing when a constraint becomes explicit
intent: Explain a deliberate replacement through a clear selection criterion.

inputs.name: criterion
inputs.description: The criterion used to explain the replacement.
inputs.constraints: 1..58 characters

inputs.name: rejected
inputs.description: The original option and the authored reason it is not selected.
inputs.constraints: Label 1..24 characters; reason 1..42 characters

inputs.name: replacement
inputs.description: The chosen replacement and the authored selection reason.
inputs.constraints: Label 1..24 characters; reason 1..42 characters

inputs.name: decisionLabels
inputs.description: Editable state labels accompanying the rejection and selection marks.
inputs.constraints: Each label 1..16 characters

inputs.name: showCriterionLink
inputs.description: Draw a short brace between the criterion and the replacement rationale.
inputs.constraints: boolean

inputs.name: rejectionMark
inputs.description: Choose the visual treatment of the rejected selection marker.
inputs.constraints: One of cross or strike; never strike through the reason text

bindingExample.shortSourceText: For a fictional traveling workshop, set aside the fixed easel and choose a folding easel because it packs for the trip.

distinction: Unlike status-cycle, two distinct alternatives exchange one selection role and retain a visible reason for rejection. The hero action is the replacement of an option, not progress through states.
limits: Exactly one rejection and one replacement are shown.
Selection is authored, not calculated from the wording or treated as a universal recommendation.
Rejection styling must not make the rejected option or rationale unreadable.
verificationFocus: At the hold, the replacement occupies the selection slot and the rejected option retains its rejection mark and rationale; changing the rejection style changes the mark.

title: Choose one branch
description: One explicit decision opens into a small number of labeled alternatives. An authored choice closes the unused gates and carries one marker to the selected outcome.
creativeDirection: The decision prompt enters at the root and two to four equal branches draw outward with condition labels. A single marker pauses at the junction while the selected condition receives emphasis. The unused branch gates close gently, the marker travels down the chosen branch, and its outcome opens into a final hold while alternate outcomes remain subdued and labeled.
goodFor: Explain an if-then choice
Trace one scenario through a decision rule
Show why one of several possible routes is taken
Explain one supplied local-or-remote execution choice
Show how a declared eligibility condition selects an illustrative plan path
Explain a decision constrained by an explicitly stated community concern
Show a principled next action in a bounded scenario
intent: Show one chosen path and the condition that selects it.

inputs.name: prompt
inputs.default: Where does the fictional sketch belong?
inputs.description: The single decision being evaluated.
inputs.constraints: 1..52 characters

inputs.name: branches
inputs.description: Mutually presented alternatives and their authored outcomes.
inputs.constraints: 2..4 items; unique IDs <= 20 characters; conditions <= 24 characters; outcomes <= 24 characters

inputs.name: selectedBranchId
inputs.description: The one branch taken by the illustrated scenario.
inputs.constraints: Must equal exactly one branches ID

inputs.name: scenarioLabel
inputs.description: Label attached to the single marker moving through the decision.
inputs.constraints: 1..32 characters

inputs.name: selectionLabel
inputs.description: Qualification accompanying the selected outcome.
inputs.constraints: 0..32 characters

inputs.name: showUnchosenOutcomes
inputs.description: Keep the alternative outcomes visible during the selected-path hold.
inputs.constraints: boolean

bindingExample.shortSourceText: In the fictional sketch workflow, a sketch ready to share goes to the review folder rather than the notebook or archive.

inputBindings.prompt: Where does the fictional sketch belong?

distinction: Unlike node-traversal, this exposes the decision conditions and explicitly closes untaken branches. It is a bounded choice at one junction, not a tour of arbitrary graph connectivity.
limits: Only one decision level and one selected branch are supported.
The author supplies the choice; conditions are labels rather than executable rules.
Branch lengths and angles do not encode probability, duration, or preference.

An authored branch is not a cost optimizer, legal eligibility assessment, or automatic classifier. No sector, intent, affordability, or trustworthiness may be inferred from dataset names or descriptive text.
If illustrating execution placement, retain the stated feasibility and data-boundary conditions. Do not imply that every task can run on either side.
Branch conditions and moral priorities are authored. The animation neither determines ethical correctness nor infers absence of harm.
verificationFocus: Only selectedBranchId receives the traveling marker and selected outcome emphasis; hiding unchosen outcomes removes those labels without changing the chosen branch.

sourceRefs.rationale: The plan proposes choosing local or remote processing according to data need and cost.
The strategy proposes differing plan conditions by declared use case.

sourceRefs.locator: pages 2, 6, 7 and 8 / technical ethics and next action
sourceRefs.rationale: The source treats community wellbeing and honest acknowledgment of implications as decision priorities.

title: A choice has two sides
description: A selected approach rotates into view with a benefit on one face and a concession on the other. Both faces open into a single hinge so the final choice retains its tradeoff.
creativeDirection: A slim vertical hinge appears beneath the approach label. Its left leaf unfolds to show the gained qualities, then the hinge pivots just enough to reveal the right leaf with the concessions. Both settle open at equal readable size, and a short priority statement locks beneath the hinge as the final hold. The angle is fixed editorial motion rather than a numeric balance.
goodFor: Explain a choice that gains one property at another's expense
State the downside alongside an advantage
Make a design rationale honest about its constraints
Explain a relationship-intensive service choice with its time requirement
Keep a mission constraint visible alongside a growth opportunity
intent: Keep a chosen approach's benefit and concession visible together.

inputs.name: approach
inputs.description: The approach whose tradeoff is explained.
inputs.constraints: 1..40 characters

inputs.name: gains
inputs.description: Qualitative benefits on the first leaf.
inputs.constraints: 1..3 items; unique IDs <= 20 characters; labels 1..32 characters

inputs.name: concessions
inputs.description: Qualitative concessions on the second leaf.
inputs.constraints: 1..3 items; unique IDs <= 20 characters; labels 1..32 characters

inputs.name: sideLabels
inputs.description: Headings for the two sides of the tradeoff.
inputs.constraints: Each label 1..22 characters

inputs.name: priorityStatement
inputs.default: For this example, portability comes first
inputs.description: Authored context explaining why the choice is acceptable.
inputs.constraints: 1..58 characters

inputs.name: revealOrder
inputs.description: Choose which side of the tradeoff the audience encounters first.
inputs.constraints: One of gain-first or concession-first

bindingExample.shortSourceText: The fictional pocket notebook favors portability while giving up room for large sketches.

inputBindings.priorityStatement: For this example, portability comes first

distinction: A single hinged argument exposes an inseparable benefit and concession. It does not rank alternatives like bar-race or merely reveal a sibling collection like stagger-cards.
limits: The number of listed points is not a score and cannot establish which side outweighs the other.
Leaf sizes and hinge angles carry no quantitative meaning.
No conclusion is calculated; the priority statement must be authored and qualified for its context.
A stated strategic preference does not establish investor duties, future behavior, customer conversion, financial return, or moral superiority. Keep the authored context and concession visible.
verificationFocus: Gain and concession text both remain at the hold; reversing revealOrder reverses their entrance order without treating the hinge angle as a numerical score.

sourceRefs.rationale: The strategy balances relationship-intensive trust building against the effort required to scale it.

sourceRefs.locator: pages 27-28, Cash distribution and work culture
sourceRefs.rationale: The strategy discusses slower near-term expansion alongside a long-term operating preference.
The plan frames funding and customer choices in terms of preserving the intended social mission.

title: The rule and its exception
description: A standard path meets a clearly labeled rule gate, while one named exception opens a separate route. The two outcomes stay distinct so the exception never silently changes the general rule.
creativeDirection: The standard rule and straight destination appear first. A single labeled case approaches the gate, pauses as its exception condition opens a side latch, and follows a curved detour to the exception outcome. The standard path remains intact and visible throughout. The final hold brackets the case, condition, and special outcome before the shared exit.
goodFor: Explain an exception to a general workflow
Qualify a broad statement with one explicit special case
Show why a named case requires different handling
intent: State a general rule while making a specific exception explicit.

inputs.name: rule

default.label: Return borrowed tools to the shelf

inputs.description: The general rule and its ordinary destination.
inputs.constraints: Rule label 1..48 characters; outcome 1..24 characters

inputs.name: exception
inputs.description: The explicit condition and special destination.
inputs.constraints: Condition 1..34 characters; outcome 1..24 characters

inputs.name: caseLabel
inputs.description: The single illustrative case that takes the exception route.
inputs.constraints: 1..34 characters

inputs.name: pathLabels
inputs.description: Visible words that distinguish the standard and exception paths.
inputs.constraints: Each label 1..18 characters

inputs.name: showStandardReference
inputs.description: Show a stationary unlabeled reference marker at the standard destination to clarify the normal path.
inputs.constraints: boolean; marker has no population meaning

inputs.name: detourSide
inputs.description: Place the exception route above or below the standard path.
inputs.constraints: One of above or below

bindingExample.shortSourceText: In a fictional studio, borrowed tools return to the shelf unless a part is loose, in which case they go to the repair tray.

rule.label: Return borrowed tools to the shelf

distinction: The semantic structure is a standing rule plus a visibly gated exception, not an unqualified pipeline or an arbitrary network path. Only the exceptional case moves.
limits: One general rule and one exception are supported.
The reference and moving markers are illustrative roles, not a sample population or exception frequency.
The animation does not validate whether a rule or its exception is correct.
verificationFocus: The case follows the exception route while the standard route remains intact; switching detourSide mirrors the route without swapping the outcomes.

title: From reasons to conclusion
description: A few authored premises form a visible support beneath one conclusion. The connecting language states whether they support, require, or merely suggest the conclusion.
creativeDirection: Two or three premise strips arrive separately along the lower third. Their ends extend and join into a single bridge deck, with a central connector label appearing only once the premises are readable. The conclusion rises onto that deck and holds above all visible premises. Nothing is transported through the bridge; it is an explicit visual model of an argument's support.
goodFor: Explain why a recommendation follows from stated reasons
Connect evidence to a qualified conclusion
Summarize an argument before the next chapter
intent: Show which stated reasons support an authored conclusion.

inputs.name: premises

default.text: The fictional room has one clear wall

inputs.description: The distinct reasons forming the conclusion's visual support.
inputs.constraints: 2..3 items; unique IDs <= 20 characters; text 1..48 characters

inputs.name: conclusion
inputs.default: Place the example board on that wall
inputs.description: The authored conclusion, revealed after the reasons.
inputs.constraints: 1..64 characters

inputs.name: relationship
inputs.description: Semantic relationship controlling solid, bracketed, or dashed support treatment.
inputs.constraints: One of supports, requires, or suggests; chosen explicitly by the author

inputs.name: connectorText
inputs.description: Visible connective language at the bridge joint.
inputs.constraints: 1..30 characters; must agree with relationship

inputs.name: premiseHeading
inputs.description: Qualification above the supporting premises.
inputs.constraints: 0..42 characters

inputs.name: showIndividualSupports
inputs.description: Retain a short support line from each premise to the common deck.
inputs.constraints: boolean

bindingExample.shortSourceText: The fictional room has one clear wall and everyone faces it, which supports placing the example board there.

premises.text: The fictional room has one clear wall

inputBindings.conclusion: Place the example board on that wall

distinction: Unlike source-merge, premises remain separate and readable as reasons rather than moving as data into a destination. The deck and relationship text distinguish logical support from transport or aggregation.
limits: The renderer does not prove validity, establish causality, or derive a conclusion.
At most three concise reasons fit the six-second argument.
Support geometry is rhetorical and carries no confidence score or evidence weight.
verificationFocus: The conclusion is supported by every supplied premise, and changing premise count changes the physical supports without introducing an unsupplied premise.

title: Narrow the question
description: A broad subject remains visible while a movable frame isolates the subset under discussion. Excluded topics stay outside the frame with explicit context rather than disappearing without explanation.
creativeDirection: A broad heading and a flat field of topic labels appear together. A rectangular aperture draws around the full field, then its edges contract and selected labels slide together within it while other labels remain outside. The narrowed question replaces the broad heading inside the frame. A final outside caption clarifies what is deferred before the common exit envelope.
goodFor: Define what an explainer will cover
Move from a broad subject to one bounded question
Separate current scope from deferred topics
Separate a long-term lifecycle vision from a bounded present focus
Clarify the domain and tasks an example is intended to cover
intent: Make the boundary of the current explanation explicit.

inputs.name: broadTopic
inputs.description: The broad subject introduced before narrowing.
inputs.constraints: 1..44 characters

inputs.name: topics
inputs.description: Topic labels and their explicit membership in the final scope.
inputs.constraints: 3..6 items; unique IDs <= 20 characters; labels 1..22 characters; 1..3 included and at least 1 excluded

inputs.name: focusedQuestion
inputs.description: The narrower question revealed inside the final frame.
inputs.constraints: 1..52 characters

inputs.name: outsideLabel
inputs.description: Qualification for the topics left outside the frame.
inputs.constraints: 1..34 characters

inputs.name: insideLabel
inputs.description: Label on the final scope boundary.
inputs.constraints: 1..24 characters

inputs.name: showExcludedTopics
inputs.description: Retain excluded topic labels during the final hold, with their outside qualification.
inputs.constraints: boolean

bindingExample.shortSourceText: This fictional studio explainer focuses on shelves and supply bins; lighting and seating will come later.

distinction: The explanatory action is a changing semantic boundary with explicit membership. Unlike stagger-cards or word-reveal, the labels begin visible and the animation changes which topics belong to the current question.
limits: The frame expresses topic membership, not physical geography or measured area.
Included topics are authored; the renderer performs no text classification.
This is a single narrowing step, not an animated camera zoom through a hierarchy.
Topics outside the aperture may be future, deferred, unsupported, or simply out of this explanation. Supply the correct outside label and do not imply they are shipped features.
verificationFocus: Only topics designated inside the focus lie within the final aperture; excluded topics remain outside or disappear according to the display toggle.

sourceRefs.rationale: The plan sets out a broad future lifecycle vision.
The plan says an initial product focus should be narrower and chosen through user feedback.

title: Both can be true
description: Two apparently conflicting statements first face each other, then separate into explicit contexts that explain how both can apply. The qualifier is supplied by the author and stays visible in the final arrangement.
creativeDirection: Two short claims enter on opposing horizontal tracks and stop at a central question mark. A context divider unfolds vertically, moving each claim to its own labeled region. The question mark resolves into a small joining brace with the authored qualifier below it. Both context-claim pairs hold together before the shared fade, without rewriting either claim.
goodFor: Resolve an apparent contradiction by naming context
Distinguish a generalization from a situation-specific statement
Explain why advice changes under different conditions
Separate source-code availability from access to independently curated content
Clarify that price sensitivity and willingness to pay are different statements
Separate the time spent preparing from the time needed for a later response
intent: Explain how two statements can coexist when their contexts differ.

inputs.name: statements
inputs.description: Two unchanged claims paired with the contexts that qualify them.
inputs.constraints: Exactly 2 items; unique IDs <= 20 characters; claims 1..42 characters; contexts 1..32 characters

inputs.name: openingLabel
inputs.description: The initial question between the statements.
inputs.constraints: 1..26 characters

inputs.name: qualifier
inputs.default: Different stages call for different treatment
inputs.description: The authored explanation of why the claims can coexist.
inputs.constraints: 1..64 characters

inputs.name: connectorLabel
inputs.description: Label accompanying the final joining brace.
inputs.constraints: 1..26 characters

inputs.name: contextPlacement
inputs.description: Place context labels above or below their corresponding claims.
inputs.constraints: One of above or below

inputs.name: showCentralDivider
inputs.description: Retain the divider that separates the two contexts during the hold.
inputs.constraints: boolean

bindingExample.shortSourceText: A fictional sketch can call for loose marks early and precise edges later; the two statements refer to different stages.

inputBindings.qualifier: Different stages call for different treatment

distinction: Unlike paired-contrast, this begins with apparent incompatibility and resolves it by revealing distinct scopes of truth. The semantic transformation is qualification rather than comparison or choosing a winner.
limits: The author must provide a valid contextual reconciliation; the renderer cannot establish that both claims are true.
Exactly two claims are shown, each with one context.
The graphic must not be used to hide a genuine unresolved contradiction behind decorative separation.
Show only supplied policy statements and their distinct objects. The animation does not interpret licenses, determine ownership, confer rights, or prove that any legal position is correct.
A low price, paid plan, or free offer by itself proves neither high nor low technical quality.
Separate time contexts explain how the authored statements can coexist. They do not establish a measured speed improvement or a guarantee of emergency performance.
verificationFocus: Both original claims survive unchanged under their respective context labels, and the qualifier appears after the context split.

sourceRefs.locator: pages 29-30, Open source offering and curated marketplace data
sourceRefs.rationale: The strategy distinguishes software-source availability from access to separately maintained directory content.

sourceRefs.locator: pages 11 and 14, Price sensitivity and quality positioning
sourceRefs.rationale: The plan separates willingness to pay from need for demonstrated value, and affordability from software-quality claims.
The source distinguishes deliberate preparation from readiness to act in a later urgent situation.

title: Find the common ground
description: Two different approaches lift to reveal one explicitly shared foundation. Their distinguishing traits remain attached, so commonality does not erase their differences.
creativeDirection: Two labeled structures stand apart with their distinct traits underneath. Their lower edges rise in parallel, exposing matching fragments of a shared foundation phrase. The fragments join into one continuous base spanning both structures, then short supports reconnect each approach to it. The final hold reads as two approaches resting on the same principle before the shared exit.
goodFor: Connect two different methods through a common principle
Transition from disagreement to shared requirements
Introduce a shared foundation before explaining separate implementations
intent: Reveal the shared principle beneath two distinct approaches.

inputs.name: approaches
inputs.description: Two distinct approaches and one distinguishing trait for each.
inputs.constraints: Exactly 2 items; unique IDs <= 20 characters; labels 1..24 characters; distinctions 1..36 characters

inputs.name: sharedPrinciple
inputs.description: The single authored principle revealed as their common foundation.
inputs.constraints: 1..58 characters

inputs.name: foundationLabel
inputs.description: Caption on the common base.
inputs.constraints: 1..26 characters

inputs.name: openingConnector
inputs.description: Visible connector above the initially separated approaches.
inputs.constraints: 0..26 characters

inputs.name: showDistinctTraits
inputs.description: Retain the distinguishing trait beneath each approach throughout the resolved hold.
inputs.constraints: boolean

inputs.name: foundationReveal
inputs.description: Join two matching foundation fragments or uncover one already continuous foundation.
inputs.constraints: One of join or uncover; both represent one shared principle, not a measured union

bindingExample.shortSourceText: Written and drawn directions take different forms but share the purpose of making the fictional route understandable.

distinction: Unlike source-merge, the two approaches never collapse into a single output. Unlike a comparison panel, the hero action uncovers and connects one common base while preserving the two distinct identities.
limits: Exactly two approaches and one shared principle are supported.
The base width does not measure the amount of agreement or similarity.
The commonality must be explicitly authored and should not imply identical capabilities or interchangeable outcomes.
verificationFocus: Distinct approach traits remain separate above one shared foundation; changing the shared principle changes the base without collapsing the approaches.

title: Work Keeps Its Place
description: A local notebook continues accepting entries while its connection indicator goes quiet. Every new entry leaves a retained impression in the device's storage drawer.
creativeDirection: Within the six-second envelope, reveal a notebook held inside a device outline. At the first entry, the small connection arc gently collapses and the supplied offline caption appears; the writing strokes continue at the same cadence. Each entry presses a matching impression into a shallow local drawer directly beneath the page. Hold on the completed page and its retained impressions with the connection still unavailable, then fade both to the opaque ground without depicting data loss.
goodFor: Explain writing notes during a connectivity interruption
Introduce local-first capture before a verified product demonstration
Illustrate a field notebook or rehearsal log that remains useful away from a shared office
Explain a bounded local collection task in an intermittent-connectivity setting
Explain keeping the original document beside extracted data
Show local-only document storage
intent: Show that losing a connection does not have to interrupt the work already supported on a device.

inputs.name: entries
inputs.description: Entries written after disconnection, in array order. Each entry creates exactly one local impression.
inputs.constraints: 1..4 entries; unique IDs <= 20 characters; labels <= 22 characters; values <= 28 characters

inputs.name: surfaceLabel
inputs.description: Name of the working surface inside the device.
inputs.constraints: 1..32 characters

inputs.name: copy
inputs.description: All connection, storage, final-state, and example captions.
inputs.constraints: Each string 1..32 characters

inputs.name: deviceShape
inputs.description: Choose a device casing or a literal paper notebook metaphor without changing the persistence action.
inputs.constraints: One of tablet, laptop, notebook

inputs.name: showStorageImpressions
inputs.description: Expose the matched local impressions beneath the page; the retained-state caption remains available when hidden.
inputs.constraints: boolean

inputs.name: showLabels
inputs.description: Show supplied entry text and captions. Hidden labels do not remove the entry strokes or storage impressions.
inputs.constraints: boolean

bindingExample.shortSourceText: In our fictional field-notes example, staff keep recording observations when reception disappears, and each entry remains on the tablet.

distinction: Unlike status-cycle, the useful operation visibly continues after a dependency disappears. The page-to-drawer impressions depict local retention without a connection graph, packet stream, or new row of cards.
limits: The number of impressions equals entries.length and is an authored example count, not storage capacity or throughput.
This scene does not imply that every product action works offline, that data is encrypted, or that remote synchronization has occurred.
No duration on screen represents actual outage duration or save latency. Notebook casing is a metaphor and should not be described as proof of digital persistence.
Show only the illustrated local operation. Do not imply that authentication, sharing, remote queries, or every product capability continues without a connection.
A stored impression does not establish backup, encryption, eviction resistance, unlimited storage, synchronization, or zero device energy and maintenance cost.
A derived table cannot reconstruct the original PDF page. Local retention is distinct from remote backup.
verificationFocus: Every supplied entry gets a local impression after connectivity disappears; entries continue at the same cadence and remain present during the offline hold. Source-derived variant: Show one retained impression per supplied entry; use separate entries for source document and extracted table without depicting either as reconstructing the other.

sourceRefs.rationale: The history places data work in a poorly connected emergency setting.
The proposed architecture combines on-device computation with local storage for low-resource settings.
PDF extraction is lossy; original documents may need retention separately from extracted tables.

title: Receipts Close the Journal
description: A retained journal folds open when a connection returns. Matching acknowledgments settle onto its entries while any unacknowledged entries keep their pending tabs.
creativeDirection: Reveal a compact accordion journal with one folded tab per pending entry. As the connection caption changes, unfold the journal just enough to expose each identifier. Authored receipt halves emerge from a separate acknowledgment pocket and register precisely against matching journal tabs; the paired tabs flatten into the page, leaving unpaired tabs raised. Hold on the visibly retained journal with only the supplied receipts closed, then fade to the shared opaque ground.
goodFor: Explain why a locally saved action can still await confirmation
Show reconnection clearing only acknowledged offline changes
Illustrate a dispatch log, expense envelope, or hand-carried register with signed receipts
intent: Explain that confirmation closes a pending entry while missing confirmation leaves it visibly unresolved.

inputs.name: entries
inputs.description: Pending entries retained in the journal, each with one tab and an identifier used for matching.
inputs.constraints: 1..5 entries; unique IDs 1..12 characters; labels 1..24 characters

inputs.name: receipts
inputs.description: The acknowledgments that arrive, in array order. Only the referenced entry's tab closes.
inputs.constraints: 0..entries.length receipts; unique entryId values; every entryId must exist in entries; receipt labels 1..20 characters

inputs.name: copy
inputs.description: Titles and all visible connection and entry-state wording.
inputs.constraints: Each string 1..32 characters

inputs.name: foldDirection
inputs.description: Choose the accordion opening direction while keeping exact receipt-to-entry alignment.
inputs.constraints: One of horizontal, vertical

inputs.name: showIdentifiers

inputs.constraints: boolean

inputs.name: showLabels

inputs.constraints: boolean

bindingExample.shortSourceText: In the fictional notebook, reconnection brings receipts for notes A and B; note C stays in the local pending journal until its receipt arrives.

distinction: Packet-stream depicts movement; this depicts identity-matched acknowledgments changing the physical condition of a retained journal. Source-merge combines sources, whereas the original entries remain in place and a matching receipt closes each obligation.
limits: One supplied receipt closes exactly one entry. A missing receipt means acknowledgment is absent from this illustration, not that remote processing failed.
No retransmission, conflict resolution, deduplication guarantee, or exactly-once delivery claim is implied.
The final state may intentionally contain pending entries. The loop reset is editorial, not a depiction of receipts being revoked.
verificationFocus: Only entries with matching receipt IDs flatten their pending tabs; a missing acknowledgement leaves its tab raised without deleting the entry.

title: A Model Inside the Device
description: A small model cartridge seats inside a device and transforms supplied input into an authored response without crossing the device outline. The casing remains the explicit boundary of the illustrated computation.
creativeDirection: Open on a fixed device cutaway with an empty cartridge socket. Seat a compact labeled model cartridge in the socket, then let a narrow fold of input text enter the device's internal writing area. A single restrained ripple crosses the cartridge face and the supplied response unfurls beneath the input, entirely inside the casing. Hold the device, model, and result together with a supplied boundary caption; fade out through the six-second opaque envelope.
goodFor: Introduce an on-device language-model task
Explain a portable assistant that uses an installed model
Illustrate computation taking place within a defined local boundary
Explain a locally installed SQL assistant
Show inference inside the device boundary
intent: Make the location of the illustrated computation clear without claiming model quality or speed.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: Model cartridge name and optional human-readable detail, such as an authored model version.
inputs.constraints: label 1..28 characters; detail 0..28 characters; no inferred parameter count or memory claim

inputs.name: input

default.label: Example instruction
default.text: Shorten: Meet at the blue shed at noon.

inputs.description: The complete supplied input shown within the device.
inputs.constraints: label 1..24 characters; text 1..96 characters

inputs.name: response
inputs.description: Literal response content supplied by the author, never generated or evaluated by the animation.
inputs.constraints: label 1..32 characters; 1..3 lines; each line 1..44 characters

inputs.name: copy
inputs.description: All device, boundary, and example captions.
inputs.constraints: Each string 1..34 characters

inputs.name: deviceShape
inputs.description: Choose the outer silhouette while retaining the same internal computation choreography.
inputs.constraints: One of phone, tablet, laptop; phone uses stacked text areas

inputs.name: showCutaway

inputs.constraints: boolean

inputs.name: showLabels

inputs.constraints: boolean

bindingExample.shortSourceText: This fictional tablet carries an installed small language model and performs the illustrated rewriting task within the device.

input.label: Example instruction
input.text: Shorten: Meet at the blue shed at noon.

distinction: The hero action seats a persistent computational object inside a bounded device and produces a response there. It is not terminal typing or a general processing pipeline, and it does not draw a local-versus-cloud comparison.
limits: The response is authored illustrative copy, not model output or evidence of correctness, safety, or measured accuracy.
Cartridge size is metaphorical and must not stand in for actual weights, memory usage, energy use, or latency.
Keeping the illustrated task inside the outline does not establish system-wide privacy, absence of telemetry, or offline support for unrelated operations.
Model installation may need a prior network download and sufficient device resources. Local inference for this task does not establish parity with every online tool.
verificationFocus: Input, model cartridge and response stay inside the device boundary for all frames; custom response text appears with no outbound processing route. Source-derived variant: All inference remains within device after cartridge installation; use an authored query as response and label it illustrative, not executed model output.

sourceRefs.rationale: Offline WebLLM uses a local context window and compact aliases.

title: Only the Chosen Fields Leave
description: A local document stays intact behind a boundary while copies of explicitly selected fields pass through a narrow opening. Retained fields remain visible on the original sheet.
creativeDirection: Reveal one local document behind a tall boundary panel and an empty disclosure envelope outside it. Each authored share field briefly lifts as a duplicate while the original stays printed; a precisely sized aperture opens only opposite that field and lets its duplicate pass into the envelope. Retained fields never lift or leave. Close the aperture and hold the complete original beside the selected disclosure contents, then return to the opaque loop ground.
goodFor: Explain an explicit data-minimization policy
Show which local facts are included in an authored remote request
Illustrate sharing an excerpt from a notebook or a limited handoff brief
Explain which authored summary fields a team chooses to publish
Show a minimal remote planning request while private details remain local
Explain a user-selected AI excerpt
Show exactly what an optional remote assist receives
Explain data existence metadata versus file contents
Illustrate opt-in bulk-data synchronization
intent: Show that a handoff can carry a declared subset while the source remains local and complete.

inputs.name: fields
inputs.description: Document fields and the exact authored disclosure choice for each. Every shared field produces one copy outside the boundary.
inputs.constraints: 1..5 fields; unique IDs <= 16 characters; labels <= 22 characters; values <= 28 characters; disclosure is retain or share

inputs.name: copy
inputs.description: All document, boundary, destination, policy, and example labels.
inputs.constraints: Each string 1..32 characters

inputs.name: direction
inputs.description: Set the direction in which permitted copies cross the boundary.
inputs.constraints: One of left-to-right, right-to-left

inputs.name: showPolicyMarks
inputs.description: Show a distinct retained or shared shape next to each field; meaning is also available through supplied captions.
inputs.constraints: boolean

inputs.name: showValues
inputs.description: Display supplied field values or hide them while retaining labels and structural marks.
inputs.constraints: boolean

inputs.name: showLabels
inputs.description: Show all supplied labels and captions; false also hides field values.
inputs.constraints: boolean

bindingExample.shortSourceText: Our fictional handoff shares the topic and tag while the full observation stays in the local notebook.

distinction: Unlike schema-mapping, the purpose is to enforce an explicit disclosure subset rather than correspond fields between schemas. The opening and retained originals carry the meaning, rather than connectors or a funnel.
limits: Shared quantity is the number of fields marked share. Retained quantity is the number marked retain. Neither is a percentage of an unshown larger dataset.
All-retain and all-share inputs are valid but communicate no disclosure and complete disclosure respectively.
The animation does not perform redaction, access control, privacy review, or secure transport. It shows only an authored policy for the depicted fields.
A published summary field must already be approved and supplied. This preset neither computes safe aggregation nor proves anonymity, privacy, consent, or correct access control.
Public visibility of selected fields does not grant access to the underlying records or establish a customer-acquisition result.
Do not claim that clean detector output means the content is safe or anonymous.
All-retain represents declining the transfer; selected fields may include sensitive values.
Keeping file bytes local does not mean the remote system knows nothing about the dataset.
verificationFocus: Only fields marked for sharing have copies outside the boundary; retained fields never appear in the disclosure envelope and the complete original stays inside. Source-derived variant: Preserve all-retain as a valid configuration with zero outbound copies. Retained source fields remain visible; a shared excerpt must not be labeled schema-only if it contains raw values. Source-derived variant: Bind metadata fields to share and raw-content fields to retain; source remains intact and labels distinguish the two classes.

sourceRefs.rationale: The plan identifies privacy-preserving AI exploration as an intended differentiation.

sourceRefs.locator: pages 12 and 15, Public content and product-driven growth
sourceRefs.rationale: The strategy describes publishing dashboards as outward-facing artifacts while teams continue their internal work.
Concrete values and text cross through a separately supported gate.
Dataset metadata sync and opt-in file bytes are distinct boundaries.

title: The Contents Stay Covered
description: An open brief folds into an opaque envelope, moves to its named recipient, and opens only at the authored reveal point. The address remains visible while the contents are covered.
creativeDirection: Begin with a short open brief resting over an unfolded envelope. Fold the lower and side flaps over the brief, then lower the final flap so the contents are fully occluded rather than faded. Move the closed envelope along one shallow hand-carried arc to a recipient tray. If the configured reveal rule is recipient, peel the flap open only after the envelope settles; otherwise hold it sealed. Resolve on the authored final state before the seam-safe fade.
goodFor: Distinguish visible routing information from covered contents
Explain a confidential briefing metaphor
Introduce a restricted handoff before separately documenting the actual security mechanism
intent: Show that routing a package and revealing its contents are separate actions.

inputs.name: brief
inputs.description: The literal brief lines visible before closure and after any permitted recipient reveal.
inputs.constraints: 1..4 lines; unique IDs <= 16 characters; line 1..36 characters

inputs.name: address
inputs.description: Routing information intentionally visible on the exterior of the sealed envelope.
inputs.constraints: Each string 1..28 characters

inputs.name: copy
inputs.description: All state and example captions.
inputs.constraints: Each string 1..34 characters

inputs.name: revealRule
inputs.description: Author whether the recipient opens the envelope or whether the loop ends with it sealed.
inputs.constraints: One of recipient, remain-sealed; no intermediate reveal during travel

inputs.name: showExteriorReference
inputs.description: Show the supplied reference on the exterior while sender and recipient remain available.
inputs.constraints: boolean

inputs.name: showLabels
inputs.description: Show the supplied address, brief text, and captions.
inputs.constraints: boolean

bindingExample.shortSourceText: The fictional coordinator receives an addressed brief whose contents stay covered throughout the handoff and become visible only when the coordinator opens it.

distinction: This is a fold, opaque enclosure, and recipient-controlled reveal, unlike packet-stream's visible abstract packets. It covers the complete payload rather than the field subset selection in disclosure-aperture.
limits: A sealed-envelope metaphor is not proof of encryption, identity verification, authorization, secure deletion, or protection from any particular adversary.
Exterior address and reference are deliberately visible. Do not describe the depiction as hiding all metadata.
The brief contains exactly the supplied lines and does not represent a measured payload size.
verificationFocus: The brief is readable before closure in both modes and fully occluded throughout envelope transit. Recipient mode reopens only after arrival; remain-sealed never re-exposes the contents after closure.

title: Release After Acceptance
description: A work object remains supported by its current holder until the next holder visibly accepts it. Acknowledgment changes responsibility before the first support withdraws.
creativeDirection: Reveal one labeled object held by the sender's bracket. The receiving bracket approaches from the opposite side and makes contact while the sender still supports the object. In the accepted outcome, the recipient's acknowledgment seal lands, the responsibility marker crosses the shared contact zone, and only then does the sender withdraw. In the waiting outcome, retain sender support and hold at the contact zone without an ownership change. Finish on an unambiguous owner state within the six-second envelope.
goodFor: Explain a support shift handoff that requires acceptance
Illustrate transfer of a physical sample, key, or production brief
Show why sending work is distinct from another person taking responsibility
Explain an explicit maintenance-responsibility handoff before a project specialist leaves
intent: Show that responsibility transfers only after the receiving party accepts the handoff.

inputs.name: holders
inputs.description: Names on the two support brackets.
inputs.constraints: Each string 1..28 characters; sender and recipient must differ

inputs.name: object
inputs.description: The single transferred object and its visible content lines.
inputs.constraints: label 1..28 characters; 0..3 details; each detail 1..28 characters

inputs.name: outcome
inputs.description: Choose whether acknowledgment occurs. Without acceptance, the sender keeps responsibility and does not release.
inputs.constraints: One of accepted, awaiting-acceptance

inputs.name: copy
inputs.description: All visible action, acknowledgment, and responsibility captions.
inputs.constraints: Each string 1..30 characters

inputs.name: objectShape
inputs.description: Choose a brief, relay, or key metaphor. Details remain on a fixed adjoining label area for narrow objects.
inputs.constraints: One of folio, baton, key

inputs.name: showResponsibilityMarker
inputs.description: Show the single marker indicating responsibility; support geometry still shows retention or release when hidden.
inputs.constraints: boolean

inputs.name: showLabels
inputs.description: Show supplied holder names, object details, and captions.
inputs.constraints: boolean

bindingExample.shortSourceText: In this fictional shift handoff, the morning team retains the brief until the evening team accepts responsibility.

distinction: The key action is overlapping physical support with delayed release, not a task passing through pipeline stages. Unlike journal-receipts, there is one responsibility marker and custody changes only after acceptance.
limits: Exactly one object and two holders are depicted. Temporary double support does not mean duplicate ownership.
Acceptance is authored data, not a verified signature, legal transfer, or live confirmation.
This scene does not prescribe a legal chain-of-custody process or imply real-world compliance.

Acceptance of responsibility does not prove that documentation, skills, access, funding, or a maintainable codebase are sufficient. A continuity story may need separate evidence for those prerequisites.
verificationFocus: The sender support remains until acknowledgement; a waiting outcome never moves the responsibility marker to the recipient.

sourceRefs.rationale: The plan identifies continuity failures when a short-term contractor or volunteer leaves a custom tool.

title: Wait for every required branch
description: Independent work ribbons reach a shared readiness latch. Completed branches release their own pins, but the common result can pass only after every required branch is ready.
creativeDirection: Reveal two to five work ribbons ending at a shared latch. Their progress advances with authored relative work units during frames 24..112; ready participants withdraw their pins as they finish, while unready participants retain theirs. At frame 122, the latch opens only if every pin is withdrawn, releasing the labeled result by frame 146. Otherwise hold the blocked gate and identify the waiting branch. Preserve completed ribbons during the final reading hold, then fade to the common ground.
goodFor: Explain an all-participants readiness condition
Illustrate coordinated publication or a stage crew's agreed cue
Show why one unresolved prerequisite keeps a shared action on hold
Explaining an all-of dependency before publication
Showing independent checks that must all finish
Introducing parallel work followed by one coordinated handoff
Explain full versus partial offline readiness
Show one missing dependency keeping an action unavailable
intent: Explain a shared action that waits for every named participant's readiness.

inputs.name: participants
inputs.description: One readiness pin per participant. Authored relative workUnits determine when ready pins withdraw during frames 24..112; equal work may finish together. Array order determines stable spatial ribbon order only. The latch opens at frame 122 if and only if every pin has withdrawn, releasing the result by frame 146.
inputs.constraints: 2..5 participants; unique IDs <= 16 characters; labels 1..24 characters; ready boolean; integer workUnits 1..5. A false ready value retains its pin regardless of elapsed editorial time.

inputs.name: sharedAction
inputs.description: The common action revealed beyond the opening when the latch can release.
inputs.constraints: 1..32 characters

inputs.name: copy
inputs.description: All readiness, final-state, and example captions.
inputs.constraints: Each string 1..30 characters

inputs.name: orientation
inputs.description: Choose the latch orientation while keeping each participant attached to their own pin.
inputs.constraints: One of horizontal, vertical

inputs.name: showParticipantStates
inputs.description: Show the supplied ready or waiting caption beside each pin in addition to its physical position.
inputs.constraints: boolean

inputs.name: showLabels
inputs.description: Show participant names, action text, and state captions.
inputs.constraints: boolean

inputs.name: showWorkValues
inputs.description: Displays each branch's supplied work quantity alongside its label.
inputs.constraints: boolean

inputs.name: unitLabel
inputs.description: Provides the unit for the supplied relative work quantities.
inputs.constraints: 1..16 characters

bindingExample.shortSourceText: In the fictional theater cue, the curtain waits until lights, sound, and stage have each marked themselves ready.

distinction: Combines a parallel-completion barrier and a readiness gate. Unlike status-cycle, the action depends on all independent branch states and may remain blocked; an early completion cannot release it.
limits: The condition is all supplied participants, not a majority, weighted vote, or consensus algorithm.
Readiness and ordering are authored. The small latch test and reveal are illustrative timing, not measured coordination latency.
A blocked final state is valid. Waiting must not be styled as a participant's fault or as proof of a failure outside the example.
The default branches and work quantities are fictional.
Work units establish relative authored timing only; the six-second playback is not a duration forecast.
Every branch is required. An unready branch remains incomplete and keeps the latch closed. Quorum and optional checks require another scene.
A cached dependency list does not establish that every other product capability works offline.
verificationFocus: One unready participant keeps the latch closed after faster branches finish; with all ready, the result crosses only after the slowest work ribbon reaches the gate. Source-derived variant: Bind participants to dataset dependencies; one incomplete required participant keeps the common result latched even when all others are ready.

sourceRefs.rationale: Offline readiness compares the dashboard dependencies to locally cached datasets.

title: Distinct Work, Shared Fabric
description: Named contributions become a woven surface while keeping their own visible thread patterns. Their interdependence is shown by alternating over-and-under crossings rather than convergence into a hub.
creativeDirection: Reveal a small loom frame with two or three vertical bands and the same bounded set of horizontal shuttles. Tension the vertical contributions first; sweep each horizontal shuttle once through an alternating over-under mask so the crossing pattern visibly locks together. Keep a short labeled end of every contributor's band outside the frame. Hold the finished fabric with all identities still traceable, then fade the complete textile within the six-second envelope.
goodFor: Explain complementary work becoming one shared deliverable
Illustrate an editorial, design, or workshop collaboration
Show contributions staying attributable inside a collective result
Explain sector-wide co-creation without erasing contributor identity
Show partnership without a central savior
intent: Show that a shared result depends on distinct contributions that remain identifiable.

inputs.name: warp
inputs.description: Vertical contributions fixed to the loom. Each item owns exactly one band and one visible labeled end.
inputs.constraints: 2..3 items; unique IDs across warp and weft <= 16 characters; labels 1..24 characters; pattern is solid, stripe, or dot

inputs.name: weft
inputs.description: Horizontal contributions woven in array order. Each item owns one shuttle pass and one final band.
inputs.constraints: 2..3 items; unique IDs across warp and weft <= 16 characters; labels 1..24 characters; pattern is solid, stripe, or dot

inputs.name: copy
inputs.description: The collective result label and example annotation.
inputs.constraints: Each string 1..34 characters

inputs.name: weaveStart
inputs.description: Choose the first crossing pattern; subsequent crossings alternate consistently without changing contributor roles.
inputs.constraints: One of over-first, under-first

inputs.name: showContributorEnds
inputs.description: Retain the outer band ends so a viewer can trace each contribution into the fabric.
inputs.constraints: boolean

inputs.name: showLabels
inputs.description: Show all contribution names, result text, and the example annotation.
inputs.constraints: boolean

bindingExample.shortSourceText: The fictional field guide brings structure, facts, wording, and layout together, while each team's contribution remains identifiable in the shared result.

distinction: Source-merge collapses inputs toward a destination. This creates alternating physical interlocks, preserves every contribution through the finished structure, and uses neither nodes nor connecting paths.
limits: Band count is the exact number of supplied contributions. Equal band width is decorative and does not represent equal effort, value, ownership, or impact.
Over-under order is a weave construction, not a ranking of contributors or a chronology of all real work.
The scene is not a dependency graph or proof of conflict-free collaborative editing. Suppressing contributor ends reduces attribution clarity.
The weave is a relationship metaphor. Thread widths and crossings do not quantify labor, ownership, compensation or social impact.
verificationFocus: Every warp and weft contributor retains one identifiable end and crossings alternate correctly; changing weaveStart changes over-under order without losing contributors.

sourceRefs.rationale: The source values shared creation and participation while treating contributors as distinct people.

title: Borrowed Permission Returns
description: A single permission token temporarily occupies one participant's socket while its authored lifetime runs down. When the lease ends, the token returns to neutral custody before another participant can hold it.
creativeDirection: Reveal a neutral permission dock and a short arc of participant sockets. Seat the one token in the chosen holder's socket while all other sockets remain empty. A finite segmented collar around that socket drains in evenly spaced editorial beats; when it empties, the socket opens and the token retracts to the neutral dock. Hold the unassigned token and the prior holder's empty socket, making expiration different from a direct handoff, then fade to the opaque ground.
goodFor: Explain a temporary edit lease
Illustrate a shared resource checked out for a limited period
Show permission returning to a pool after an authored expiry
intent: Explain that temporary permission can end without transferring directly to another holder.

inputs.name: participants
inputs.description: Participant sockets arranged around the neutral dock, each showing whether it holds the single token.
inputs.constraints: 2..4 participants; unique IDs <= 16 characters; labels 1..24 characters

inputs.name: holderId
inputs.description: The participant who holds the token before expiry. No successor is inferred.
inputs.constraints: Must equal one participant id

inputs.name: permissionLabel
inputs.description: The particular permission represented by the single token.
inputs.constraints: 1..30 characters

inputs.name: lifetime
inputs.description: The supplied illustrative lease length. The collar uses one segment per unit and the scene compresses the entire lifetime into its main beat.
inputs.constraints: value integer 1..8; unit 1..20 characters; explicitly author the unit, never infer seconds from playback

inputs.name: copy
inputs.description: All neutral-dock, possession, expiry, and example captions.
inputs.constraints: Each string 1..32 characters

inputs.name: showLifetime
inputs.description: Show the collar and supplied lifetime. When hidden, the authored expiry still returns the token but makes no quantity visible.
inputs.constraints: boolean

inputs.name: showLabels
inputs.description: Show participant, permission, lifetime, and state text.
inputs.constraints: boolean

bindingExample.shortSourceText: In the fictional shared editor, editor A borrows an editing lease for four example turns, then the permission returns to the pool instead of passing automatically to editor B.

distinction: Custody-transfer moves responsibility after acceptance. This permission expires and returns to neutral custody with no successor, while a physically exclusive token makes its temporary nature visible. It is not an orbital ecosystem or a generic status cycle.
limits: There is always exactly one permission token. Socket count comes only from participants, and collar segment count comes only from lifetime.value.
The six-second loop compresses the supplied lifetime and must not be interpreted as actual elapsed time or server-clock behavior.
This illustrates an authored lease concept, not a verified distributed lock, fairness guarantee, race-condition solution, or automatic permission policy.
verificationFocus: Exactly one holder owns the token initially, no holder owns it after expiry, and the returned token is retained at the neutral dock.

title: Assemble a dashboard
description: Loose information panels reshape and dock into a deliberately composed dashboard. The motion explains how a chosen layout gives several views a shared reading order.
creativeDirection: Frames 12-40 establish supplied widgets as differently sized panels and an empty dashboard outline. During frames 40-64, the featured panel docks while supporting panels resize and stage clear of it. During frames 64-112, supporting panels dock in staggered order with fixed-size text; frame 88 witnesses this final-docking stage. Grid guides extend from the featured edges, a shared scope strip settles across the board, guides withdraw, and the completed composition holds through frame 166 before the opaque exit.
goodFor: Introduce building a dashboard from reusable views
Explain a featured insight with supporting context
Bridge separate analyses into a shared overview
Explain saving an analysis view into a dashboard
Show a map or chart joining a composed report
intent: Show that arranging information changes how easily its parts can be read together.

inputs.constraints: 1..48 characters

inputs.name: widgets

inputs.constraints: 2..4 widgets; unique IDs <= 20 characters; titles <= 28 characters; 1..3 lines per widget, each <= 38 characters; value kind requires exactly one line

inputs.description: Widget occupying the large slot.
inputs.constraints: Must reference exactly one widget ID

bindingExample.shortSourceText: In this fictional workspace, place the stock figure beside supply details to create one dashboard.

distinction: Unlike stagger-cards, the hero action is constrained layout assembly: unequal panels change geometry, establish alignment, and acquire a shared context. The content is already visible before docking.
limits: All default content is fictional.
Panel size expresses authored editorial priority, never numeric magnitude.
Value strings are supplied labels rather than counters or calculated metrics.
This is a conceptual board builder, not a recording of a supported product feature.
Layout assembly does not imply that queries, source data or permissions have been independently verified.

Source-derived variant: Preserve all supplied widget identities while docking; shared layout does not silently merge their data or denominators.

sourceRefs.rationale: Reusable visualizations and an Explorer result can become dashboard blocks.

title: Bind a shareable report

One section equals one page; this is an authored diagram, not a text-layout engine.
Arrival at the destination tray means prepared for handoff, not transmitted or read.
No actual PDF generation, network sharing, or product capability is demonstrated.
An exported map needs its units, classification legend, source and limitation note; a decorative map image alone is incomplete.

title: Clean values in place

bindingExample.shortSourceText: In the fictional location list, trim the leading spaces in Bay A and standardize the capitalization of Bay B.

distinction: Unlike schema-mapping, field identity never changes and no source-to-destination connectors appear. The explanatory action occurs inside characters of the same cells.

Before and after strings are authored examples; the animation performs no inferred cleanup.

Parentheses after a number may be a second measure rather than a negative sign.

title: Refine a chart for reading

A small context heading settles beside the selected mark. Hold the cleaner chart through frame 166 before the standard exit.
goodFor: Explain editorial refinement of an existing visualization
Show how emphasis can guide attention without changing data
Bridge a broad chart to one discussed category
intent: Show that visual emphasis can improve reading while preserving the data.

Emphasis is an editorial selection, not statistical significance or detected importance.

title: Insert a processing step
description: A new operation is fitted into the middle of an existing processing sequence. The sequence physically makes room, reconnects, and presents an authored input/output example.

A small before/after preview opens below the insertion during frames 98-132 and holds with the recomposed strip until the exit envelope.
goodFor: Explain adding a reusable step to an existing workflow
Show composing a transformation without rebuilding the whole sequence
Introduce the effect of a newly inserted operation
intent: Show that a process can be changed by inserting one explicit operation.

bindingExample.shortSourceText: Insert a trim-spaces operation between reading and saving the fictional location rows.

limits: All default operations and values are fictional.
This supports a single middle insertion, not branching, arbitrary execution, or reorder validation.
Preview strings are supplied; the animation does not execute operations.
The final step array owns both order and count.
verificationFocus: The inserted operation occupies the requested gap exactly once; downstream modules shift and the final connectors follow the new ordered sequence.

title: Reveal the source behind a claim
description: A summary statement lifts like a transparent sheet to expose the source excerpts beneath it. One cited passage is aligned with the statement so its origin can be inspected without a network diagram.
creativeDirection: Frames 12-40 hold a summary strip resting over a short stack of source sheets. During frames 40-104, the summary lifts in place and the source sheets fan out with their text kept upright. The selected source rises, its excerpt receives a narrow underline, and a citation tab aligns with the summary edge. Hold the statement and source passage side by side through frame 166, then return to the opaque ground.
goodFor: Explain provenance of a reported statement
Introduce traceable source citations
Show why a summary should retain its supporting excerpt
Show the decision record behind a design choice
Explain page-and-region provenance for extracted figures
Inspect a source excerpt before accepting a report value
intent: Connect a summary to an inspectable source passage.

inputs.name: summary

default.label: Fictional stock note
default.text: The sample register lists labels in Bay C.

inputs.constraints: label 1..32 characters; text 1..82 characters

inputs.name: sources

default.title: Sample review notes
default.excerpt: Use the register for item locations.

inputs.constraints: 2..3 sources; unique IDs <= 18 characters; titles <= 30 characters; locators <= 24 characters; excerpts <= 78 characters
