bindingExample.shortSourceText: The fictional stock note cites Row C of the sample register; reveal that passage behind the summary.

summary.label: Fictional stock note
summary.text: The sample register lists labels in Bay C.

sources.title: Sample review notes
sources.excerpt: Use the register for item locations.

distinction: Unlike node-traversal or network-graph, lineage is conveyed by physical layers, citation alignment, and readable excerpts. Unlike scan-lines, the focal action is exposing an already identified source.
limits: All default documents and statements are fictional.
A citation indicates supplied attribution, not independent verification or factual truth.
One focal source is inspected per cycle; the remaining sheets supply context.
Source locators are literal labels, not live document links or page lookup instructions.
An exposed decision record makes reasoning inspectable. It does not prove that the decision was correct or publicly accepted.
A source locator documents attribution, not proof that extraction or interpretation is correct.
verificationFocus: The focal citation aligns with the selected source's exact excerpt and locator; other sources remain distinguishable and no citation is fabricated. Source-derived variant: A selected source locator can state page and region label; focal excerpt must match the supplied observation and remain visible.

sourceRefs.rationale: The source calls for explaining methods, choices and their reasons.
Review rows link to page regions and carry extraction provenance.

title: Join matching records
description: Two small tables align on equal keys and zip their matched rows together. Unmatched rows remain visibly distinct, making the selected join rule understandable.
creativeDirection: Frames 12-42 establish two tables with key columns facing each other. Between frames 42-108, equal keys align vertically, their key cells meet at a shared seam, and each matched pair closes into one wider row. Rows without a partner move into a context tray for an inner join, or retain a labeled empty partner for a left join. Hold the derived result and any context tray through frame 166, then exit.
goodFor: Explain joining records by an exact shared key
Compare matched and unmatched rows in an inner or left join
Show enrichment of a record with one related attribute
Explain a P-code or administrative-boundary join
Show why unmatched geographic keys remain in diagnostics
intent: Explain which records combine and what happens when a matching key is absent.

inputs.name: leftRows
inputs.description: Primary table rows, preserving their order in the result.
inputs.constraints: 1..4 rows; unique non-empty keys <= 10 characters; values <= 24 characters

inputs.name: rightRows
inputs.description: Lookup table rows matched by exact key equality.
inputs.constraints: 1..4 rows; unique non-empty keys <= 10 characters; values <= 24 characters; at least one shared key with leftRows

inputs.name: joinType
inputs.description: Exact result membership rule.
inputs.constraints: inner retains only matched left rows; left retains every left row

inputs.name: labels
inputs.description: All visible headings and the absent-partner label.
inputs.constraints: title <= 40 characters; all other labels 1..24 characters

inputs.name: showKeys
inputs.description: Keep key labels visible in the resolved result; keys remain visible during matching.
inputs.constraints: boolean

inputs.name: showUnmatchedTray
inputs.description: Retain excluded input rows in a separate labeled context tray.
inputs.constraints: boolean; this affects context only, never result membership

bindingExample.shortSourceText: Join the fictional item list to its locations by Key, keeping item B even though its location is absent.

distinction: Unlike schema-mapping, the relation is between records with equal key values rather than corresponding field names. Unlike source-merge, unmatched rows and the selected join rule determine the result.
limits: All default rows are fictional.
Keys are unique within each table; many-to-many joins and row multiplication are excluded.
Equality is exact and case-sensitive with no inferred normalization.
Result count is derived from the arrays and joinType, never supplied independently.
An empty partner means no matching input row, not proof the real-world value does not exist.
Use exact matching in this preset. If normalization is needed, show it explicitly in a separate cell-normalization scene before the join.
Missing matches are not zero geographic measures.

Exact raw data in leftRows[].key, leftRows[].value, rightRows[].key and rightRows[].value uses fixed 12px LiteralDataText. Whole-grapheme whitespace is presented with amber underlined marks: space ·, tab ⇥, line break ↵, carriage return ␍ and fallback ␣. Authored literal marker glyphs remain unmarked text. Raw input, accessible text, data attributes, equality and bounds are unchanged. This is presentation, not normalization.
verificationFocus: Matched keys join once; inner joins retain unmatched rows in context only, and left joins retain unmatched left rows with explicit empty partners. Source-derived variant: Keep every unmatched left/right row according to the chosen join rule and display the unmatched tray in boundary-join bindings.

sourceRefs.rationale: Boundary joins report unmatched keys and distinguish exact from normalized-name matching.

title: Reconcile conflicting values
description: Alternative values for the same record remain visible while explicit per-field choices build a reconciled result. Unresolved fields stay open instead of receiving an automatic answer.
creativeDirection: Frames 12-42 show one record with parallel source columns. Between frames 42-112, authored choice rails move toward the selected source for each resolved field, lifting that value into the result column. An unresolved field keeps both alternatives separated by a review bracket. Rejected alternatives remain in a quieter side ledger when enabled. Hold resolved and unresolved fields together through frame 166 before exiting.
goodFor: Explain reconciliation of disagreeing record values
Show a deliberate field-by-field choice
Communicate that unresolved conflicts require review
intent: Show that combining records can require explicit decisions rather than silent overwrites.

inputs.name: recordTitle
inputs.description: Record heading shared by all source alternatives.
inputs.constraints: 1..42 characters

inputs.name: sources
inputs.description: Source columns and their labels.
inputs.constraints: Exactly 2 sources; unique IDs <= 18 characters; labels <= 26 characters

inputs.name: fields
inputs.description: Per-field alternatives and explicit selections. A null choice stays unresolved.
inputs.constraints: 2..4 fields; unique IDs <= 18 characters; labels <= 22 characters; candidates contain each source exactly once; values <= 26 characters; chosenSourceId is null or a listed source ID

inputs.name: labels
inputs.description: All result, decision, and retained-alternative labels.
inputs.constraints: Each label 1..28 characters

inputs.name: showRetainedAlternatives
inputs.description: Keep nonchosen source values visible after selections settle.
inputs.constraints: boolean; unresolved alternatives are always shown

inputs.name: decisionStyle
inputs.description: Visual mark connecting a source choice to its result cell.
inputs.constraints: One of the declared values

bindingExample.shortSourceText: For the fictional item, keep the register name but leave the conflicting locations open for review.

distinction: Unlike source-merge and schema-mapping, this centers disagreement and explicit per-field choices. It never turns multiple inputs into an unexplained single answer.
limits: All default values and choices are fictional.
The supplied choice is an editorial decision, not a recommendation, confidence score, or automatic truth finding.
The animation neither edits source records nor discards alternatives.
No timestamp priority or source authority is inferred.

Exact raw data in fields[].candidates[].value uses fixed 12px LiteralDataText. Whole-grapheme whitespace is presented with amber underlined marks: space ·, tab ⇥, line break ↵, carriage return ␍ and fallback ␣. Authored literal marker glyphs remain unmarked text. Raw input, accessible text, data attributes, equality and bounds are unchanged. This is presentation, not normalization.
verificationFocus: Resolved fields use only their selected source value; unresolved fields retain alternatives and do not acquire a fabricated result.

title: Drill into a selected group
description: Nested selection windows isolate a group and then a subgroup while retaining the parent context. The remaining record tiles expand into readable detail without changing membership.
creativeDirection: Frames 12-40 show record slips organized by the first supplied dimension. A window outlines the first selected group, and other groups recede into a parent strip. For a two-element selectionPath, frames 74-118 open second-dimension compartments and isolate the supplied subgroup. For a one-element path, omit that second selection and move the first group directly into the detail region. Retain exactly the supplied selections in the breadcrumb, hold through frame 166, then use the shared opaque exit.
goodFor: Explain hierarchical filtering from overview to detail
Show exactly which records remain after a drilldown
Preserve context while narrowing a question
intent: Show how a specific answer is reached by narrowing an explicit set of records.

inputs.name: records
inputs.description: Individual record slips and their two group memberships.
inputs.constraints: 4..8 records; unique IDs <= 18 characters; labels <= 22 characters; exactly 2 group strings per record, each 1..18 characters; 1..3 distinct groups per dimension

inputs.name: dimensions
inputs.description: Ordered names of the two grouping dimensions.
inputs.constraints: Exactly 2 strings, each 1..22 characters; array positions match each record.groups position

inputs.constraints: 1..2 strings; each <= 18 characters; the full prefix must match at least one record; no inferred fuzzy matching

inputs.name: labels

inputs.constraints: boolean; breadcrumb remains visible in either mode

inputs.name: selectionStyle
inputs.description: Visual form of the narrowing selection boundary.
inputs.constraints: One of the declared values

bindingExample.shortSourceText: From the fictional supply list, drill into North and then Stored to inspect Paper and Folders.

distinction: Unlike dot-matrix, units do not arrive to illustrate a proportion. Existing named records retain identity while hierarchical membership determines which records occupy the detail view.
limits: All default records and group names are fictional.
Every slip denotes one supplied record; visible totals, if shown, must derive from records and exact-prefix matching.
No geographical shape or location precision is implied by area names.
At most two selection levels fit the six-second cycle.
Record text is re-laid out at a fixed font size rather than enlarged with a camera scale.

Exact raw data in records[].groups[] and selectionPath[] uses fixed 12px LiteralDataText. Whole-grapheme whitespace is presented with amber underlined marks: space ·, tab ⇥, line break ↵, carriage return ␍ and fallback ␣. Authored literal marker glyphs remain unmarked text. Raw input, accessible text, data attributes, equality and bounds are unchanged. This is presentation, not normalization.

Where a retained record is supplied, the other slips fold into an offset stack behind it while their ID tabs remain available; an unresolved group stays open. Show a selected record retained with alternatives still inspectable
Distinguish duplicate candidates from confirmed consolidation
intent: Show duplicate review as a visible grouping and selection decision.

inputs.constraints: Each label 1..28 characters

inputs.constraints: One of the declared values; unresolved groups remain open in either mode

inputs.name: showRecordIds
inputs.description: Display supplied record IDs on the slips and retained stack tabs.
inputs.constraints: boolean

bindingExample.shortSourceText: Review the fictional duplicate candidates, retain A1 for the paper group, and leave the ink group undecided.

distinction: Unlike stagger-cards, the content aligns around a shared comparison value and then consolidates through an explicit selection. Unlike field-conflict-choice, this chooses a record identity rather than separate values for individual fields.
limits: All default records and candidate groups are fictional.
Groups are supplied by the author; no duplicate-detection algorithm, similarity score, or match accuracy is implied.
Matching comparison values alone do not establish that records describe the same real entity.
A retainedId demonstrates an authored selection, not actual deletion or merging of data.
Record and group counts come only from the nested arrays.

Exact raw data in groups[].records[].comparisonValue and, when showRecordIds is true, groups[].records[].id uses fixed 12px LiteralDataText. Whole-grapheme whitespace is presented with amber underlined marks: space ·, tab ⇥, line break ↵, carriage return ␍ and fallback ␣. Authored literal marker glyphs remain unmarked text. Raw input, accessible text, data attributes, equality and bounds are unchanged. This is presentation, not normalization.
verificationFocus: Only an explicitly chosen retained record closes its candidate group; unresolved groups remain open and candidate IDs are not silently discarded.

title: Relieve the bottleneck
description: A visible queue builds behind limited service capacity. Additional service slots open and the same waiting items clear through them.
creativeDirection: Frames 0..12 reveal a queue corridor and named service slots. During 12..54, every supplied item arrives and only initially open slots accept work, making the waiting line visible. Keep initial service items occupied until the capacity expansion beat so a backlog remains visible. During 54..90, the additional slots unfold from closed outlines into usable bays. During 90..138, waiting items enter those bays without changing their original order and emerge into a completed tray. Hold the emptied queue and all completed items through frame 168, then fade to the opaque ground by 179. The hero action is the release of accumulated work after capacity changes.
goodFor: Explaining why a backlog forms around limited service capacity
Introducing additional processing slots or staffed counters
Distinguishing waiting work from work being serviced
intent: Show that opening more service capacity allows an existing backlog to move.

inputs.name: items
inputs.description: The exact work items that wait, enter service, and complete.
inputs.constraints: 3..8 items; unique IDs <= 16 characters; labels <= 14 characters; collection order defines service order; item count must exceed the number of initially open slots

inputs.name: serviceSlots
inputs.description: Service bays and which are available before the expansion; all supplied bays are open after it.
inputs.constraints: 2..4 slots; unique IDs <= 16 characters; labels <= 18 characters; at least one initially open and one initially closed

inputs.name: queueLabel
inputs.description: Caption attached to the waiting corridor.
inputs.constraints: 1..24 characters

inputs.name: completionLabel
inputs.description: Caption attached to the completed-item tray.
inputs.constraints: 1..24 characters

inputs.name: capacityChangeLabel
inputs.description: Explains the authored capacity change at the opening beat.
inputs.constraints: 1..36 characters

inputs.name: showItemLabels
inputs.description: Retain item identifiers during their trip through the service bays.
inputs.constraints: boolean

bindingExample.shortSourceText: In a fictional help desk, five requests wait for one desk until a second desk opens and helps clear the queue.

distinction: Unlike packet-stream, movement is initially constrained and the waiting inventory matters. Unlike status-cycle, the central change is service capacity across several work items, not the status of one task.
limits: The default is a fictional five-request example; each token represents exactly one supplied item.
Timing demonstrates the authored sequence, not a measured arrival rate, throughput increase, or staffing forecast.
All work is homogeneous and completes within the scene; priorities, varying task durations, and continuous arrivals are outside this proposal.
verificationFocus: Closed service slots accept no items before opening; queued items enter newly open slots in original order and every completed item remains accounted for. Reject an initial configuration with no waiting items; preserve the backlog until the expansion beat.

title: Wait longer before retrying
description: One operation returns from unsuccessful attempts and waits through successively wider intervals. Its final attempt either completes or stops, according to the supplied outcome.
creativeDirection: Frames 12..36 introduce the operation token and its first attempt marker. The token makes a short out-and-back trip for each retry outcome, then traverses a visibly wider waiting bracket before the next attempt. Bracket widths are proportional to the authored delay values, while the full action is compressed into frames 36..140. At the final marker, the token either docks in a completed socket or rests against a stop cap. Hold the final outcome and the complete chain of attempts through frame 168, then fade to ground. The growing gaps, not repeated flashes, explain the backoff.
goodFor: Explaining increasing waits after temporary failures
Introducing a bounded retry policy
Showing that retries can end without eventual success
intent: Explain that repeated attempts can be deliberately spaced farther apart.

inputs.name: attempts
inputs.description: Defines every attempt, its outcome, and the waiting interval before the next attempt.
inputs.constraints: 3..4 attempts; labels <= 16 characters; nonfinal outcomes must be retry; nonfinal delayAfter integers 1..16 and strictly increasing across nonfinal attempts; final outcome complete or stop with delayAfter 0

inputs.name: operationLabel
inputs.description: Names the operation that is retried without changing its identity.
inputs.constraints: 1..24 characters

inputs.name: outcomeLabels
inputs.description: Supplies the visible labels for attempt outcomes and waiting brackets.
inputs.constraints: All four keys required; each label 1..18 characters

inputs.name: delayUnit
inputs.description: Names the authored delay unit shown beside waiting values.
inputs.constraints: 1..12 characters; all delays use this same unit

inputs.name: showDelayValues
inputs.description: Shows the supplied waits as values in addition to proportional brackets.
inputs.constraints: boolean

inputs.name: showAttemptLabels
inputs.description: Shows the authored attempt labels under their markers.
inputs.constraints: boolean

bindingExample.shortSourceText: In this fictional request sequence, the first retry waits one second, the next waits two seconds, and the third attempt returns the sample.

distinction: Status-cycle advances once through states; this repeatedly returns the same operation to an attempt point and makes increasing wait intervals the main explanatory device. It does not change the operation after feedback.
limits: All default outcomes and waits are fictional; the animation does not recommend a retry policy.
Timeline widths represent supplied relative waits, but playback is editorially compressed and is not a wall clock.
No probability of eventual success, randomized jitter, or independent concurrent requests is implied.
verificationFocus: Waiting brackets are proportional to supplied delays; the last attempt's declared outcome alone determines completion or stop, and no extra attempt appears. Reject fewer than three attempts and equal or decreasing nonfinal delays.

title: Reuse the stored result
description: A first lookup finds an empty cache and retrieves a result from its origin. A repeated lookup with the same key is answered by the stored copy.
creativeDirection: Reveal a requester, a small empty cache shelf, and a distant origin after frame 12. During 24..68, a key token probes the empty shelf, continues along the longer origin route, and returns carrying the supplied result. During 68..92, an identical result impression settles on the shelf while the requester receives its response. During 102..138, the same key token returns, matches the visible shelf key, and receives the stored result along the short local route without activating the origin. Hold both the keyed cache entry and returned response through 168, then exit. The second lookup visibly uses what the first lookup stored.
goodFor: Explaining cold and warm lookups
Introducing keyed result reuse
Showing why a repeated request may avoid repeating upstream work
Explain resident-versus-persistent cache lookup
Illustrate on-demand loading without upfront copying
intent: Show how storing one result changes the path of a repeated lookup.

inputs.name: request
inputs.description: The shared lookup key and operation label used by both requests.
inputs.constraints: key 1..20 characters; label 1..24 characters; both depicted requests use exactly this key

inputs.name: result
inputs.description: The exact result shown at the origin, in storage, and in both responses.
inputs.constraints: label 1..20 characters; value 1..28 characters

inputs.name: systemLabels
inputs.description: Names the three participants in the lookup.
inputs.constraints: All three keys required; each label 1..22 characters

inputs.name: pathLabels
inputs.description: Provides the explanatory captions for the miss, storage, and hit beats.
inputs.constraints: All three keys required; each label 1..26 characters

inputs.name: showStoredValue
inputs.description: Shows the result value within the stored entry, with its key always visible.
inputs.constraints: boolean

inputs.name: showPathLabels
inputs.description: Shows the authored explanatory captions along the two lookup routes.
inputs.constraints: boolean

bindingExample.shortSourceText: A fictional viewer fetches tile 7 once, keeps its result, and answers the second lookup for tile 7 from the stored copy.

distinction: The first trip changes persistent local state and the second trip uses it. Packet-stream and node-traversal show movement through routes without explaining a miss-to-hit transition for one identical key.
limits: The default key, result, and participants are fictional.
Route length communicates fewer depicted steps, not a measured latency improvement or a guaranteed speedup.
The entry remains valid for both requests; expiry, invalidation, eviction, freshness, and privacy guarantees are not represented.
A cache hit does not establish source freshness or current authorization; those require separate checks.
verificationFocus: The first miss activates the origin and stores the result; the repeated matching request uses only the cache route and returns the same result. Source-derived variant: Keep the existing exact-key miss-to-hit contract. When captions describe a resident or persistent tier, label that tier explicitly and never imply a source fetch on the second hit.

sourceRefs.rationale: Two cache tiers precede source acquisition.

title: Restore a saved version
description: A chosen earlier version returns as an aligned impression over the current document. Current content changes while every saved version remains visible on the history rail.

Select the authored earlier revision, lift its impression from the optional local drawer, and align it over the current document without moving historical snapshots. Between frames 78..126 replace changed lines in place and clear their change notches. Hold the restored document and complete history through frame 167, then fade to ground.
goodFor: Explaining restoration from saved revisions
Showing that earlier content remains recoverable
Introducing a non-destructive version-history workflow
Explain restoring a local checkpoint
Show a rehearsal state returning to a known version
Illustrate the distinction between saved content and later unsaved edits
intent: Show that a saved earlier state can become current without erasing the history.

inputs.constraints: Must match a revisions ID other than the final entry; selected content must differ from final content

inputs.name: artifactLabel

inputs.constraints: 1..24 characters

inputs.name: statusLabels
inputs.description: Supplies the labels for the initial state, restored state, and retained history.
inputs.constraints: All three keys required; each label 1..28 characters

inputs.name: showVersionLabels
inputs.description: Displays the supplied labels beneath saved snapshots.
inputs.constraints: boolean

inputs.name: showChangedLines
inputs.description: Briefly marks current line positions whose text differs from the restored snapshot.
inputs.constraints: boolean; line comparisons are positional, not a semantic text diff

inputs.name: showStorageDrawer
inputs.description: Show the local drawer around the stored impression. When false, keep the stored impression in a labeled margin recess.
inputs.constraints: boolean

inputs.name: surface
inputs.description: Use a paper page or writing slate while preserving the same stored-impression restoration action.
inputs.constraints: One of page, slate

bindingExample.shortSourceText: In fictional sample notes, restoring Draft A brings back its open questions while Drafts B and C remain in saved history.

distinction: One restoration preset combines a local checkpoint impression with a selectable history. Unlike status-cycle, content is reverted; unlike a destructive rewind, later saved versions stay on the rail.
limits: The default document and revisions are fictional and use short text impressions rather than a full editor.
The scene shows restored content, not a claim about how a product records a restoration, resolves conflicts, or persists it.
There is one linear revision history and one restoration; branches, merges, and simultaneous edits are excluded.
Only the listed fields are represented. Do not imply restoration of an entire device, database, or application unless supported separately.
Later values are deliberately replaced in the final state. The scene must not imply that unsaved edits are also recovered.
The checkpoint is an authored example, not evidence of an actual backup, tested recovery process, version history, or guaranteed data durability.
verificationFocus: Current contents equal the selected earlier revision after restoration while all later historical snapshots still exist; changed-line marks clear after replacement.

title: Let the buffer absorb a delay
description: A scheduled sequence leaves a visible reserve before a fixed deadline. An interruption shifts later work into that reserve while the deadline stays in place.
creativeDirection: During 12..44, assemble one horizontal schedule from proportionally sized task blocks followed by a hatched reserve segment and a stationary deadline pin. During 44..74, reveal the supplied interruption block immediately after its named task. During 74..118, the remaining task blocks translate together by the interruption's width and the reserve shortens by exactly that width. A contour along the schedule keeps the total endpoint aligned with the unchanged deadline pin. Hold the inserted interruption, shifted tasks, and remaining reserve through 168, then exit to the opaque ground. The viewer sees precisely where the delay was absorbed.
goodFor: Explaining planned slack in a schedule
Showing a bounded delay absorbed before a deadline
Discussing contingency without changing the scope of the planned work
intent: Show how unused schedule capacity can absorb a specific interruption.

inputs.name: tasks
inputs.description: The sequential task blocks, their order, and their shared-unit durations.
inputs.constraints: 2..4 tasks; unique IDs <= 16 characters; labels 1..16 characters; integer durations 1..4

inputs.name: reserveUnits
inputs.description: Initial unused duration between the last task and the deadline.
inputs.constraints: Integer 1..4; deadline position is derived from task durations plus this reserve

inputs.name: interruption
inputs.description: Names the inserted delay, its location in the sequence, and its duration.
inputs.constraints: label 1..18 characters; afterTaskId must identify a nonfinal task; integer duration 1..reserveUnits

inputs.name: scheduleLabels
inputs.description: Names the flexible reserve segment and the fixed endpoint.
inputs.constraints: Both keys required; each label 1..20 characters

inputs.name: unitLabel
inputs.description: Names the common unit for tasks, delay, and reserve.
inputs.constraints: 1..12 characters; all durations share this unit

inputs.name: showValues
inputs.description: Shows authored durations and the derived remaining reserve next to their segments.
inputs.constraints: boolean

inputs.name: resultLabel
inputs.description: States the authored result above the resolved schedule.
inputs.constraints: 1..38 characters

bindingExample.shortSourceText: A fictional delivery plan reserves two slots, so an extra one-slot review pass can shift later work without moving delivery.

distinction: This conserves one schedule's total width while reallocating reserve time. It is neither a chart of changing rankings nor a pipeline whose stages merely activate in order.
limits: The default schedule is fictional; segment widths exactly encode supplied duration units, not evidence of real delivery performance.
The interruption must fit within the supplied reserve; overruns and moving deadlines are intentionally excluded.
Tasks are sequential, indivisible, and unchanged in duration; parallel work and resource calendars are not modeled.
verificationFocus: The interruption reduces reserve by exactly its duration and leaves the deadline fixed; an interruption exceeding reserve fails instead of squeezing task widths.

title: Collect, then release a batch
description: Individual items wait together inside a forming batch boundary. Once every item in the supplied group arrives, the boundary closes and the group crosses the dispatch boundary as one unit.
creativeDirection: After the entrance, item tokens arrive separately at a shallow loading cradle during 18..62. A bracket grows around the supplied group but remains open while any member is missing. At 68, the final item docks, the bracket closes into an envelope, and the supplied release caption appears. During 82..112, the envelope crosses one dispatch line with its member tokens still visible inside. If a second batch is supplied, its shorter arrival and release sequence occupies 94..146 in a second cradle. Hold the released envelopes and their exact contents through 168, then fade to ground. The transformation is many arrivals becoming one handled bundle without combining their contents.
goodFor: Explaining grouped dispatch or scheduled collection
Showing that items wait for a complete supplied batch
Distinguishing item arrival from group release
intent: Show why individual arrivals are held and then handled together.

inputs.name: batches
inputs.description: Defines exact batch membership and the visible label on each envelope.
inputs.constraints: 1..2 batches; 2..3 items per batch; at most 6 items total; IDs globally unique and <= 16 characters; batch labels <= 18 characters; item labels <= 12 characters

inputs.name: intakeLabel
inputs.description: Names the region where individual items arrive.
inputs.constraints: 1..24 characters

inputs.name: boundaryLabel
inputs.description: Labels the boundary crossed by each complete batch.
inputs.constraints: 1..20 characters

inputs.name: destinationLabel
inputs.description: Names the region holding released batches.
inputs.constraints: 1..26 characters

inputs.name: releaseLabel
inputs.description: Names the release condition when all supplied members have arrived.
inputs.constraints: 1..26 characters; must describe completion of the supplied group, not an unmodeled timer or size threshold

inputs.name: showItemLabels
inputs.description: Preserves individual labels inside each moving batch envelope.
inputs.constraints: boolean

bindingExample.shortSourceText: In a fictional collection workflow, items A, B, and C arrive separately and are dispatched together once Bundle A is complete.

distinction: Source-merge converges inputs into a shared destination; this preserves separate items inside a new handling boundary and explains the wait before one dispatch. The batch envelope, not a relabeled row of cards, is the hero transformation.
limits: Default groups and items are fictional; every token is one supplied item and every envelope is one supplied batch.
The authored membership defines completion; no scheduler, elapsed-time rule, transaction guarantee, or automatic grouping algorithm is implied.
No processing-efficiency or cost improvement is quantified by the animation.
verificationFocus: A batch crosses dispatch only after every member arrives; its contents and membership remain unchanged and separate batches never silently combine.

title: Revise through feedback
description: A short draft travels to a reviewer and returns with an attached note. The author changes the draft in response and sends the revised version back for the supplied closing outcome.
creativeDirection: Frames 12..32 establish an author station, a reviewer station, and one readable draft between them. During 32..62, the draft crosses to the reviewer and an authored feedback tab attaches to its edge. During 62..94, it returns with that tab visibly tethered to the draft, and the draft text wipes into the supplied revised wording. During 94..132, the revised draft crosses back along the same route; the feedback tab detaches into a small review trail and the closing outcome settles beside the draft. For two supplied rounds, divide frames 32..144 evenly between their paired return trips. Hold the final draft through 168, then exit. The object changes between trips rather than merely retrying the same operation.
goodFor: Explaining a review-and-revision workflow
Showing how a specific note changes a draft
Introducing short feedback iterations without claiming an objective quality score
Show a community contribution receiving an explicit maintainer response
Connect a participant concern to an authored product or service revision
Show an open design draft revised after an authored community comment
Explain respectful peer feedback with a retained comment trail
intent: Connect a concrete piece of feedback to an authored revision.

inputs.name: artifactLabel
inputs.description: Names the artifact that makes each review trip.
inputs.constraints: 1..24 characters

inputs.name: rounds
inputs.description: Supplies each concrete draft, returned note, and resulting text.
inputs.constraints: 1..2 rounds; labels 1..12 characters; draft and revised 1..26 characters; feedback 1..28 characters; revised must differ from draft; each later draft must exactly match the previous revised value

inputs.name: roleLabels
inputs.description: Names the two participants in the review exchange.
inputs.constraints: Both keys required; each label 1..20 characters

inputs.name: finalLabel
inputs.description: Names the supplied closing outcome of the final review.
inputs.constraints: 1..26 characters; authored outcome, not a computed quality assessment

inputs.name: showReviewTrail
inputs.description: Keeps completed feedback tabs below the final draft during the hold.
inputs.constraints: boolean

inputs.name: showRoundLabels
inputs.description: Displays the supplied pass label beside the active round.
inputs.constraints: boolean

bindingExample.shortSourceText: In a fictional writing review, the note to name the next step changes Share update to Review the draft before the message is ready to share.

distinction: Retry-backoff repeats an unchanged operation; this makes feedback alter the artifact before it returns. Data cleanup transforms records according to a rule, whereas this shows an authored human review exchange with its note retained.
limits: The default exchange and outcome are fictional.
The renderer displays supplied revisions and does not generate, evaluate, or infer improvements.
Short text snippets stand for the artifact; simultaneous reviewers, contradictory notes, approvals with legal effect, and full document editing are outside this scene.

The depicted revision must follow the supplied note and closing outcome. A contribution does not imply automatic upstream acceptance, deployment, broad representativeness, or improved social outcomes.
A submitted comment does not prove consent, adoption, representation of the whole community or that every concern has been resolved. The closing label must reflect the authored outcome.
verificationFocus: Each return trip carries the supplied feedback and replaces draft text with the corresponding revision; the next round starts from that revision.

sourceRefs.locator: pages 15-16, Open source community growth and community participation
sourceRefs.rationale: The strategy treats users and communities as potential contributors rather than passive consumers.
The plan proposes changing the initial product focus in response to user research.

sourceRefs.locator: pages 4, 7 and 10 / co-creation, candor and user learning
sourceRefs.rationale: The source calls for community discussion, kind direct feedback and learning from users after delivery.

title: Break the work into parts
description: A single block representing an undertaking is cut into a bounded set of labeled work packages. Its conserved-area pieces separate into a reserved enclosing bracket while the original thin contour remains a fixed reference to the whole.
creativeDirection: Reveal one continuous filled slab with the parent label during 12..38. A visually distinct enclosing bracket reserves gap space from setup while the original contour remains a fixed thin reference. During 38..86, ruled cut lines travel across the slab in the chosen partition layout, dividing its area according to supplied effort weights. During 86..124, the full-area pieces separate by a small equal gap into the reserved space and their individual labels settle. The parent label remains above the grouping without changing size. Hold the complete labeled partition through 168, then fade to ground. Piece areas are conserved; separated pieces are not required to fit inside the identical original filled outline.
goodFor: Explaining work breakdown before planning
Showing the components of a bounded undertaking
Illustrating relative effort allocation without prescribing task order
intent: Make a large undertaking understandable as an explicit set of constituent parts.

inputs.name: parentLabel
inputs.description: Names the original whole retained by the thin reference contour and the separate reserved grouping bracket.
inputs.constraints: 1..28 characters

inputs.name: workItems
inputs.description: Defines the complete set of pieces and their proportional areas.
inputs.constraints: 3..6 items; unique IDs <= 16 characters; labels 1..18 characters; integer effort 1..5; parent effort is derived as the sum

inputs.name: unitLabel
inputs.description: Names the common unit used by the piece areas and optional values.
inputs.constraints: 1..16 characters; all effort weights use this same unit

inputs.name: groupingLabel
inputs.description: Labels the resolved set of constituent pieces.
inputs.constraints: 1..26 characters

inputs.name: showEffortValues
inputs.description: Displays each supplied effort and the derived parent total.
inputs.constraints: boolean; area remains proportional even when values are hidden

inputs.name: partitionLayout
inputs.description: Chooses parallel cuts or alternating horizontal and vertical cuts through the same whole.
inputs.constraints: strips or alternating-cuts; both preserve area proportional to effort; no ranking or time order is encoded

bindingExample.shortSourceText: A fictional release is broken into drafting, review, and packaging, with three, two, and one illustrative effort units respectively.

distinction: Stagger-cards introduces separate siblings; this starts with one continuous whole and visibly partitions its conserved area. It does not imply a sequential pipeline or relationships among independently existing nodes.
limits: The default undertaking and effort values are fictional.
Piece area represents the supplied relative effort allocation, not task duration, staffing, cost, or measured productivity unless the caller explicitly supplies that meaning and unit.
All pieces together exhaust the depicted whole; overlapping work, unallocated effort, dependencies, and recursive subtasks are excluded.
verificationFocus: Piece areas reflect supplied effort shares and sum to the original slab; changing partition orientation preserves all shares and parent membership.

title: Make room for urgent work
description: A newly prioritized item enters an existing ordered queue. One slot opens ahead of a chosen waiting item while every existing item keeps its relative order.
creativeDirection: During 12..38, lay an existing queue into numbered track slots, with its service end visibly marked. During 38..64, the new item arrives on a small side spur carrying the authored priority caption. During 64..108, the chosen insertion slot opens and all items from that position onward shift exactly one slot away from service as a single movement. During 108..132, the new item travels along the spur into the opening. Hold the changed queue and optional faint original-position markers through 168, then exit to ground. The new item gains precedence without scrambling the order of existing work.
goodFor: Explaining insertion of an urgent task into a waiting queue
Showing the effect of a priority change on already planned work
Introducing stable ordering while reprioritizing one new item
intent: Show exactly which waiting work moves when one new item gains precedence.

inputs.name: queue
inputs.description: The existing queue in service order, which remains stable around the insertion.
inputs.constraints: 3..5 items; unique IDs <= 16 characters; labels 1..16 characters; first item is nearest service

inputs.name: incomingItem
inputs.description: The single new item entering the queue from the side spur.
inputs.constraints: ID <= 16 characters and distinct from every queue ID; label 1..18 characters

inputs.name: insertBeforeId
inputs.description: Identifies the waiting item before which the new item is placed.
inputs.constraints: Must match an ID in queue; resulting queue length is derived from queue plus incomingItem

inputs.name: priorityLabel
inputs.description: Explains the authored reason or ordering instruction beside the incoming item.
inputs.constraints: 1..34 characters; any named destination must agree with insertBeforeId

inputs.name: serviceLabel
inputs.description: Marks the front of the queue so precedence is unambiguous.
inputs.constraints: 1..22 characters

inputs.name: showOriginalPositions
inputs.description: Keeps faint original slot markers behind the shifted items to make displacement legible.
inputs.constraints: boolean; ordinals are derived from the original collection order

bindingExample.shortSourceText: In a fictional draft queue, a time-sensitive request is inserted before Draft B; B, C, and D each move back one place while their order is preserved.

distinction: Bar-race reorders measured rankings; this makes one explicit queue insertion without scores or a wholesale sort. Queue-relief changes service capacity, whereas this changes precedence while service capacity is absent from the argument.
limits: The default tasks and priority are fictional and do not prescribe a prioritization policy.
Only waiting items are reordered; there is no interruption of work already in progress.
Slot positions encode precedence only, not duration, importance scores, fairness, or a delivery commitment.
verificationFocus: The incoming item occupies the supplied insertion point while the relative order of all existing queue items remains unchanged.

title: Show the range behind the estimate
description: A point estimate opens into a bounded interval on one fixed scale. An optional reference remains visible so the interval's relation to that reference can be read without turning uncertainty into certainty.
creativeDirection: At the entrance, a supplied estimate marker stands on a fixed ruler. Two folded sleeves extend from the marker to the supplied lower and upper endpoints, exposing a patterned interval and its explicit meaning. An optional reference blade then lowers across the ruler, with its position preserved even when it crosses the interval. Hold the estimate, both endpoints, interval label and authored interpretation together before fading to the opaque ground. All movement fits six seconds and reveals supplied values rather than simulating evidence or a time trend.
goodFor: Explain why a single planning estimate has a range
Introduce a supplied confidence interval alongside its point estimate
Show that a reference value lies within or outside authored bounds
Label a supplied scenario range separately from statistical uncertainty
Keep an untested operating assumption visible beside a point estimate
intent: Make the limits around an estimate as visible as the estimate itself.

inputs.name: estimate
inputs.description: The estimate and two endpoints revealed by the unfolding sleeves.
inputs.constraints: label 1..32 characters; finite numbers; lower <= point <= upper; lower < upper; all values inside axis bounds

inputs.name: axis
inputs.description: The fixed linear ruler and unit shared by the point, interval and reference.
inputs.constraints: finite min < max; unit 1..16 characters; no automatic rescaling during the animation

inputs.name: interval
inputs.description: Names what the interval represents. Confidence labels must explicitly include the supplied level and method when applicable.
inputs.constraints: one listed kind; label 1..64 characters; kind does not generate endpoints or statistical claims

inputs.name: reference
inputs.description: Optional fixed reference blade used to inspect the interval's position.
inputs.constraints: null or a finite value inside axis bounds; label 1..32 characters

inputs.name: interpretation
inputs.default: The range spans the planning allowance.
inputs.description: The authored closing explanation shown beside the completed interval.
inputs.constraints: 1..80 characters; must agree with the supplied numeric relationship; never inferred from interval overlap

inputs.name: showValues
inputs.description: Shows the point and endpoint numbers without changing their scale positions.
inputs.constraints: boolean; interval label and axis unit remain visible

inputs.name: contextLabel
inputs.description: Visible context or source qualifier for the supplied values.
inputs.constraints: 1..64 characters

bindingExample.shortSourceText: In a fictional workshop plan, preparation is estimated at five hours with an illustrative range of three to eight hours. The six-hour allowance falls inside that range.

inputBindings.interpretation: The range spans the six-hour allowance.

distinction: Unlike line-trace, the scale has no time axis and no observed series is drawn. Unlike chart-focus-edit, this reveals the uncertainty contract hidden by a point alone. Contact-window-overlap compares recorded visits in time; this unfolds one numerical estimate into its explicitly named epistemic bounds.
limits: One estimate and at most one reference. Endpoints are supplied, never statistically calculated or narrowed by the animation.
Interval width represents numeric span on a linear scale, not probability density, likelihood or sample size.
Confidence intervals, measurement ranges and scenario ranges are different meanings. The selected kind and label must match the source.
Crossing or not crossing a reference is not automatically a significance test, recommendation or certainty claim. No automatic success or failure color is applied.

A conservative adjustment or downside scenario is not a confidence interval, a validated error margin, or a representative population estimate. Match interval.kind and its visible label to the actual evidence.
No endpoints, probabilities, sample precision, or validation status are inferred from a business plan or the width of the displayed band.
verificationFocus: The interval endpoints and point stay on one fixed scale, the point remains inside the interval, and an optional reference never moves to create a desired conclusion; invalid bounds fail.

sourceRefs.rationale: The plan acknowledges limited survey evidence and applies a conservative adjustment before projecting revenue.
The plan separately acknowledges that operating-cost assumptions still need real-world evaluation.

title: Try a change, then return
description: One source control moves to a trial value while explicitly coupled output scales respond. Returning the source restores every dependent value and leaves the independent example unchanged.
creativeDirection: A source slider and two to four output rulers appear at their baseline positions. Visible mechanical couplings connect only outputs with nonzero multipliers. Over the middle two seconds the source slides to its trial setting and coupled pointers move simultaneously according to their supplied affine rules, with optional hollow baseline markers left behind. After a brief trial hold, the source slides back and every coupled pointer returns to its exact baseline. An uncoupled output stays still throughout. Hold the restored state with its authored caption, then fade to the same opaque ground within six seconds.
goodFor: Explain which quantities change when a planning assumption changes
Demonstrate a reversible what-if calculation
Contrast a linked value with an explicitly independent constant
Rehearse a fictional per-user cost and allowance rule
Expose how one planning assumption changes only declared dependent quantities
intent: Show the precise scope of a reversible change without implying every nearby quantity is affected.

inputs.name: source
inputs.description: The single numeric input moved to its trial value and restored.
inputs.constraints: label 1..28 characters; unit 1..16 characters; finite min < max; distinct baseline and trial inside bounds

inputs.name: outputs
inputs.description: Output values are multiplier times the source plus offset. Zero multiplier is an explicitly independent constant with no coupling.
inputs.constraints: 2..4 outputs; unique IDs 1..20 characters; labels 1..28 characters; units 1..16 characters; all numbers finite; min < max; computed baseline and trial values inside each output's bounds; at least one multiplier nonzero and at least one multiplier exactly zero; no separate output count or supplied output values

inputs.name: phaseLabels
inputs.description: Visible captions identify the initial, trial and restored holds.
inputs.constraints: each label 1..36 characters

inputs.name: showRules
inputs.description: Displays each numeric affine rule alongside its ruler, including the constant rule for an independent output.
inputs.constraints: boolean; rendered rules use supplied numeric coefficients and the source label; no free-form executable expressions

inputs.name: showBaselineMarkers
inputs.description: Retains hollow starting pointers during the trial so change can be inspected.
inputs.constraints: boolean; ghost positions always equal computed baseline values

inputs.name: contextLabel
inputs.description: A visible qualifier or assumption note stays attached to the entire rehearsal.
inputs.constraints: 1..72 characters

bindingExample.shortSourceText: In a fictional workshop, trying four batches instead of two doubles parts from six to twelve and reduces reserve credits from eight to four. One booked room stays fixed. Reverting the assumption restores the starting quantities.

inputBindings.contextLabel: Fictional workshop arithmetic, not a forecast

distinction: Unlike node-traversal or event-bus, no signal tours a graph. Physically coupled pointers move together under explicit equations, then reverse. Revision-restore replaces a saved document; this restores one source assumption and recomputes only its declared numeric dependents. Cell-normalization corrects values once, whereas these values remain linked throughout an intentional trial and return.
limits: Only one source and direct affine dependencies are supported. No arbitrary graphs, cycles, chained expressions or inferred causal links.
Each output uses its own labeled fixed scale. Equal visual travel across rulers does not imply equal numerical change or comparable units.
Pointer positions always use multiplier times the current source plus offset, including intermediate frames. Fractions during movement are interpolation, not discrete operations performed.
Returning the parameter represents reversible arithmetic only. It does not claim that real-world impacts or external side effects can be undone.
Use the existing affine contract only. Tier cliffs, nonlinear growth, churn, caps, payment fees, and compounding require a separately specified model and must not be approximated silently.
A trial value is an authored scenario, not measured demand, market validation, or a prediction of financial performance. Use fictional values and explicit units and periods.
verificationFocus: Every dependent value equals multiplier times the current source plus offset at all sampled frames; zero-multiplier outputs stay fixed and returning to baseline restores exact initial values. Require both a dependent output and an independent output with multiplier zero.

sourceRefs.locator: pages 12-14, Value metrics and Subscription Plans
sourceRefs.rationale: The strategy links plan allowances and charges to explicit usage and team-size metrics.
Financial projections depend on authored assumptions about growth and costs.

title: Track monitored custody
description: The same vaccine carrier or specimen container passes through authored custody stops. Identity, seal state, monitoring records and acknowledgements stay visible and distinct throughout the handoffs.
creativeDirection: Establish one to five labeled containers and their persistent identity ribbons. Between frames 36..115 carry each container through three custody stops; attach a seal marker, monitoring tab and acknowledgement stub at each stop, keeping missing records visibly open. The same identifier stays attached through every handoff. Hold the received containers beside a checkpoint ledger at frames 116..167 before the common exit. A small globe is optional context; the local route is always schematic.
goodFor: Explain why a shipment needs both custody and condition records.
Introduce a fictional vaccine distribution story before showing sourced operational evidence.
Distinguish containers delivered from containers with complete monitoring records.
Introduce specimen traceability without depicting a test result.
Explain a missing custody acknowledgement despite physical receipt.
Distinguish the specimen's identity from its transport packaging.
intent: Show that arriving at the destination does not by itself establish a complete condition record.
distinction: Merges cold-chain monitoring and specimen identity tracking. Unlike the generic custody-transfer gate, this preserves a multi-stop identity/record ledger and may show missing evidence after physical receipt.
limits: One container glyph represents one shipping container, never one dose or one vaccinated person. Container count is crates.length and remains constant throughout all handoffs.
Every crate has exactly one checkpoint per stop. Monitoring categories are authored records, not temperature calculations, clinical clearance, or evidence of potency.
The globe provides general world context only. The route and local map are fictional, have no real coordinates or borders, and must carry the configured schematic caption.
No temperatures, thresholds, vaccine recommendations, handling instructions, or real delivery speed are inferred. All delivery motion is editorial compression.
A receipt acknowledgement proves only the authored administrative event, not specimen suitability, test completion, a result, or diagnostic validity.
Transport and packaging are stylized props. This animation gives no clinical collection, biosafety, shipping, storage, or chain-of-custody compliance instructions.
The example has one linear custody sequence and cannot depict pooled specimens, aliquots, split ownership, or bulk shipment counts.
The legend treats monitoring, custody acknowledgement and seal records as distinct. None establishes temperature compliance, specimen validity or clinical safety without supplied evidence.

inputs.name: stops
inputs.description: Ordered physical custody locations.
inputs.constraints: Exactly 3 ordered stops; unique IDs <= 16 characters; labels <= 24 characters; kind is one declared value. Stops illustrate supplied custody roles, not a required clinical protocol.

inputs.name: crates
inputs.description: Containers, their identities, and authored monitoring record states at each handoff.
inputs.constraints: 1..5 containers; unique IDs <= 16 characters; labels <= 20 characters; exactly one checkpoint per stop in stop order; checkpoint references must exist. Record state, acknowledgement and seal are separate supplied facts.

inputs.name: sceneLabel
inputs.description: Persistent qualifier identifying the invented scene.
inputs.constraints: 1..40 characters; must identify fictional or approved sourced content.

inputs.name: geographyMode
inputs.description: Include a recognizable globe before the schematic local delivery scene.
inputs.constraints: Enum only; no implied geolocation or real route.

inputs.name: showMonitoring
inputs.description: Show the per-container record tabs, with shape and text in addition to color.
inputs.constraints: boolean

inputs.name: showLedger
inputs.description: Show the container total and final-state subtotals derived from crates.
inputs.constraints: boolean

inputs.name: copy
inputs.description: All captions, legend labels, and quantity nouns used by the scene.
inputs.constraints: Exactly the documented default keys; each value 1..42 characters; preserve the defined meaning of each key.

inputs.name: showIdentityRibbon
inputs.description: Keep the same specimen ID visible across all custody locations.
inputs.constraints: boolean

bindingExample.shortSourceText: In this fictional delivery, three vaccine containers arrive at Hill clinic, but only one has a final monitoring record marked logged.

verificationFocus: Container IDs persist through every stop; missing acknowledgements, unknown seals and monitoring-review states remain separately visible after receipt and never become success markers implicitly.

title: Session dose balance
description: An opened supply carrier empties into three visible destinations: documented use, remaining stock, and recorded loss. Every represented dose unit is accounted for at the end.
creativeDirection: Open a carrier containing the supplied discrete dose tokens. Move each token exactly once to the authored used, remaining or recorded-loss destination; only used tokens settle beside recipient silhouettes. Hold every destination simultaneously with a derived conservation equation and a separate people total, then fade to the unchanged ground.
goodFor: Explain a fictional end-of-session stock reconciliation.
Distinguish administered-dose counts from the number of people served.
Show why unused stock and recorded loss need separate categories.
intent: Make every dose unit visible in exactly one final accounting category.
distinction: Unlike metric-counter, dot-matrix, or data-pipeline, the same physical stock units leave a carrier and partition into mutually exclusive destinations, with conservation remaining visible throughout.
limits: units.length is the opening dose-unit denominator. Final administered + remaining + discarded always equals this denominator; no independent total input is allowed.
The people denominator is the number of unique non-null recipientId values among administered units. Multiple units may refer to one recipient, so doses and people are never interchangeable.
This is a bookkeeping metaphor with no injection demonstration, dose size, product, eligibility rule, or disposal procedure.
Loss is an authored accounting outcome. The animation does not determine whether a product should be discarded or reused.

inputs.name: units
inputs.description: Opening units and their mutually exclusive final destinations.
inputs.constraints: 1..12 units; unique IDs <= 16 characters; every administered unit requires a nonempty recipientId <= 16 characters; all other outcomes require recipientId null; at most 6 unique recipients.

inputs.name: recipients
inputs.description: Labels for the people receiving the documented units.
inputs.constraints: 0..6 recipients; unique IDs <= 16 characters; labels <= 18 characters; IDs must equal exactly the set of recipientId values used by units.

inputs.name: sceneLabel
inputs.description: Persistent qualifier identifying the invented scene.
inputs.constraints: 1..40 characters; must identify fictional or approved sourced content.

inputs.name: showPeopleTotal
inputs.description: Display a distinct unique-person subtotal beside the dose ledger.
inputs.constraints: boolean

inputs.name: showEquation
inputs.description: Display the derived opening equals administered plus remaining plus discarded equation.
inputs.constraints: boolean

inputs.name: copy
inputs.description: All captions, legend labels, and quantity nouns used by the scene.
inputs.constraints: Exactly the documented default keys; each value 1..42 characters; preserve the defined meaning of each key.

bindingExample.shortSourceText: A fictional clinic opens with six dose units and records three used, two remaining, and one lost, serving three distinct people.

verificationFocus: Used, remaining and lost dose tokens sum exactly to starting units; people counts remain distinct from doses and no person appears for an unused dose. Reject administered units without a recipient ID and non-administered units with a recipient ID.

title: The same cohort returns
description: Keep the same people visible as a fictional multi-dose cohort returns for successive recorded visits. Missed and unobserved visits leave visible gaps instead of removing people from the denominator.
creativeDirection: Introduce the supplied cohort at the first visit arch. Slide later visit arches across the same identity lanes: a person enters an arch only when that visit is recorded, while missed, not-yet-due and unknown marks remain distinct. Hold the attendance fabric with separate visit numerators over one fixed cohort denominator before the opaque exit.
goodFor: Explain retention across a fictional multi-dose programme.
Show how a missed visit differs from an unknown record or a visit not yet due.
Keep the baseline cohort visible while comparing later attendance.
intent: Show who returned across visits without silently changing the population being compared.
distinction: Unlike dot-matrix or status-cycle, each person retains identity across multiple visit gates, and missing observations stay spatially visible. Unlike missed-visit-reconnect, this compares the entire baseline cohort rather than the work of following up an already missed group.
limits: The fixed baseline denominator is participants.length. Each per-visit recorded numerator counts participant records with that visit marked recorded; no population coverage or protection percentage is inferred.
Missing, missed, and not-yet-due are different supplied states. They are never auto-converted into clinical noncompliance or a recommendation.
Visit order is ordinal only. No elapsed time, vaccine name, interval, dose schedule, eligibility, or catch-up dosing advice is supplied.
Each participant occupies one lane throughout; a returning participant is not a newly added person. Arrays, not independent totals, own all counts.

inputs.name: visits
inputs.description: Ordered fictional follow-up checkpoints.
inputs.constraints: 2..4 visits; unique IDs <= 16 characters; labels <= 18 characters; ordinal labels only in default examples.

inputs.name: participants
inputs.description: Stable cohort identities and the supplied record at each visit.
inputs.constraints: 2..8 participants; IDs <= 16 and labels <= 18 characters; exactly one record for every visit ID; unique IDs and no duplicate visit record.

inputs.name: sceneLabel
inputs.description: Persistent qualifier identifying the invented scene.
inputs.constraints: 1..40 characters; must identify fictional or approved sourced content.

inputs.name: emphasis
inputs.description: Direct attention to all records, a recorded return after a missed visit, or unknown observations.
inputs.constraints: Enum only; visual emphasis does not change denominator or data.

inputs.name: showFractions
inputs.description: Show recorded participants over the fixed baseline total at every visit.
inputs.constraints: boolean

inputs.name: copy
inputs.description: All captions, legend labels, and quantity nouns used by the scene.
inputs.constraints: Exactly the documented default keys; each value 1..42 characters; preserve the defined meaning of each key.

bindingExample.shortSourceText: Six fictional people began a multi-visit programme; a later return must still be counted against the original six, with missed and unknown records shown separately.

verificationFocus: Every visit uses the same cohort denominator; recorded, missed, not-yet-due and unknown states remain distinct and changing one visit never creates a new person.

title: Reconnect after a missed visit
description: A field worker follows up a small, explicitly defined group whose visits were missed. A conversation, a booking, and an attended return resolve into separate outcomes.
creativeDirection: Frames 12..38 show four silhouettes with empty appointment marks beside their homes. Frames 39..114 animate one worker making the authored phone or doorstep contacts; a booking tab folds onto a calendar for one person, while only a documented attendee walks back through the clinic door. Frames 115..167 hold everyone in a distinct final state with the original group total; fade to ground by frame 179.
goodFor: Explain the operational work after missed appointments.
Distinguish successful contact from a booked or completed return.
Show unresolved follow-up honestly in a fictional public health story.
intent: Show that reaching someone, booking a visit, and recording attendance are different achievements.
distinction: Unlike status-cycle or node-traversal, this shows a worker contacting people in their physical setting and an actual return through a clinic doorway only for attended records. Unlike dose-cohort-return-paths, its denominator is a preselected missed-visit group and its action is reconnection.
limits: The denominator is cases.length: the authored missed-visit group, not the whole service population. Each person has one exclusive final state, so state subtotals sum to the group total.
Attempts are contact events and may exceed unique people. A contact or booking does not imply attendance, vaccination, eligibility, or health benefit.
The sequence depicts recorded administrative outcomes and supplies no follow-up timing, clinical priority, or dosing advice.
Identities are fictional. Household and phone graphics must not imply a particular reason for the missed visit.

inputs.name: cases
inputs.description: The fixed missed-visit group, contact method, attempt count, and final administrative outcome.
inputs.constraints: 1..6 cases; unique IDs <= 16 characters; labels <= 18 characters; attempts integer 1..3; enum values only; one outcome per person.

inputs.name: places
inputs.description: Names for the real-world settings and calendar prop.
inputs.constraints: Exactly these keys; each label 1..24 characters.

inputs.name: sceneLabel
inputs.description: Persistent qualifier identifying the invented scene.
inputs.constraints: 1..40 characters; must identify fictional or approved sourced content.

inputs.name: showAttemptCount
inputs.description: Show total contact attempts separately from unique people.
inputs.constraints: boolean

inputs.name: showOutcomeLedger
inputs.description: Show exclusive final-state counts over the original missed-visit group.
inputs.constraints: boolean

inputs.name: copy
inputs.description: All captions, legend labels, and quantity nouns used by the scene.
inputs.constraints: Exactly the documented default keys; each value 1..42 characters; preserve the defined meaning of each key.

bindingExample.shortSourceText: Among four fictional people with missed visits, six contact attempts lead to one recorded return, one booking, one conversation, and one person not reached.

verificationFocus: Contact and booking do not move a person through the clinic door; only the authored attended outcome does, and all original cases retain a final state.

title: Shared place, overlapping time
description: Place-time strips reveal which recorded visits overlap a supplied investigation window. Unknown times remain unresolved, and overlap never becomes an inferred transmission link.
creativeDirection: Reveal the shared place above the supplied person-specific time ribbons. Position the authored intervals on one axis and lower the investigation-window stencil over them; outline only actual interval intersections. Hold overlapping, nonoverlapping and unknown records alongside the same people, then fade. The intersection represents a review candidate, not a confirmed transmission.
goodFor: Explain how an investigation filters recorded presence by time and place.
Distinguish temporal overlap from proof of exposure or transmission.
Show why missing visit times remain unresolved.
intent: Explain the difference between sharing a place and being recorded there during the same defined window.
distinction: Unlike network-graph, node-traversal, or line-trace, the hero action is a window stencil intersecting interval lengths attached to people and a physical venue. No traveling signal implies transmission.
limits: The denominator is records.length, one record per distinct person in this bounded example. Overlap + no overlap + unknown equals that denominator; counts are derived from interval intersection.
Intervals and the supplied investigation window use half-open bounds [start,end), so touching endpoints alone do not count as overlap. Unknown means both bounds are null.
Any overlap is only recorded co-presence under the supplied window. It is not a case definition, exposure determination, disease-specific contact rule, causal link, or medical recommendation.
The time axis is a fictional relative scale, not an epidemiological duration. No transmission arrows or infection probabilities may be added.

inputs.name: records
inputs.description: Recorded presence intervals for distinct fictional people at the venue.
inputs.constraints: 2..6 records; unique IDs <= 16 and labels <= 18 characters; numeric bounds 0..12 with start < end, or both null; one record per person.

inputs.name: investigationWindow
inputs.description: The authored comparison interval, not a generated clinical window.
inputs.constraints: 0 <= start < end <= axis.end; label 1..28 characters.

inputs.name: axis
inputs.description: Shared linear time extent and physical setting label.
inputs.constraints: start must be 0; end integer 2..12; all numeric record bounds and window bounds must lie within the axis; labels 1..24 characters.

inputs.name: sceneLabel
inputs.description: Persistent qualifier identifying the invented scene.
inputs.constraints: 1..40 characters; must identify fictional or approved sourced content.

inputs.name: showOverlapFractions
inputs.description: Show counts of overlap, no overlap, and unknown over all supplied people.
inputs.constraints: boolean

inputs.name: copy
inputs.description: All captions, legend labels, and quantity nouns used by the scene.
inputs.constraints: Exactly the documented default keys; each value 1..42 characters; preserve the defined meaning of each key.

bindingExample.shortSourceText: At a fictional market, two of four people's recorded visit intervals intersect a supplied review window, one does not, and one person's time is unknown.

verificationFocus: Only actual interval intersections with the investigation window are highlighted; touching nonoverlapping intervals and unknown records do not become confirmed contacts.

title: One sample, several aliquots
description: A parent specimen divides into labeled aliquot tubes while the parent identity stays visible. The remaining parent volume and the aliquot volumes reconcile exactly.
creativeDirection: Reveal the parent sample tube with its supplied volume. Move only the authored aliquot volumes into their child tubes while identity tethers retain the parent relationship; the parent level falls by the transferred amount. Hold the remaining parent volume plus all child volumes beside a derived equality and a separate specimen-family count, then fade.
goodFor: Explain why several laboratory tubes may originate from one collected specimen.
Show volume conservation during fictional aliquoting.
Distinguish source specimens, child containers, and measured volume.
intent: Show that splitting a specimen increases container count without creating more source specimens or volume.
distinction: Unlike source-merge or network-graph, matter visibly divides rather than information merely branching, and the parent liquid level changes to preserve volume. Unlike specimen-custody-seal, this explicitly creates child containers while preserving one source identity.
limits: Exactly one source specimen is represented. Child-tube count is aliquots.length; total shown tube count is 1 + aliquots.length, regardless of whether the parent remainder is zero.
sum(aliquots.volume) must be <= parent.volume. Parent remainder is derived by subtraction, so source volume equals child volume plus remainder; no loss or separate remainder input exists.
Volume units are fictional schematic units. Tube geometry is illustrative, not a calibrated laboratory instrument or a practical aliquoting procedure.
This shows lineage and bookkeeping only. No assay, sample suitability, diagnostic result, laboratory method, or clinical recommendation is implied.

inputs.name: parent
inputs.description: Source identity and starting schematic volume.
inputs.constraints: ID <= 16 and label <= 24 characters; volume integer 1..12.

inputs.name: aliquots
inputs.description: Child tube identities and assigned volumes.
inputs.constraints: 1..4 aliquots; unique IDs distinct from parent ID and <= 16 characters; labels <= 20 characters; volume integer 1..12; total child volume <= parent.volume.

inputs.name: unitLabel
inputs.description: The common unit used in all volume annotations.
inputs.constraints: 1..20 characters; defaults must remain explicitly schematic; no automatic unit conversion.

inputs.name: sceneLabel
inputs.description: Persistent qualifier identifying the invented scene.
inputs.constraints: 1..40 characters; must identify fictional or approved sourced content.

inputs.name: showLineage
inputs.description: Display persistent parent-to-child identity tethers and IDs.
inputs.constraints: boolean

inputs.name: showEquation
inputs.description: Display the source equals aliquots plus remainder equation using derived values.
inputs.constraints: boolean

inputs.name: copy
inputs.description: All captions, legend labels, and quantity nouns used by the scene.
inputs.constraints: Exactly the documented default keys; each value 1..42 characters; preserve the defined meaning of each key.

bindingExample.shortSourceText: One fictional specimen containing six schematic volume units is split into two aliquots of two and three units, leaving one unit in the parent tube.

verificationFocus: Parent remainder plus child aliquot volumes equals original volume, and every child retains its parent reference; oversubscribed volume fails validation.

title: Close the referral loop
description: People move from a referring clinic to a receiving service, while an acknowledgement travels back independently. Attendance and a closed communication loop remain visibly distinct.
creativeDirection: Frames 12..40 reveal the referring clinic with three people and three matching referral slips. Frames 41..113 let only attended people cross to the receiving service, then send a returned acknowledgement slip back for only the supplied completed loop. Frames 114..167 hold one returned loop, one attended-but-unacknowledged case, and one waiting case in their physical locations; fade to ground by frame 179.
goodFor: Explain referral tracking across separate care teams.
Distinguish attendance at another service from confirmation returned to the referring team.
Show an unresolved handoff without implying treatment failure.
intent: Show that a referral is not fully communicated merely because the person attended.
distinction: Unlike node-traversal or data-pipeline, person movement and document return are independent motions traveling in opposite directions. The resolved view can contain attendance without a returned acknowledgement.
limits: The denominator is referrals.length, one referral for one distinct person in this example. Waiting + attended without return + returned acknowledgement equals the total.
acknowledged=true requires attended=true. Derived attendance counts and returned-acknowledgement counts are labeled separately and may overlap; they must not be summed as exclusive categories.
An acknowledgement is communication evidence only. It does not establish diagnosis, treatment completion, recovery, clinical quality, or an appropriate referral.
No emergency priorities, treatment choices, clinical referral criteria, travel durations, or personal medical information are depicted.

inputs.name: referrals
inputs.description: Distinct fictional referrals and their attendance and returned-communication facts.
inputs.constraints: 1..5 referrals; unique IDs <= 16 and person labels <= 18 characters; boolean values; acknowledged implies attended; one referral per depicted person.

inputs.name: services
inputs.description: Names on the two physical care settings.
inputs.constraints: Exactly these keys; labels 1..24 characters.

inputs.name: sceneLabel
inputs.description: Persistent qualifier identifying the invented scene.
inputs.constraints: 1..40 characters; must identify fictional or approved sourced content.

inputs.name: emphasis
inputs.description: Choose whether the main emphasis follows attendance or the acknowledgement coming back.
inputs.constraints: Enum only; both facts remain separately represented.

inputs.name: showLedger
inputs.description: Show mutually exclusive final states and separately labeled attendance and acknowledgement fractions.
inputs.constraints: boolean

inputs.name: copy
inputs.description: All captions, legend labels, and quantity nouns used by the scene.
inputs.constraints: Exactly the documented default keys; each value 1..42 characters; preserve the defined meaning of each key.

bindingExample.shortSourceText: Of three fictional referrals, two people attended the receiving service, but only one acknowledgement returned to the referring clinic.
