verificationFocus: Attendance alone does not close the loop; only the supplied return acknowledgement reaches the referring service, with waiting cases retained separately.

title: Visits are not unique reach
description: An outreach worker walks a schematic neighborhood, visiting some homes more than once. A repeated visit adds to the activity count while the unique-household count stays unchanged.
creativeDirection: Reveal the supplied homes on a schematic neighborhood map. Move a worker through the authored visit sequence and leave event stamps at each stop. On repeat visits, add an activity stamp without changing the household's unique-reach outline. Hold contacted, not-contacted and unvisited households beside distinct event and unique-contact totals before fading.
goodFor: Explain why outreach visit totals differ from households contacted.
Show revisits and unvisited homes in a fictional community campaign.
Keep the household denominator visible when describing operational reach.
intent: Separate repeated outreach activity from the number of distinct households actually contacted.
distinction: Unlike node-traversal or dot-matrix, revisiting the same physical home deliberately increments one measure without incrementing another, making event-versus-entity semantics the central animation.
limits: The denominator is households.length and represents households, never residents or eligible people. Each home glyph is one household, independent of drawn house size.

Total visits is visits.length. Unique visited households is the distinct householdId count; unique contacted households is the distinct householdId count among visits marked contacted. These nested measures must not be added together.

Each household's final exclusive state is contacted if any visit made contact, visited-no-contact if visited but never contacted, or unvisited. These three state counts sum to the household denominator.

The local map is invented, normalized, and not georeferenced. Contact means only the supplied outreach encounter, not consent, service receipt, vaccination, health impact, or complete community coverage.

inputs.name: households
inputs.description: Fixed fictional household universe and schematic positions.
inputs.constraints: 3..8 households; unique IDs <= 16 and labels <= 16 characters; x and y in 0.1..0.9; minimum normalized center separation 0.18; coordinates are not longitude or latitude.

inputs.name: visits
inputs.description: Ordered outreach events, including repeated household visits.
inputs.constraints: 1..8 visits; each householdId must exist; contacted boolean; at most 3 visits per household; collection order is editorial sequence only.

inputs.name: sceneLabel
inputs.description: Persistent qualifier identifying the invented scene.
inputs.constraints: 1..40 characters; must identify fictional or approved sourced content.

inputs.name: showVisitStamps
inputs.description: Leave a discrete activity stamp for every visit, including revisits.
inputs.constraints: boolean

inputs.name: showUniqueLedger
inputs.description: Display total visits, unique visited households, and unique contacted households as separate measures.
inputs.constraints: boolean

inputs.name: copy
inputs.description: All captions, legend labels, and quantity nouns used by the scene.
inputs.constraints: Exactly the documented default keys; each value 1..42 characters; preserve the defined meaning of each key.

bindingExample.shortSourceText: Five fictional outreach visits reach four distinct homes and make contact with three households in a neighborhood containing six households.

verificationFocus: A repeat visit adds an event stamp but does not increase unique households reached; unsuccessful contacts remain distinct from successful household reach.

title: Bring the service closer
description: A mobile clinic relocates between two schematic community sites, carrying a finite set of appointment slots. People receive only the explicitly assigned bookings, with open slots and unbooked people still visible.
creativeDirection: Frames 12..40 show a mobile clinic parked at the first site, nearby people, and its finite appointment-slot strip. Frames 41..113 fold the clinic awning, drive the same vehicle along a schematic road, and reopen it at the second site; assigned people connect to distinct slot tabs while unmatched people remain in place. Frames 114..167 hold both the person-booking ledger and slot-capacity ledger together; fade to ground by frame 179.
goodFor: Explain a fictional mobile service relocation and bounded booking capacity.
Show that moving a service and booking people are distinct from delivering care.
Introduce community access planning while retaining unmet demand in the picture.
intent: Show a service moving toward a community while keeping finite appointment capacity and unbooked people visible.
distinction: Unlike radial-network or packet-stream, a physical service vehicle changes location and unfolds into a service point. Unlike outreach-household-revisits, the moving object is the service itself and the core constraint is one person per supplied slot, not visit activity.
limits: The people denominator is people.length. Booked people equals the number of non-null slotId values, and booked + unbooked equals the people total.

Slot capacity is slots.length. Occupied slots is the distinct assigned slotId count; occupied + open equals capacity. Each slot can have at most one assigned person, and no duplicated glyph creates extra capacity.
All assignments are authored. This is not a routing optimizer, access-distance model, clinical prioritization rule, eligibility decision, or recommendation for service placement.
Bookings are administrative plans, not attendance or treatment. The schematic map has no real geography, scale, journey time, distance measurement, or implied population coverage.

inputs.name: sites
inputs.description: The mobile clinic's starting and ending schematic locations.
inputs.constraints: Exactly 2 sites in travel order; unique IDs <= 16 and labels <= 22 characters; x and y in 0.15..0.85; center separation >= 0.4; no real coordinates.

inputs.name: slots
inputs.description: Finite bookable appointment slots shown after the clinic opens.
inputs.constraints: 1..6 slots; unique IDs <= 16 and labels <= 14 characters; no times or implied clinical duration.

inputs.name: people
inputs.description: The fictional community group and supplied booking assignments.
inputs.constraints: 1..8 people; unique IDs <= 16 and labels <= 16 characters; non-null slotId must exist and be unique across people; null means unbooked.

inputs.name: sceneLabel
inputs.description: Persistent qualifier identifying the invented scene.
inputs.constraints: 1..40 characters; must identify fictional or approved sourced content.

inputs.name: showSlotLedger
inputs.description: Show occupied and open slots alongside, but separately from, booked and unbooked people.
inputs.constraints: boolean

inputs.name: view
inputs.description: Use a schematic local scene directly or precede it with a small recognizable globe for context.
inputs.constraints: Enum only; globe does not locate or georeference the fictional sites.

inputs.name: copy
inputs.description: All captions, legend labels, and quantity nouns used by the scene.
inputs.constraints: Exactly the documented default keys; each value 1..42 characters; preserve the defined meaning of each key.

bindingExample.shortSourceText: A fictional mobile clinic moves to a community site with four appointment slots; three of five depicted people are booked and one slot remains open.

verificationFocus: The same clinic travels between sites; each supplied appointment slot is assigned at most once and unmatched people remain visible without invented bookings.

title: A world of separate crises
description: A slowly turning globe reveals fictional conflict X markers on recognizable world land outlines. Separate callouts stay distinct so a global overview does not collapse different situations into one story.
creativeDirection: Over six seconds, reveal an orthographic globe with simplified but recognizable continental outlines. Rotate through the supplied longitude interval, revealing each X only while its surface location faces the viewer; leader lines connect it to a fixed outside label slot. Ease the rotation to a stop, hold the visible markers and their scenario labels, then fade all scene elements to the opaque ground using the shared entrance and exit envelope. Keep the fictional-scenario caption visible with the globe, and never animate explosions, spreading red territory, or a conflict disappearing.
goodFor: Open an explicitly fictional global humanitarian scenario
Explain that response planning concerns several separate situations
Introduce a geographical overview before a local logistics example
intent: Show the geographic separation of several hypothetical response contexts without suggesting that one action resolves them.

inputs.name: incidents
inputs.description: Places authored X markers on the globe; array length alone determines marker count.
inputs.constraints: 1..4 entries; unique IDs <= 24 characters; labels <= 28 characters; latitude -60..70; longitude -180..180; use hypothetical locations only; no real conflict names

inputs.name: longitudeSweep
inputs.description: Sets the starting and ending central longitude of the orthographic view.
inputs.constraints: Each value -180..180 degrees; shortest sweep magnitude 40..160 degrees; at least one incident must be front-facing at the end

inputs.name: markerMeaning
inputs.description: Supplies the visible legend defining the X symbol.
inputs.constraints: Nonempty; <= 36 characters; must retain explicit fictional meaning

inputs.name: scenarioCaption
inputs.description: Keeps the distinction between real land outlines and invented incidents visible.
inputs.constraints: Nonempty; <= 54 characters; must explicitly identify fictional scenario data

inputs.name: showLabels
inputs.description: Shows the external incident callouts; the marker legend and scenario caption remain visible.
inputs.constraints: boolean

inputs.name: showGraticule
inputs.description: Adds restrained latitude and longitude curves for geographic orientation.
inputs.constraints: boolean

bindingExample.shortSourceText: For this fictional exercise, three separate conflict situations appear around a slowly turning world globe.

distinction: Unlike orbital-system, the central object is recognizable geographic land with front/back occlusion and surface-anchored incident markers. Unlike network-graph, no edges imply relationships among the incidents.
limits: The land outline is real geographic context; every conflict location and label is invented and must be marked as such.
X markers denote separate authored situations, not incident totals, severity, casualty counts, territorial control, or live intelligence.
No country borders or ownership claims are drawn. Marker visibility follows the chosen view and is not a statement that hidden regions lack need.
Six seconds supports orientation only; this is not a navigable map or an incident monitoring system.
verificationFocus: Markers behind the sphere are hidden, markers on the front project to their supplied coordinates, and X counts change only with supplied incidents, not globe rotation.

title: Keep the delivery moving
description: A delivery vehicle encounters a marked obstruction and takes an authored alternative road through a schematic local map. The destination remains the same while the route visibly changes.
creativeDirection: Reveal a depot, destination, and two roads within six seconds. The vehicle rolls toward the blocked segment, brakes before the barrier, then pivots at the preceding junction as the alternative route gains emphasis. The vehicle follows that authored detour to the destination, where the receiving team opens the gate; hold both the still-blocked road and the arrived vehicle before the shared opaque exit fade. Do not erase the obstruction or imply that a route was automatically verified.
goodFor: Explain a fictional access constraint in aid logistics
Show continuity through an agreed alternative route
Contrast an intended route with the route actually used
intent: Make an adaptation to a blocked route visible while preserving the original delivery purpose.

inputs.name: locations
inputs.description: Names the departure point, receiving point, and decision junction.
inputs.constraints: Each label <= 24 characters; fictional names only

inputs.name: routes
inputs.description: Defines both roads using normalized coordinates in the schematic map area.
inputs.constraints: Exactly 2 entries, one per role; IDs <= 24 characters; labels <= 24 characters; 4..6 points each; coordinates 0.1..0.9; routes share first two points and final point; detour must avoid blocked segment

inputs.name: obstruction
inputs.description: Chooses the blocked segment of the original road and the physical obstruction drawn there.
inputs.constraints: Index is an integer from 1 to blocked-route points.length - 2; label <= 26 characters; obstruction never lies on the detour

inputs.name: vehicle
inputs.description: Chooses the delivery vehicle silhouette without changing cargo quantity.
inputs.constraints: One listed value

inputs.name: scenarioCaption
inputs.description: Labels the geography and route as illustrative.
inputs.constraints: Nonempty; <= 48 characters; retain fictional and schematic meaning

inputs.name: showRouteLabels
inputs.description: Shows the names of the two authored roads.
inputs.constraints: boolean

bindingExample.shortSourceText: In the fictional Willow exercise, a closed bridge sends the aid truck along an agreed alternative road to the same reception point.

distinction: The physical braking, turn, obstacle persistence, and gate arrival explain adaptation. node-traversal only traces a fixed connection, while this scene replaces an unusable physical journey with a supplied detour.
limits: Routes are schematic and supplied by the author; the scene performs no routing, safety assessment, or access negotiation.
One vehicle represents one illustrative trip, never a fleet total or a delivery capacity.
Travel distance, speed, and elapsed animation time have no geographic or operational scale.
An open receiving gate denotes the authored arrival, not proof of permission, safety, or completed distribution.
verificationFocus: The vehicle stops before the blocked segment and uses the authored detour; the obstruction remains visible after arrival and the vehicle never traverses the closed edge.

title: One load, several carriers
description: The same labeled aid parcels move between physical transport modes. Keeping each parcel visible through the handoffs explains how a load can continue when the carrier changes.
creativeDirection: Within six seconds, reveal a boat or truck carrying the supplied parcels at the first transfer point. Animate one restrained unload-and-load motion per boundary: a dock hoist or handcart moves those exact parcels onto the next carrier, then the carrier advances into the next part of the cutaway landscape. End with the final carrier and its intact load at the named receiving point. Keep a persistent parcel identity mark through every handoff, hold the result, and use the shared entrance and opaque exit envelope.
goodFor: Explain a fictional boat-to-road or road-to-last-mile delivery
Show custody continuity across a transport change
Introduce intermodal constraints without a process chart
intent: Show that assistance continues as the same physical load across different carriers.

inputs.name: carriers
inputs.description: Sets the ordered transport modes and names their arrival or transfer places.
inputs.constraints: 2..3 entries; unique IDs <= 24 characters; handoff labels <= 24 characters; adjacent modes must differ; a boat may only appear first

inputs.name: parcels
inputs.description: Defines the load whose identities persist through every transfer.
inputs.constraints: 1..4 entries; unique IDs <= 24 characters; labels <= 26 characters; one parcel glyph per entry with no duplicates or disappearing parcels

inputs.name: transferMethod
inputs.description: Selects a visual handling method; the hoist is used only at a boat boundary.
inputs.constraints: One listed value; hoist-and-cart requires the first carrier to be boat

inputs.name: receivingLabel
inputs.description: Names the team opening the receiving area for the final carrier.
inputs.constraints: Nonempty; <= 30 characters

inputs.name: showParcelLabels
inputs.description: Shows short parcel labels alongside their persistent identity marks.
inputs.constraints: boolean

inputs.name: scenarioCaption
inputs.description: Keeps the scene framed as an illustrative delivery.
inputs.constraints: Nonempty; <= 48 characters; retain explicit fictional meaning

bindingExample.shortSourceText: A fictional food parcel and blanket pack move from a river boat to a truck and finally to a cargo bike without losing their identities.

distinction: This is a physical transshipment cutaway with unloading, loading, and conserved parcel identity. data-pipeline changes abstract stages; packet-stream moves interchangeable packets without carrier changes or handling actions.
limits: Parcel glyphs count the authored example parcels only; they are not weights, pallet equivalents, or reported distributions.
Transfer speed and carrier sizes are illustrative, not travel times or engineering capacity.
The scene ends at a receiving point, before household receipt; use a separate handover concept to explain confirmation by recipients.
No real route, organization branding, vehicle markings, or third-party assets are required.
verificationFocus: The exact parcel identities and counts survive every carrier transfer; a parcel occupies one carrier or transfer mechanism at a time without duplication.

title: Choose and count the handover
description: A household representative selects and physically counts the goods they want from an offered delivery. Only the chosen quantities move into their basket, while unselected goods remain with the delivery team.
creativeDirection: Within six seconds, reveal offered goods on a delivery table and the household representative indicating their configured selections. They pull exactly the selected units across a counting mat into their basket, one visible object per unit; untouched quantities stay on the delivery side. The chosen-quantity rows on a receipt fill from those actual movements, then the recipient acknowledges that specific list and keeps one copy. Hold the counted basket, retained goods, and receipt together before the shared opaque exit fade. The physical choice and counting occupy most of the shot; acknowledgement is only the final beat.
goodFor: Show household participation in a fictional last-mile handover
Explain the distinction between offered goods and selected quantities
Connect a receipt to the physical goods someone chose and counted
intent: Show the household controlling and checking which quantities it receives.

inputs.name: contents
inputs.description: Defines the offered objects, the household-authored selection, and the quantities copied onto the final receipt.
inputs.constraints: 1..4 entries; unique IDs <= 24 characters; labels <= 26 characters; offeredUnits integer 1..4; selectedUnits integer 0..offeredUnits; 2..10 offered units overall; 1..5 selected units overall; at least one unit remains unselected; one physical object per unit

inputs.name: participantLabels
inputs.description: Names the participating roles without identifying real people.
inputs.constraints: Each string nonempty and <= 28 characters

inputs.name: receiptLabels
inputs.description: Supplies every receipt label and the labels for offered, chosen, and retained goods.
inputs.constraints: Each string <= 28 characters; acknowledgement describes the listed received quantities only, never satisfaction or program success

inputs.name: acknowledgementMark
inputs.description: Chooses a fictional recipient-controlled acknowledgement symbol.
inputs.constraints: One listed value; initials uses the configured initials text

inputs.name: initialsText
inputs.description: Supplies the invented initials when that mark is selected.
inputs.constraints: 1..3 uppercase letters; fictional only; ignored for tick

inputs.name: showQuantityList
inputs.description: Shows the offered and selected quantity list while physical selection and counting remain visible.
inputs.constraints: boolean; receipt still lists actual selected quantities; displayed values derive only from contents

inputs.name: scenarioCaption
inputs.description: Labels the people, goods, and receipt as an authored example.
inputs.constraints: Nonempty; <= 48 characters; retain explicit fictional meaning

bindingExample.shortSourceText: In a fictional handover, a household representative chooses and counts two grain packs and one blanket, leaves the soap packs, and keeps a receipt for the selected goods.

distinction: The hero action is recipient-directed selection and physical counting from a larger offered set, with selected and retained quantities conserved. This differs from a generic custody acknowledgement or status-cycle, because acknowledgement follows a visible material choice rather than merely unlocking a transfer.
limits: Each drawn object is one fictional unit; offeredUnits equals selectedUnits plus retainedUnits for every good, with retainedUnits derived rather than separately configured.
Selected quantities are authored household choices, not a recommended package, nutritional target, eligibility entitlement, or real preference measurement.
The example assumes the offered goods may be selected individually; it does not claim that any real aid program permits substitutions or partial collection.
The receipt is a fictional acknowledgement of quantities, not legal proof, identity verification, satisfaction, or measured impact. Avoid real names, signatures, and identifiers.
verificationFocus: The basket and receipt equal the recipient's selected quantities; unselected goods remain on the table and no acknowledgement changes quantities.

title: Pool support, preserve its purpose
description: Contributor-marked demo credits gather in a transparent shared tray before being allocated to named funding requests. Earmarked credits keep their destination restriction, flexible credits can support different requests, and every unit remains attributable.
creativeDirection: Over six seconds, contributors tip small stacks of individually marked demo-credit tokens into a transparent shared tray. Earmarked tokens retain their destination ribbon; flexible tokens retain a distinct flexible marker. A community coordinator slides the configured tokens into labeled funding-request envelopes, preserving donor marks and respecting every earmark, while any unallocated tokens stay in the tray. Set each funded envelope upright with contributor marks visible above its edge, and hold the allocation totals alongside the remaining pool without transforming money into goods before the shared opaque exit fade. No token changes value, duplicates, or loses attribution.
goodFor: Explain earmarked and flexible contributions in a fictional pooled fund
Show how donor attribution survives shared resource allocation
Connect a jointly managed pool to specific funding requests without implying delivered outcomes
intent: Show that pooling resources can preserve both donor attribution and restrictions on their use.

inputs.name: requests
inputs.description: Defines the labeled funding-request envelopes receiving allocations.
inputs.constraints: 2..3 entries; unique IDs <= 24 characters; labels <= 28 characters; requests describe planned spending, not achieved outcomes

inputs.name: contributions
inputs.description: Defines exact contributor balances and whether each contribution is restricted to one request or flexible.
inputs.constraints: 2..4 entries; unique IDs <= 24 characters; donor labels <= 24 characters; unique marks 1..2 characters; credits integer 1..5; total credits <= 14; earmarkedRequestId null or existing request ID; include at least one earmarked and one flexible contribution

inputs.name: allocations
inputs.description: Assigns specific contributor units to request envelopes; unallocated units remain visibly in the pool.
inputs.constraints: 2..8 entries; valid contribution and request IDs; unique contribution/request pairs; credits integer 1..5; allocated sum per contribution <= its credits; earmarked contributions may allocate only to their earmarkedRequestId; each request receives at least one unit

inputs.name: labels
inputs.description: Supplies all visible role, restriction, allocation, residual, and quantity-unit labels.
inputs.constraints: Each string <= 26 characters; unit must explicitly identify fictional credits; labels must not imply goods have been delivered

inputs.name: showAllocationTotals
inputs.description: Shows per-envelope totals and the remaining pool balance, all derived from the configured token movements.
inputs.constraints: boolean; hiding numeric labels never hides or changes contributor marks or token quantities

inputs.name: envelopeArrangement
inputs.description: Places the receiving request envelopes around the shared physical tray.
inputs.constraints: One listed value; final donor marks remain visible above the envelope edge

inputs.name: scenarioCaption
inputs.description: Marks all contributions and allocations as illustrative demo units.
inputs.constraints: Nonempty; <= 48 characters; retain explicit fictional meaning

bindingExample.shortSourceText: Three fictional donors pool ten demo credits: four are earmarked for food transport, three for shelter access, and three are flexible; nine are allocated and one flexible credit remains.

distinction: Unlike source-merge, pooling is followed by a constrained physical allocation into separate funding requests, and contributor identity survives the entire sequence. The hero action is sorting and retaining attributed, restricted units, not convergence toward one destination or a fundraising counter.
limits: Every token is exactly one fictional demo credit; total contributions equal total allocations plus the visibly retained pool. Totals and residuals are derived, never separately authored.
Earmarked credits cannot move to another request. Flexible credits may be split only as explicitly configured, and donor marks remain visible throughout.
Funding envelopes represent planned spending allocations only. No conversion into goods, people served, delivery completion, or impact is implied.
The scene is a small authored example, not accounting software, a fundraising transaction, a financial recommendation, or real donor reporting.
verificationFocus: Every allocated token preserves donor attribution and obeys its earmark; allocations plus residual funds equal contributions and overspending fails.

title: A household chooses its basket
description: A household shopper chooses goods from a small market shelf and pays with fictional cash assistance or a voucher. The scene connects assistance to an authored choice instead of prescribing the same package for everyone.
creativeDirection: Reveal a shelf of configurable products and a shopper holding the chosen tender within six seconds. The shopper considers the shelf, reaches only for products marked chosen, and places those items into their own basket while the other options stay available. At the counter, move the cash or voucher to the retailer and show the exact selected-price sum, with any remaining demo credits retained by the shopper. Hold the chosen basket, then use the shared opaque exit fade.
goodFor: Explain household choice in an illustrative cash assistance program
Show a voucher redeemed for an authored basket
Bridge a funding story to the goods a shopper selects
intent: Show that assistance can support a household making its own purchase choices.

inputs.name: products
inputs.description: Defines the visible options, authored shopper choices, and fictional unit prices.
inputs.constraints: 2..5 entries; unique IDs <= 24 characters; labels <= 24 characters; integer price 1..9; 1..3 products chosen; selected price sum must not exceed availableCredits; one purchasable item per entry

inputs.name: availableCredits
inputs.description: Sets the shopper balance in explicitly fictional demo units.
inputs.constraints: Integer 1..30; at least the sum of chosen product prices; no real currency symbol

inputs.name: tender
inputs.description: Selects a paper cash or voucher object while preserving the same authored basket.
inputs.constraints: One listed value; cash and voucher are illustrations, not claims of equivalent real restrictions

inputs.name: labels
inputs.description: Supplies all role, unit, checkout, and tender labels.
inputs.constraints: Each string <= 24 characters; unit must explicitly identify fictional credits; tender label must match selected tender

inputs.name: showRemainingBalance
inputs.description: Shows availableCredits minus the selected product price sum after payment.
inputs.constraints: boolean; hidden balance does not change arithmetic or basket selection

inputs.name: scenarioCaption
inputs.description: Keeps the product choices and prices visibly illustrative.
inputs.constraints: Nonempty; <= 48 characters; retain explicit fictional meaning

bindingExample.shortSourceText: A fictional household uses an eight-credit voucher to choose grain and beans, leaving vegetables on the shelf and three demo credits for later.

distinction: The distinguishing action is an actor choosing among physical shelf goods and completing a purchase. This is neither source-merge nor metric-counter; the arithmetic supports the visible choice and does not become the hero motion.
limits: All prices and balances are small fictional values in demo credits, never real currency or current market information.
No nutritional, financial, or program eligibility recommendation is implied by the selected basket.
The scene assumes the authored goods are available and the authored tender is accepted; it does not establish real program rules.
One shopper represents the example household role, not household size or a reported beneficiary count.
verificationFocus: Only chosen products enter the household basket; their summed prices reduce the available credits exactly, and unaffordable selections fail.

title: Keep the shelf supplied
description: A retailer notices empty shelf spaces, receives a small replenishment, and makes the goods available for a shopper to choose. Physical inventory changes connect retail supply to usable assistance.
creativeDirection: Over six seconds, reveal the supplied opening stock as individual objects on a cutaway shelf. The retailer points to the empty spaces and places an order slip on the counter; a small delivery trolley arrives with exactly the incoming objects, which the retailer places into those spaces. A shopper then selects the authored purchase quantity while the remaining stock stays visible. Hold the final shelf and basket, with opening plus incoming minus selected quantities conserved, then fade to the opaque ground.
goodFor: Explain why cash assistance also depends on stocked local shops
Illustrate a fictional retailer replenishment cycle
Make the relationship between demand and physical availability visible
intent: Show that purchasing choice depends on goods reaching and remaining on the shelf.

inputs.name: goods
inputs.description: Defines all opening, delivered, and purchased objects for each shelf section.
inputs.constraints: 1..3 entries; unique IDs <= 24 characters; labels <= 24 characters; each quantity integer 0..4; openingUnits + incomingUnits <= 5 per good and <= 12 overall; total incomingUnits 1..6; total selectedUnits 1..3; selectedUnits <= openingUnits + incomingUnits

inputs.name: labels
inputs.description: Names the two participants, order slip, delivery, and the displayed quantity unit.
inputs.constraints: Each string <= 26 characters; unit must distinguish example objects from real measured inventory

inputs.name: deliveryMode
inputs.description: Selects the vehicle bringing the supplied incoming items.
inputs.constraints: One listed value

inputs.name: showQuantityLabels
inputs.description: Shows the derived on-shelf quantities at opening, after replenishment, and after purchase.
inputs.constraints: boolean; quantities are derived only from goods fields

inputs.name: showOrderSlip
inputs.description: Shows the retailer-authored request before the physical replenishment arrives.
inputs.constraints: boolean; no claim of automated ordering

inputs.name: scenarioCaption
inputs.description: Labels the shelf and inventory changes as an illustrative example.
inputs.constraints: Nonempty; <= 48 characters; retain explicit fictional meaning

bindingExample.shortSourceText: A fictional retailer replenishes grain and beans before a shopper chooses one item from each shelf.

distinction: Unlike data-pipeline, quantities physically leave a vehicle, occupy shelf slots, and move into a customer basket. Unlike household-market-choice, the main action is restoring availability before the purchase, with explicit conservation of inventory.
limits: Every visible product object corresponds to one authored example unit; no real stock, sales, price, or availability data is represented.
This animation illustrates an authored sequence, not a demand forecast, inventory optimization system, or guarantee against shortages.
Incoming supply and shopper choice are configured separately and validated for feasible quantities; no goods are silently invented.
The process is inspired by the relationship between retail supply and cash assistance, without copying agency assets or asserting any measured result.
verificationFocus: Closing stock equals opening plus incoming minus purchases for every product; the shelf and basket display those exact quantities.

title: Open the service someone chooses
description: A participant chooses a named community service and an access barrier is visibly addressed at its entrance. The person then approaches and enters by the accessible path shown in the example.
creativeDirection: Within six seconds, reveal two or three modest service entrances and a participant considering their labels. The participant points to the configured choice. At that entrance, either unfold a ramp over the step or roll a physical obstruction clear, according to the supplied access change; the staff member holds the door while the participant moves under their own power through it. Keep the other service options visible, hold the selected doorway and cleared path, then apply the shared opaque exit fade.
goodFor: Explain a fictional barrier to accessing shelter or community support
Show the combination of service choice and a usable entrance
Introduce an accessibility improvement through a physical action
intent: Show that a service becomes usable when a person can choose it and physically reach its entrance.

inputs.name: services
inputs.description: Defines the available service entrances and their visible labels.
inputs.constraints: 2..3 entries; unique IDs <= 24 characters; labels <= 26 characters; no medical services

inputs.name: chosenServiceId
inputs.description: Chooses the service the participant explicitly points toward and enters.
inputs.constraints: Must match exactly one services ID; <= 24 characters

inputs.name: accessChange
inputs.description: Selects the visible barrier removal at the chosen entrance.
inputs.constraints: One listed value; ramp changes a step; clear-entrance moves a portable obstruction; no other barrier is implied

inputs.name: participantMobility
inputs.description: Chooses the participant silhouette and self-directed movement along the accessible route.
inputs.constraints: One listed value; use a self-propelled wheelchair pose when selected; do not animate staff pushing the participant

inputs.name: labels
inputs.description: Supplies the role labels and the label for the participant-selected doorway.
inputs.constraints: Each string <= 24 characters

inputs.name: showChoiceLabel
inputs.description: Shows the short choice label after the participant points.
inputs.constraints: boolean; physical choice remains visible

inputs.name: scenarioCaption
inputs.description: Labels the participant and entrance arrangement as illustrative.
inputs.constraints: Nonempty; <= 48 characters; retain explicit fictional meaning

bindingExample.shortSourceText: A fictional participant chooses the shelter desk and enters independently after staff unfold a ramp over its step.

distinction: The central transformation changes physical access to a doorway, followed by participant-directed entry. It is not node-traversal, a generic status transition, or merely labels arriving on cards.
limits: The ramp and entrance are conceptual silhouettes, not dimensional design guidance or a certification of accessibility.
Removing one depicted physical barrier does not imply that language, eligibility, safety, affordability, or other barriers have been resolved.
Entry into a shelter desk does not imply a shelter placement, admission entitlement, or guaranteed housing.
The scene shows one fictional participant; it makes no population-level access or impact claim.
verificationFocus: Only the selected service's authored barrier changes; the participant follows the opened path and other available services retain their state.

title: Meet by mutual agreement
description: Two fictional family groups independently accept an arranged meeting and travel toward a shared meeting place. The scene centers their decisions and reunion rather than surveillance or automatic identity matching.
creativeDirection: Over six seconds, reveal the two groups on opposite sides of a schematic local setting, each holding their own invitation. Each group actively marks its invitation accepted; only after both marks appear do the groups begin walking toward the chosen meeting place. They arrive, turn toward each other, and make the configured greeting gesture without merging their silhouettes. Hold the gathering and the two accepted invitations, then fade with the standard opaque envelope.
goodFor: Illustrate an agreed reunion in a fictional displacement story
Explain why both parties participate in arranging a meeting
Show restored contact without implying automated identification
intent: Show a reunion as a mutually chosen meeting between people, not a system matching records.

inputs.name: groups
inputs.description: Defines the two consenting groups and the exact number of visible fictional people.
inputs.constraints: Exactly 2 groups; group IDs unique and <= 24 characters; group labels <= 28 characters; 1..3 members per group; member IDs globally unique and <= 24 characters; member labels <= 20 characters; no real identifying details

inputs.name: meetingLabel
inputs.description: Names the shared location chosen for the illustrated meeting.
inputs.constraints: Nonempty; <= 36 characters; fictional name only

inputs.name: invitationLabels
inputs.description: Supplies the invitation heading and active acknowledgement from each group.
inputs.constraints: Each string <= 26 characters; acceptance must express voluntary agreement

inputs.name: greeting
inputs.description: Sets the final greeting without requiring physical contact.
inputs.constraints: One listed value; no forced embrace or transformation of people into symbols

inputs.name: showMemberLabels
inputs.description: Shows the fictional member labels beneath their respective silhouettes.
inputs.constraints: boolean; group labels remain visible

inputs.name: scenarioCaption
inputs.description: Marks the example people and spatial arrangement as invented.
inputs.constraints: Nonempty; <= 54 characters; retain fictional and schematic meaning

bindingExample.shortSourceText: Two fictional family groups each agree to meet, walk to the community meeting place, and greet one another.

distinction: Two independent acts of agreement precede self-directed physical movement and a human greeting. Unlike source-merge, the people remain individuals; unlike schema-mapping, there is no inferred identity match.
limits: This portrays an already arranged fictional meeting, not tracing operations, identity verification, legal reunification, or safeguarding assessment.
Group membership and silhouette counts come only from the supplied arrays and are illustrative, not statistics about displaced families.
The setting has no geographic scale, real addresses, border crossings, or recommendations for travel.
No photographs, biometric matching, distress imagery, or real personal data are used.
verificationFocus: Groups move only after both invitations are accepted, and every member remains a distinct silhouette through the meeting and final greeting.

title: Rebalance a shared response
description: Community representatives and response teams rearrange physical service markers on a shared schematic tabletop map. An overlapping assignment moves to a requested location so the final plan reflects an explicit community priority.
creativeDirection: Within six seconds, reveal a tabletop map with authored community requests and team markers at their starting assignments. Where two team markers overlap, the community representative points to the requested destination; the reassigned team lifts its own marker and places it at that destination. Turn the relevant request tags face-up to show the configured final assignments, then hold the full plan with all remaining requests still visible. Use the shared opaque entrance and exit envelope, and avoid turning the whole map green.
goodFor: Explain a fictional coordination meeting about duplicated coverage
Show community input changing where a team plans to work
Contrast initial assignments with an agreed allocation
intent: Show a community request changing a shared plan while preserving visibility of what remains unassigned.

inputs.name: places
inputs.description: Defines the fictional local places and visible community requests on the table.
inputs.constraints: 2..4 entries; unique IDs <= 24 characters; place labels <= 24 characters; request labels <= 30 characters; normalized x and y 0.15..0.85; minimum separation 0.2 in normalized map coordinates

inputs.name: teams
inputs.description: Defines team markers and their authored starting and agreed assignments.
inputs.constraints: 2..4 entries; unique IDs <= 24 characters; labels <= 24 characters; service labels <= 22 characters; place references must exist; exactly one team changes place; its service must match the meaning of the destination request; at least two teams initially share its starting place

inputs.name: communityLabel
inputs.description: Names the people who point out the requested change before the team moves its own marker.
inputs.constraints: Nonempty; <= 30 characters

inputs.name: planLabels
inputs.description: Supplies phase and still-unassigned request labels without implying completed service delivery.
inputs.constraints: Each string <= 28 characters; wording must describe planning rather than achieved coverage

inputs.name: showUnassignedRequests
inputs.description: Shows the explicit open-request label for places with no team in the agreed plan; all request tags remain on the map.
inputs.constraints: boolean; disabling the extra label never erases unassigned requests

inputs.name: markerStyle
inputs.description: Selects physical tokens used by participants to revise the plan.
inputs.constraints: One listed value

inputs.name: scenarioCaption
inputs.description: Makes the geography and assignment plan visibly illustrative.
inputs.constraints: Nonempty; <= 54 characters; retain fictional and schematic meaning

bindingExample.shortSourceText: In a fictional community meeting, two information teams initially share area A; one agrees to move to the request in area B while area C remains unassigned.

distinction: The main action is a participant lifting and relocating a physical assignment in response to a visible community request. Unlike radial-network or schema-mapping, no abstract hub distributes signals and the plan is revised rather than merely connected.
limits: Markers represent authored team assignments, not measured coverage, beneficiary counts, delivery capacity, or verified access.
The final scene is an agreed illustrative plan, not evidence that a service reached a location.
The map is schematic and has no real geography or travel scale; no automatic allocation or route calculation is implied.
Service compatibility is an author-validated semantic constraint; the renderer cannot infer needs or determine an appropriate humanitarian response.
verificationFocus: Only supplied reassignments move team markers; all final teams reference valid places and unanswered community requests remain visible when requested.

title: Account for captured carbon
description: A cutaway follows atmospheric CO2 into storage while separately accounting for releases and operating emissions. The retained mass and the net accounting result remain visibly different quantities.
creativeDirection: Reveal an air boundary, capture unit and underground vessel. At the operator cue, divide the supplied captured-carbon ribbon into retained and released portions while a separate operating-emissions ribbon enters the accounting bracket. Hold the explicit retained-minus-operating-emissions calculation, including a negative result when supplied, then fade to the shared opaque ground without emptying the store on screen.
goodFor: Explain why gross capture differs from net removal accounting
Introduce a supplied capture-to-storage balance
Make operating emissions and a reporting boundary visible
intent: Show exactly what is counted before presenting a carbon removal total.

inputs.name: capture
inputs.description: Supply gross atmospheric capture and releases from that captured stream during the stated boundary.
inputs.constraints: Captured > 0 and <= 1000 t CO2; released between 0 and captured; finite numbers. Retained is derived as captured minus released, never an independent input.

inputs.name: operatingEmissions
inputs.description: Supply lifecycle emissions attributed to this capture batch, displayed in a separate CO2e lane.
inputs.constraints: 1..3 rows; unique IDs <= 20 characters; labels <= 26 characters; 0..1000 t CO2e each. Sum all rows once.

inputs.name: boundary
inputs.description: Name the system boundary, period and included operations.
inputs.constraints: Each string 1..44 characters; must describe the same boundary used for capture, releases and emissions.

inputs.name: decision
inputs.description: Name the person or organization responsible for executing the transfer.
inputs.constraints: Strings 1..32 characters; an editorial decision cue, not an interactive approval or verification stamp.

inputs.name: showNetAccounting
inputs.description: Show the retained CO2 minus operating-emissions calculation.
inputs.constraints: Boolean. When true, show negative results with their sign; never clamp the result to zero.

inputs.name: view
inputs.description: Choose a schematic underground store or an above-ground accounting vessel.
inputs.constraints: Enum only; neither option implies verified storage durability.

inputs.name: copy
inputs.description: Configure every remaining visible caption and unit label.
inputs.constraints: Captions <= 30 characters; disclaimer <= 48; unit labels <= 10 and must preserve tonnes CO2 versus tonnes CO2e semantics.

bindingExample.shortSourceText: For this fictional atmospheric-capture batch, 12 tonnes of CO2 were captured, 1 tonne was released, and operating emissions were 2 tonnes CO2e, leaving a 9-tonne CO2e accounting result.

distinction: Uses a split physical mass stream, a visible storage boundary and a separate emissions subtraction. It is neither a renamed data pipeline nor a standalone metric counter.
limits: Retained CO2 = captured CO2 - released CO2. Net result = retained CO2 expressed as CO2e - summed operating emissions. CO2 has a conversion factor of one here; no other captured gas is modeled.
Storage beyond the named reporting period, additionality, displacement and verification are not inferred. A positive balance is not a durability certificate.
All defaults are fictional. The six-second motion compresses one supplied reporting period and is not a capture-rate simulation.
verificationFocus: Retained carbon equals captured minus released carbon; net removal subtracts separately supplied operating emissions with compatible units, and negative net values remain negative rather than clipped.

title: Pack work, release capacity
description: Fixed compute workloads move between server bays while their total resource demand stays constant. An operator-approved placement leaves an empty host eligible for sleep without claiming a measured energy saving.
creativeDirection: Reveal host bays holding the supplied work blocks. After the scheduler cue, slide intact blocks into the authored available capacity on retained hosts; emptied hosts fold into the chosen idle-state outline. Hold unchanged total work beside occupied and empty host counts derived from the inputs, then fade to ground. Workload consolidation does not invent measured energy savings.
goodFor: Explain resource-aware workload placement
Show how consolidation can free an entire host
Separate compute demand from a claim about electricity consumption
intent: Show how a placement decision can free capacity while preserving the work performed.

inputs.name: hosts
inputs.description: Define host bays and their available CPU-time capacity within one common window.
inputs.constraints: 2..4 hosts; unique IDs <= 20 characters; labels <= 20; capacity > 0 and <= 64 CPU-hours. Array determines bay count.

inputs.name: jobs
inputs.description: Move whole authored workloads between placements without changing their CPU-hours.
inputs.constraints: 2..8 jobs; unique IDs <= 20 characters; labels <= 18; cpuHours > 0 and <= 64. Both host IDs must exist. Each placement must fit every host capacity; no splitting or dropped work.

inputs.name: windowLabel
inputs.description: Label the common workload and capacity accounting interval.
inputs.constraints: 1..36 characters. CPU-hours are summed core time, not elapsed time or kWh.

inputs.name: decision
inputs.description: Expose the person choosing to apply the proposed placement.
inputs.constraints: Both strings 1..32 characters; feasibility must be supplied, not inferred by the drawing.

inputs.name: emptyHostState
inputs.description: Choose whether empty hosts visibly enter sleep or remain available.
inputs.constraints: Enum only; host state is a declared operational choice, not proof of a power-state transition.

inputs.name: showCapacityGuides
inputs.description: Show filled and unused portions of each host bay.
inputs.constraints: Boolean; proportional heights use CPU-hour capacity on a common scale.

inputs.name: copy
inputs.description: Configure visible placement, state, accounting and unit captions.
inputs.constraints: Captions <= 28 characters; unit <= 14 and must retain CPU-hour meaning; disclaimer <= 48.

bindingExample.shortSourceText: A fictional platform operator repacks three batches totaling 6 CPU-hours onto two hosts and puts the empty third host to sleep.

distinction: The main action is geometric bin packing with an emptied physical resource. Unlike source-merge, each job keeps its identity and size; unlike bar-race, there is no ranking.
limits: The workload total is the sum of jobs in both placements. Host counts and occupied capacity are derived from assignments, never separately entered.
CPU-hours do not establish kWh, carbon emissions, runtime, latency or monetary savings. Memory, locality, reliability and migration cost are outside this schematic.
Defaults are fictional and represent supplied feasible placements, not a scheduling algorithm or an optimization guarantee.
verificationFocus: Every job preserves its work quantity and runs within host capacity; only truly empty hosts enter the chosen idle state and no energy/emissions savings are inferred from CPU-hours.

title: Hold water, show the spill
description: A local cutaway routes a bounded stormwater volume through infiltration, controlled discharge and finite detention. Any remaining water visibly spills instead of disappearing.
creativeDirection: Reveal a schematic street and basin with a marked storage lip. At the operator cue, the supplied inflow divides into infiltration, controlled outflow and detention compartments. Once detention reaches its capacity, the remaining water crosses a distinct overflow crest. Hold all destinations with an explicit conserved-volume equation before fading.
goodFor: Explain finite stormwater storage and overflow
Introduce a supplied event water balance
Show what an outlet operating choice accounts for
intent: Make the limit of an adaptation measure visible alongside the water it manages.

inputs.name: event
inputs.description: Supply event inflow and two known outflows across the named boundary.
inputs.constraints: Incoming > 0 and <= 10000 m3; nonnegative infiltration and discharge whose sum <= incoming. These are supplied totals, not outputs of a hydrology model.

inputs.name: detentionCapacityM3
inputs.description: Set the initially empty basin capacity.
inputs.constraints: 0..10000 m3. Detained = min(capacity, incoming - infiltration - discharge); overflow is the remaining volume.

inputs.name: boundary
inputs.description: Label the local catchment and event represented.
inputs.constraints: Strings 1..42 characters; always identify geography as schematic. No real location is inferred.

inputs.name: decision
inputs.description: Name the operational choice before the water balance unfolds.
inputs.constraints: Strings 1..32 characters; the animation uses supplied event totals and does not calculate gate performance.

inputs.name: overflowSide
inputs.description: Place the separate overflow path on a readable side of the cutaway.
inputs.constraints: Enum only; presentation choice, not a real downstream destination.

inputs.name: showBalance
inputs.description: Show inflow equaling infiltration plus discharge plus detention plus overflow.
inputs.constraints: Boolean; when hidden, the visible water still follows the same conserved partition.

inputs.name: copy

default.disclaimer: Fictional volumes; not a flood forecast

inputs.description: Configure all flow, storage and unit captions.
inputs.constraints: Captions <= 30 characters; unit <= 8 with cubic-metre meaning; disclaimer <= 50.

bindingExample.shortSourceText: In a fictional storm event, 120 cubic metres reaches a block: 20 infiltrates, 50 is discharged, 40 is held, and 10 overflows.

copy.disclaimer: Fictional volumes; not a flood forecast

distinction: A vessel physically reaches capacity and activates a spill path. This explains a finite storage boundary rather than a generic stream or state progression.
limits: The basin begins empty. Incoming = infiltrated + controlled discharge + final detention + overflow; no water is deleted or counted in two destinations.
Inputs describe aggregate event volumes, not simultaneous flow rates. Terrain, drainage capacity, soil and downstream risk are not simulated.
The scene does not claim flood prevention or predict a real flood extent. Defaults and local geography are fictional.
verificationFocus: Infiltration, controlled discharge, detention and overflow sum to inflow; detention never exceeds capacity and excess remains visible as overflow.

title: Place shade where people wait
description: Authored shade footprints unfold over a schematic street after a selected installation decision. The scene measures added shaded area at one stated sun condition without implying a temperature or health outcome.
creativeDirection: Reveal the supplied street zones with their existing shade footprints. At the installation cue, extend awnings or open canopy footprints over the authored nonoverlapping additions. Hold total shaded area against the complete zone area at the supplied reference condition, retaining the unshaded ground, then fade without implying a measured temperature reduction.
goodFor: Explain the physical footprint of a heat-adaptation proposal
Show where a shade investment is placed
Distinguish installed shade area from a cooling claim
intent: Connect an implementation choice to a clearly bounded change in shade coverage.
family: Schematic plan with unfolding shade footprints

inputs.name: zones
inputs.description: Define nonoverlapping ground zones and their existing shaded area.
inputs.constraints: 1..4 zones; unique IDs <= 20 characters; labels <= 26; area > 0 and <= 10000 m2; existing shade between 0 and area.

inputs.name: installations
inputs.description: Supply additional nonoverlapping footprints and their visual forms.
inputs.constraints: 1..4 installations; unique IDs <= 20 characters; labels <= 28; existing zoneId; added shade >= 0. Sum of added plus existing shade in each zone must not exceed zone area.

inputs.name: referenceCondition
inputs.description: State the single sun condition to which the supplied footprint applies.
inputs.constraints: 1..42 characters; not a weather prediction or an automatically computed solar position.

inputs.name: decision
inputs.description: Expose who chooses the locations and whether the supplied design is proposed or installed.
inputs.constraints: Actor/action 1..32 characters; enum stage. Proposal uses outlined structures; installed uses solid structures. Neither proves performance.

inputs.name: showAreaBalance
inputs.description: Show shaded and unshaded areas summing to the total mapped zone area.
inputs.constraints: Boolean; counts and totals are derived from zones and installations.

inputs.name: copy
inputs.description: Configure every map, status, area and unit caption.
inputs.constraints: Captions <= 28 characters; unit <= 8 and denotes square metres; disclaimer <= 48.

bindingExample.shortSourceText: A fictional design places an awning and a canopy footprint over two waiting spaces, adding 60 square metres of nonoverlapping shade to the existing 40.

distinction: Canopies unfold into visible ground footprints and preserve uncovered area. This is a spatial intervention, not a chart of temperatures or a relabeled card collection.
limits: Total ground area stays constant. Final shade = existing shade + supplied nonoverlapping additions; unshaded area = total ground - final shade.
The plan is schematic. Footprint tiling communicates area totals rather than real street geometry or a solar calculation.
Tree-canopy dimensions are authored for the named condition, not instantaneous tree growth. No temperature, exposure, health or measured efficacy claim is derived.
verificationFocus: Added nonoverlapping shade plus existing shade never exceeds each zone area; the total shaded denominator remains the full supplied street area.

title: Keep sediment within the slope
description: A hillside cross-section shows a supplied sediment load encountering an installed contour barrier. Retained soil settles visibly upstream while exported sediment crosses the catchment boundary.
creativeDirection: Reveal a bare schematic slope and its outlet boundary. A land steward places the selected contour treatment, then the supplied sediment ribbon moves downslope and separates into retained material behind the strip and export beyond the boundary. Hold both destinations against their common incoming mass, then fade rather than reversing erosion.
goodFor: Explain a sediment retention mechanism
Make exported material visible in a land-restoration story
Present an authored soil-mass balance without claiming a universal retention rate
intent: Show where supplied sediment ends up after a particular land-management intervention.

inputs.name: sediment
inputs.description: Supply sediment entering the depicted transport segment and retained within it.
inputs.constraints: Mobilized > 0 and <= 1000 kg; retained between 0 and mobilized. Export is derived by subtraction.

inputs.name: intervention
inputs.description: Select the physical barrier silhouette and its label.
inputs.constraints: Enum kind; label 1..30 characters. Changing kind never changes the supplied retained quantity automatically.

inputs.name: boundary
inputs.description: Name the area and event represented by the mass accounting.
inputs.constraints: Strings 1..42 characters; area is explicitly schematic and period is not animation duration.

inputs.name: decision
inputs.description: Name the implementation action that precedes transport.
inputs.constraints: Strings 1..32 characters; no implied autonomous land restoration.

inputs.name: showExportTray
inputs.description: Show the external collection tray as well as the outlet arrow.
inputs.constraints: Boolean. If false, export quantity stays labeled at the boundary; it cannot disappear from the accounting.

inputs.name: copy

default.disclaimer: Fictional mass balance; not a field result

inputs.description: Configure sediment, boundary, unit and qualification captions.
inputs.constraints: Captions <= 30 characters; unit <= 8 and denotes kilograms; disclaimer <= 52.

bindingExample.shortSourceText: For one fictional runoff event, an installed contour strip retains 5 kilograms of an 8-kilogram mobilized sediment load, while 3 kilograms leaves the boundary.

copy.disclaimer: Fictional mass balance; not a field result

distinction: Particles settle into a persistent landform while the remainder crosses a boundary. It demonstrates selective deposition, not simple packet movement through stages.
limits: Mobilized sediment = retained sediment + exported sediment. The water carrying it is illustrative and unquantified; do not equate water-particle counts with sediment kilograms.
The retained mass is supplied content, never inferred from barrier type, slope angle or vegetation. No before/after efficacy comparison is manufactured.
No soil formation rate, crop yield, water quality outcome or ecological recovery is predicted. Defaults are fictional.
verificationFocus: Retained sediment plus exported sediment equals the incoming mass; changing the intervention representation does not change supplied outcome quantities.

title: Recover parts, account for residue
description: A returned object opens into identifiable components that follow reuse, repair, recycling or residue routes. Reassembled output and separate material bins reconcile with returned mass plus any replacement inputs.
creativeDirection: Reveal the returned assembly within its stated material boundary. An operator separates its labeled parts into their supplied reuse, repair, recycling and residue destinations. Separately labeled replacement inputs join the recovered parts in the new assembly. Hold the new assembly, recycling and residue with an input-output mass equation, then fade.
goodFor: Explain repair and reuse before material recycling
Account for material leaving a circular process
Show replacement input alongside recovered components
intent: Show which material returns to use and which material still leaves the loop.

inputs.name: parts
inputs.description: Define the returned assembly and the supplied disposition of each whole component.
inputs.constraints: 2..6 parts; unique IDs <= 20 characters; labels <= 22; mass > 0 and <= 100 kg. Each part has exactly one route; no hidden recovery yield.

inputs.name: replacementInputs
inputs.description: Supply new material entering the reassembled output from outside the return boundary.
inputs.constraints: 0..3 inputs; unique IDs <= 20 characters and distinct from part IDs; labels <= 26; mass > 0 and <= 100 kg. All replacement mass enters output.

inputs.name: decision
inputs.description: Identify who chooses and executes the supplied routes.
inputs.constraints: Strings 1..34 characters; no automated inspection, certification or repair success is inferred.

inputs.name: assemblyShape
inputs.description: Choose a generic recognizable object silhouette for the exploded view.
inputs.constraints: Enum only; geometry is schematic and does not assert actual component compatibility.

inputs.name: showMassEquation
inputs.description: Show returned plus replacement mass equaling assembly plus recycling plus residue.
inputs.constraints: Boolean; all quantities derive from the two collections.

inputs.name: copy
inputs.description: Configure destination, boundary, mass-unit and qualification labels.
inputs.constraints: Captions <= 30 characters; unit <= 8 and denotes kilograms; disclaimer <= 48.

bindingExample.shortSourceText: A fictional 10-kilogram returned module contributes 6 kilograms of reused or repaired parts; adding 2 kilograms of replacements leaves an 8-kilogram assembly, 3 kilograms sent to recycling and 1 kilogram of residue.

distinction: Identifiable parts physically disassemble and some reassemble into a new whole. The explicit external input and residue prevent the closed-circle illusion of a generic circular arrow.
limits: Returned mass + replacement input = reassembled mass + recycling-stream mass + residue. Reassembled mass includes reuse and repair routes without assuming mass loss.
Sent to recycling is not the same as recovered secondary material. No recovery yield, virgin-material displacement, embodied-carbon saving or infinite recyclability is claimed.

Repair success and component compatibility are authored assumptions in this fictional example. Additional process inputs or losses require extending the supplied boundary, not silently discarding mass.
verificationFocus: Original component mass plus replacement inputs equals assembled mass plus recycling plus residue; each component goes to exactly its declared destination.

title: Store energy, deliver less
description: A battery cutaway connects a charging window to a later dispatch window while retaining explicit conversion losses. A human dispatch instruction determines when the stored energy is released.
creativeDirection: Reveal the battery between authored charging and delivery windows. Charging input enters the boundary, a distinct loss channel peels away, and the remaining energy fills storage. At the dispatch cue, delivered energy reaches the later load while discharge losses enter their own channel. Hold input, delivery, losses and final storage together with a conserved-energy equation before fading.
goodFor: Explain energy time shifting
Show why delivered energy is below charging input
Present a supplied battery dispatch schedule and its losses
intent: Explain how a dispatch decision moves usable energy between time windows with losses accounted for.

inputs.name: battery
inputs.description: Define usable capacity and energy already inside the battery boundary.
inputs.constraints: Capacity > 0 and <= 10000 kWh; initial stored between 0 and capacity.

inputs.name: cycle
inputs.description: Supply the energy entering, delivered and lost during this cycle.
inputs.constraints: All values finite and 0..10000 kWh; chargeLoss <= chargeInput. Peak stored = initial + input - chargeLoss must fit capacity. Final stored = peak - delivered - dischargeLoss must be >= 0.

inputs.name: windows
inputs.description: Label the ordered time windows, source and destination.
inputs.constraints: Strings 1..32 characters; charging precedes dispatch. Labels do not establish renewable origin or emissions intensity.

inputs.name: decision
inputs.description: Expose who implements the supplied schedule.
inputs.constraints: Strings 1..32 characters; no autonomous grid optimization is claimed.

inputs.name: showLossChannels
inputs.description: Show separate heat-like ribbons for charge and discharge loss.
inputs.constraints: Boolean; loss numbers remain in the equation even when decorative ribbons are hidden.

inputs.name: orientation
inputs.description: Choose a left-to-right or top-to-bottom battery and load layout.
inputs.constraints: Enum only; energy accounting and window ordering stay identical.

inputs.name: copy
inputs.description: Configure remaining energy captions, unit and qualification.
inputs.constraints: Captions <= 26 characters; unit <= 8 and denotes kilowatt-hours; disclaimer <= 48.

bindingExample.shortSourceText: A fictional operator charges a battery with 10 kWh at midday and later delivers 8 kWh, with 1 kWh lost on charging and 1 kWh on discharge.

distinction: A finite physical store fills and empties across distinct time windows while loss branches remain visible. Unlike metric-counter or line-trace, the explanation rests on conserved energy and dispatch timing.
limits: Initial stored energy + charge input = final stored energy + delivered energy + charge loss + discharge loss. All values are energy, never power.
The six-second animation does not model charge rates, degradation, battery chemistry, grid constraints, costs or emissions. No round-trip efficiency is claimed beyond the supplied cycle arithmetic.
Source and load labels are configurable, but electricity origin and environmental benefit require separate evidence. Defaults are fictional.
verificationFocus: Charge input equals delivered energy plus charge/discharge losses and storage change; capacity and efficiency bounds reject impossible cycles.

title: Keep gaps visible in the evidence
description: A recognizable globe opens onto a schematic environmental observation tile. A cloud mask leaves missing cells blank, and a field-check marker adds point evidence without filling the surrounding unsampled area.
creativeDirection: Reveal the globe as geographic context, then unfold a detached schematic observation tile. A cloud layer lifts to reveal supplied cell readings while missing cells retain their hatch. A field team places the supplied point checks without replacing any whole-cell missing value. Hold the distinction between point sampling and area coverage, then fade.
goodFor: Explain cloud gaps in environmental observations
Distinguish area samples from point field checks
Show monitoring evidence requiring a follow-up visit
intent: Show that an additional observation does not automatically resolve every nearby evidence gap.

inputs.name: cells
inputs.description: Define the schematic tile observations; null is an explicit missing area observation.
inputs.constraints: 4..12 cells; unique IDs <= 20 characters; labels <= 16; integer rows 0..2 and columns 0..3; unique coordinates forming a filled rectangle. Values finite within metric bounds or null. Array determines grid dimensions.

inputs.name: metric
inputs.description: Define the measured variable, shared value scale, support area and observation period.
inputs.constraints: Label <= 26, unit <= 12, period <= 38 characters; minimum < maximum, both finite; cell area > 0 and <= 1000 ha. All cells and field checks use this variable and unit.

inputs.name: fieldChecks
inputs.description: Add explicitly point-supported readings at selected cells.
inputs.constraints: 0..3 checks; unique IDs <= 20 characters; labels <= 22; existing cellId; finite value within metric bounds. Point observations never replace the cell value.

inputs.name: decision
inputs.description: Name the team and deliberate follow-up action.
inputs.constraints: Strings 1..32 characters; adding a field-check prop means an authored observation, not proof that a visit occurred.

inputs.name: context
inputs.description: Choose whether to introduce the local evidence tile with a recognizable globe.
inputs.constraints: Enum only; globe uses built-in continental silhouettes with no location pin or zoom route. The detached tile is never presented as a mapped real place.

inputs.name: showCoverageTotals
inputs.description: Show area with supplied cell readings and area missing those readings.
inputs.constraints: Boolean; area totals derive solely from cell count times cellAreaHa. Point checks do not increase area coverage.

inputs.name: copy
inputs.description: Configure geographic, observation-support and unit captions.
inputs.constraints: Captions <= 34 characters; areaUnit <= 8 and denotes hectares; disclaimer <= 48.

bindingExample.shortSourceText: A fictional environmental tile has readings for 4 of 6 hectares; a point field check inside a cloudy cell adds evidence but leaves the area-wide observation missing.

distinction: Masks preserve spatial gaps while a second sampling support is layered over them. This is neither a scanning band nor a node network, and it avoids converting point evidence into invented area coverage.
limits: Observed area + missing area = number of cells times cellAreaHa. Field checks have point support and contribute no hectares to coverage totals.
The globe is recognizable context only; the tile is explicitly schematic. No real region, live sensor, remote basemap, satellite accuracy or environmental trend is implied.
Values are fictional and share one variable, unit and authored observation period. The graphic cannot establish measurement comparability or field validation accuracy.
verificationFocus: Unknown cells retain a missing-data hatch; adding a point field check does not silently fill the entire cell or count its whole area as observed.

title: Budget the water below ground
description: A subsurface water store changes as recharge and approved withdrawals cross its boundary. A planner reduces an authored request to an approved allocation while the final storage and remaining request stay explicit.
creativeDirection: Reveal a schematic aquifer at its supplied initial storage and the requested withdrawal beside it. A planner sets the authored approved withdrawal; show recharge entering while pumping and natural outflow leave through distinct paths. Hold the derived remaining storage and any unmet portion of the request, then fade without refilling the aquifer.
goodFor: Explain withdrawal decisions within a water budget
Show that recharge does not erase other outflows
Distinguish requested water from water actually allocated
intent: Make the storage consequence of a human allocation decision visible.

inputs.name: aquifer
inputs.description: Define initial accounting stock and the capacity of the schematic storage scale.
inputs.constraints: Initial >= 0; diagram capacity > 0 and <= 1000000 m3; initial <= capacity. Diagram capacity is a visual bound, not a measured aquifer safe yield.

inputs.name: flows
inputs.description: Supply recharge, natural outflow, requested withdrawal and the executed allocation.
inputs.constraints: All values 0..1000000 m3; approved <= requested. Initial + recharge must fit diagram capacity; final = initial + recharge - natural outflow - approved must be >= 0. Request is not an executed flow.

inputs.name: boundary
inputs.description: Name the reservoir boundary, period and included accounting scope.
inputs.constraints: Strings 1..44 characters; all supplied flow totals use this same period and boundary.

inputs.name: decision
inputs.description: Identify the actor setting the final allocation.
inputs.constraints: Strings 1..34 characters; the choice is supplied, not presented as an optimized or legally authorized allocation.

inputs.name: showUnallocatedRequest
inputs.description: Retain the difference between requested and approved withdrawal as a hollow bracket.
inputs.constraints: Boolean; unallocated request = request minus approval and never enters the water balance.

inputs.name: copy

default.disclaimer: Fictional budget; not a sustainable-yield model

inputs.description: Configure every water-budget and qualification caption.
inputs.constraints: Captions <= 28 characters; unit <= 8 and denotes cubic metres; disclaimer <= 56.

bindingExample.shortSourceText: In a fictional aquifer budget, a planner approves 150 cubic metres of a 200-cubic-metre request; with 120 entering and 30 leaving naturally, storage falls from 1000 to 940 cubic metres.

copy.disclaimer: Fictional budget; not a sustainable-yield model

distinction: The visible store changes because of bounded inflow and outflow, and a hollow unfulfilled request is deliberately excluded from physical water. This is an allocation-and-stock explanation rather than a generic flow chart.
limits: Initial storage + recharge = final storage + natural outflow + approved withdrawal. Unallocated requests are quantities of demand, not water stored elsewhere.
The diagram treats only listed boundary flows and a single accounting period. Water level, pressure, quality, ecological needs and lateral flow are not simulated.
Neither final storage nor a reduced request proves sustainable use, legal compliance or equity. Defaults and the cutaway are fictional.
verificationFocus: Final storage equals initial storage plus recharge minus withdrawals and natural outflow; unmet request remains visible and withdrawals cannot exceed available water.

title: Build a route between habitats
description: A planned habitat strip and crossing physically reconnect two separated patches on a schematic land-use map. The same mapped area changes use, and an optional illustrative traversal shows designed connectivity without asserting ecological recovery.
creativeDirection: Reveal habitat patches separated by working land and a road. At the land-management cue, lay the authored corridor footprint across the gap and lift its crossing over the road. Transfer that footprint's area from other land to habitat within the fixed boundary. Optionally move an explicitly illustrative marker along the supplied connection, then hold the conserved land balance.
goodFor: Explain spatial habitat reconnection
Show the land commitment behind a corridor proposal
Distinguish a designed route from evidence of animal use
intent: Show the physical land-use change required to connect separated habitat patches.
family: Schematic land-use map and constructed crossing

inputs.name: patches
inputs.description: Define the two habitat patches on either side of the barrier.
inputs.constraints: Exactly 2 patches; unique IDs <= 20 characters; labels <= 24; each area > 0 and <= 10000 ha. Array owns patch count.

inputs.name: corridor
inputs.description: Define the new nonoverlapping strip and its endpoint patches.
inputs.constraints: Label <= 32 characters; length and width > 0 and <= 10000 m; different existing endpoint IDs. New area = length * width / 10000 ha; dimensions describe a rectangular accounting footprint.

inputs.name: landBoundaryHa
inputs.description: Set the unchanged area of the schematic land-use boundary.
inputs.constraints: Greater than or equal to patch area sum plus corridor area and <= 100000 ha. Corridor land is reclassified from the remaining other-land area, never added to the map total.

inputs.name: decision
inputs.description: Name the implementation decision and whether its footprint is proposed or implemented.
inputs.constraints: Actor/action 1..34 characters; enum stage. Proposed route remains outlined; implemented route is solid. Status is authored content, not certification.

inputs.name: showIllustrativeTraversal
inputs.description: Optionally move a neutral marker along the designed connection.
inputs.constraints: Boolean. If true, the illustrative-traversal caption stays visible; the marker is not an animal count or observed movement record.

inputs.name: showLandBalance
inputs.description: Show habitat and other land summing to the fixed boundary area.
inputs.constraints: Boolean; both before and after values derive from patches, corridor dimensions and boundary.

inputs.name: copy

default.disclaimer: Fictional plan; no ecological outcome claim
