inputs.description: Configure geography, land-use, dimension, status and qualification captions.
inputs.constraints: Captions <= 28 characters; unit labels <= 8 and preserve hectares/metres; disclaimer <= 54.

bindingExample.shortSourceText: A fictional team proposes a 200-metre by 20-metre habitat connection between 3- and 4-hectare patches, reallocating 0.4 hectares within a fixed 20-hectare boundary.

copy.disclaimer: Fictional plan; no ecological outcome claim

distinction: A physical strip changes land use and bridges a barrier before a route can be traversed. Unlike network-graph or node-traversal, the connection requires a visible spatial intervention and an area budget.
limits: Total mapped area is conserved: existing habitat + other land before = existing habitat + corridor + other land after. The crossing is part of the corridor footprint, not additional habitat area.
Geometry is schematic; footprint area is calculated from supplied rectangular dimensions, while visual patch shape is not a geographic measurement.

Designed connectivity does not establish species suitability, movement, survival, biodiversity gain or long-term restoration success. Traversal is optional and explicitly illustrative; defaults are fictional.
verificationFocus: Added corridor area transfers from other land within a fixed land boundary; illustrative traversal does not imply measured species use and all route gaps are actually connected.

title: The same classroom, different days
description: A fixed classroom shows which members of one fictional roster are present across several school days. Empty seats and unknown attendance remain visibly different.
creativeDirection: Reveal the supplied roster at named desks and a day label. Across the authored day changes, the same learner silhouettes occupy or vacate their own desks while absent seats keep empty outlines and unknown seats keep question markers. Preserve small day impressions beneath each desk instead of sending people through lanes. Hold the final room with present, absent, unknown and roster totals before fading.
goodFor: Explain daily attendance without confusing repeat visits with new students
Show that an unchanged roster can have changing classroom presence
Make missing attendance records visible
intent: Distinguish who belongs to a class from who is recorded present on each day.

inputs.name: learners
inputs.description: The fixed roster. Each entry owns exactly one desk and one persistent learner identity.
inputs.constraints: 3..8 learners; unique IDs 1..20 characters; labels 1..16 characters

inputs.name: days
inputs.description: Authored daily attendance, played in array order with no inferred interpolation between days.
inputs.constraints: 2..3 days; unique IDs 1..20 characters; day labels 1..16 characters; each day must contain exactly one record for every learner ID; the roster is unchanged

inputs.name: labels
inputs.description: Visible legend and denominator wording.
inputs.constraints: Each label 1..18 characters

inputs.name: deskLayout
inputs.description: The physical classroom arrangement, without changing learner IDs or attendance.
inputs.constraints: One of the declared values

inputs.name: showDayImpressions
inputs.description: Keep small previous-day marks at each desk so the viewer can compare the same learner across days.
inputs.constraints: boolean; marks use both shape and legend labels

inputs.name: caption
inputs.description: Persistent context identifying the example.
inputs.constraints: 1..48 characters

bindingExample.shortSourceText: In a fictional class of six learners, four are present on Day A, five on Day B, and four on Day C; one Day C record is unknown.

distinction: Uses persistent desks and occupied space across school days, rather than a dot matrix or a cohort flowing through dose-return lanes. The explanatory change is daily room occupancy, with absent and unknown records retained as separate states.
limits: Each silhouette represents one roster member, not a sample weight.
Every daily present numerator is divided by the full supplied roster length. Absent and unknown counts are shown separately and all three states sum to that denominator.
Unknown does not mean absent. The animation never infers reasons for absence, dropout, retention, or educational impact.
The three day changes are editorial beats, not proportional elapsed time. All defaults are fictional.
verificationFocus: Each day classifies the same learner roster into present, absent or unknown; totals equal roster size and an unknown day is never treated as absent.

title: Unpack the cost of attending
description: A school satchel opens to reveal the different expenses a fictional household is asked to plan for over one stated period. The costs stay attached to recognizable school objects.
creativeDirection: Begin with a learner beside an open school doorway carrying a closed satchel. Open the bag and unfold exactly the object kinds supplied in the expense array, ordered by unpackOrder onto a small ground cloth. Each object reveals its authored amount; a bracket gathers their amounts into a clearly labeled total for the stated period. Hold the objects, period, and total together, then close the scene through the shared exit envelope.
goodFor: Introduce financial barriers beyond a tuition headline
Explain what is included in a fictional school-access budget
Separate a named expense from the total household cost being discussed
intent: Make the components of an attendance-related expense visible without claiming affordability or exclusion.

inputs.name: expenses
inputs.description: The expense objects unpacked from the bag. Their amounts are the only source of the displayed total.
inputs.constraints: 2..5 entries; unique IDs 1..20 characters identify distinct authored costs; labels 1..22 characters; amounts integers 0..20; sum must be positive. Each ID is summed once. Equal labels, object kinds and amounts under distinct IDs are accepted. Preventing the same real-world cost from being supplied under multiple IDs is an authoring responsibility, not tuple deduplication.

inputs.name: periodLabel
inputs.description: The common accounting window for every expense.
inputs.constraints: 1..32 characters; all supplied amounts must already refer to this same period

inputs.name: unitLabel
inputs.description: The fictional currency or other authored common monetary unit.
inputs.constraints: 1..18 characters; one unit for all amounts; no exchange-rate conversion

inputs.name: sceneLabels
inputs.description: Visible person, building, and total labels.
inputs.constraints: Each label 1..24 characters

inputs.name: showExpenseShares
inputs.description: Show each expense amount over the sum of listed expenses, using the same unit as the total.
inputs.constraints: boolean; share denominator is the derived sum, never a separately entered budget

inputs.name: unpackOrder
inputs.description: Choose the order in which cost objects leave the bag.
inputs.constraints: One of the declared values; equal amounts preserve input order

inputs.name: caption
inputs.default: Fictional costs, not an affordability test
inputs.description: Context for the illustrative expense breakdown.
inputs.constraints: 1..56 characters

bindingExample.shortSourceText: A fictional household plans three example credits for a workbook, two for transport, and one for school clothing over the same term.

inputBindings.caption: Fictional costs, not an affordability test

distinction: The satchel physically reveals the objects behind a school-cost total. It does not show a purchasing choice, generic bar comparison, money gate, or an access intervention automatically succeeding.
limits: The total is the sum of the expense amounts. In the default, workbook cost is 3 of 6 example credits, not 3 of 6 learners.
The bag and objects are semantic illustrations. Their sizes do not encode price, weight, deprivation, or a household income share.
The open doorway does not imply enrollment is conditional on payment. No admission, dropout, affordability, or causal impact is inferred.
Amounts require a common period and unit. The animation does not annualize one-off costs or estimate missing expenses. Defaults are fictional.

Distinct IDs denote distinct authored costs. These fields cannot detect one real-world expense entered under multiple IDs; the author must prevent that duplication. Equal label, kind and amount tuples remain valid under different IDs.
verificationFocus: The total equals every supplied expense in the same unit and period; shares use that total and no hidden recurring cost is multiplied without an authored frequency.

title: Return with earlier work intact
description: A learner returns to a classroom with earlier work still visible while a teacher adds an explicitly chosen return activity. A break in schooling is shown as time away, not as erased knowledge.
creativeDirection: Reveal one learner at a classroom desk with the supplied prior-work samples, preserving their authored forms and marks without grading them. Move the learner and the same portfolio to a side table while the interruption-period label appears. Bring the learner back to the desk, where the teacher places exactly the supplied return activities. Link each review activity to its referenced prior work and show each new activity without inventing a prior artifact. Hold the original work and supplied activities together, then fade out.
goodFor: Explain a fictional return-to-school support arrangement
Show that time away and retained prior work are different facts
Introduce an authored bridge lesson without predicting learning recovery
intent: Present reentry as building from known prior work rather than restarting a learner from zero.

inputs.name: people
inputs.description: Names for the two participants in the fictional return session.
inputs.constraints: Each label 1..20 characters

inputs.name: periodLabels
inputs.description: The three ordered time labels. They carry no implicit duration or cause.
inputs.constraints: Each label 1..24 characters

inputs.name: priorWork
inputs.description: Persistent artifacts carried through every scene beat. Their content is schematic and is never scored.
inputs.constraints: 1..3 items; unique IDs 1..20 characters; labels 1..24 characters

inputs.name: returnActivities
inputs.description: The teacher-authored activities placed beside the retained work at return.
inputs.constraints: 1..3 activities; unique IDs 1..20 characters; labels 1..28 characters; review references an existing priorWork ID; new uses an empty priorWorkId; activity kind does not encode ability or grade

inputs.name: activityLabels
inputs.description: Labels for the distinct purposes of the visible materials.
inputs.constraints: Each label 1..24 characters

inputs.name: showPortfolioTrail
inputs.description: Keep a subtle persistent outline of the same portfolio during the move away and back.
inputs.constraints: boolean; no duplicate learner or work-sample counts

inputs.name: caption
inputs.description: Persistent illustrative context.
inputs.constraints: 1..48 characters

bindingExample.shortSourceText: In a fictional return session, Learner A brings earlier shape and number work, revisits one familiar activity with a teacher, and tries one new activity.

distinction: A learner carries tangible prior work through a discontinuity and joins a physical teaching session. Unlike missed-visit followup or restoring a software checkpoint, nothing is retrieved by an alert and no human knowledge is rolled back or automatically recovered.
limits: One learner is represented. Work samples count artifacts only, not mastered competencies, credits, or school days.
The middle beat does not specify why schooling was interrupted, where the learner lived, or what learning happened while away.
Review and new are authored activity roles, not diagnostic judgments. A return scene does not prove reenrollment or learning recovery.
All defaults are fictional. Durations are editorial and the loop reset is not another interruption.
verificationFocus: Previously supplied work survives the interruption and return; the added review/new activity does not overwrite that portfolio or imply measured attainment.

title: One fraction, several ways to show it
description: Learners demonstrate the same fictional lesson using folded paper, counters, and a shaded board. The objects change while the mathematical relationship stays constant.
creativeDirection: Reveal one learner and work surface per supplied representation facing a shared fraction prompt. Animate only the chosen materials: folded paper divides into equal parts, counters gather into equal units, and shaded-board cells select their authored fraction. Every representation selects the same numerator out of the same denominator. Briefly align corresponding selected parts without merging or ranking learners. Hold the supplied representations and common fraction, then use the shared fade.
goodFor: Explain differentiated materials for a common lesson goal
Introduce equivalent concrete representations of a fraction
Show a teacher offering more than one way to demonstrate an idea
intent: Show that one mathematical idea can be expressed through different physical representations.

inputs.name: fraction
inputs.description: The common exact fraction represented by each material.
inputs.constraints: Integer denominator 2..8; integer numerator 1..denominator; every representation must use this same fraction

inputs.name: representations
inputs.description: Learners and their chosen visible representations. One entry owns one learner and one material.
inputs.constraints: 2..3 entries; unique IDs 1..20 characters; unique material values; learner labels 1..16 characters; material labels 1..22 characters

inputs.name: lessonLabel
inputs.description: The shared lesson prompt above the learning surfaces.
inputs.constraints: 1..36 characters

inputs.name: showFractionNotation
inputs.description: Display the exact numerator and denominator next to each material and the shared prompt.
inputs.constraints: boolean; notation must use fraction values, never independent text numbers

inputs.name: resolvedArrangement
inputs.description: Keep materials at their desks or bring only their work surfaces into a shared comparison at the hold.
inputs.constraints: One of the declared values; learners and artifacts remain distinct

inputs.name: caption
inputs.description: Context for the example lesson.
inputs.constraints: 1..56 characters

bindingExample.shortSourceText: In a fictional lesson, three learners each show one half: one folds paper, one selects a counter from a pair, and one shades a cell out of two.

distinction: Each material undergoes a different physical operation that preserves an exact mathematical relationship. This is neither relabeled comparison cards nor a branching workflow that sorts learners into fixed ability tracks.
limits: Numerator means selected equal parts and denominator means all equal parts of that representation. The default is 1 of 2 in each material, not 3 of 6 learners.
Counter groups and board partitions are generated from the fraction denominator. No independent part-count input can contradict it.
Representation choices do not diagnose learning styles or prove superior learning outcomes. The sequence does not rank learners.
This bounded preset explains fractions only. Every example classroom, learner, and lesson is fictional.
verificationFocus: Every physical representation selects exactly the same numerator from the same denominator; changing a representation never changes the fraction.

title: Make room for teacher learning
description: A colleague covers a fictional class while its teacher works with a mentor nearby, then the teacher returns. The classroom remains visibly attended throughout the handoff.
creativeDirection: Open on one teacher and a fixed group of learners in a classroom with a small adjacent planning alcove. A covering colleague arrives before the teacher moves to the mentor; the two adults rehearse a prompt with a small teaching board while the colleague stays with the class. Return the teacher before the colleague leaves. Hold the class and the retained prompt together, then fade out.
goodFor: Explain scheduled cover that enables teacher development
Describe a fictional mentoring or rehearsal session
Show the people needed to keep a class attended during teacher support
intent: Show that a teacher support session requires an explicit classroom cover arrangement.

inputs.name: staff
inputs.description: The three distinct adults and their fixed roles in this example.
inputs.constraints: Exactly three distinct IDs 1..20 characters; labels 1..20 characters; no role doubles as another role during the same beat

inputs.name: learners
inputs.description: The same represented learners remain in the classroom during the support session.
inputs.constraints: 2..6 entries; unique IDs 1..20 characters; labels 1..16 characters

inputs.name: session
inputs.description: The authored teacher-support activity and visible prompt.
inputs.constraints: Label 1..24 characters; prompt 1..40 characters; mode determines a short board rehearsal or shared planning gesture

inputs.name: roomLabels
inputs.description: The two schematic physical locations.
inputs.constraints: Each label 1..24 characters

inputs.name: phaseLabels
inputs.description: Labels attached to the three authored handoff beats.
inputs.constraints: Each label 1..24 characters

inputs.name: showClassroomResponsibility
inputs.description: Keep a short bracket between the adult currently attending the class and its learner area.
inputs.constraints: boolean; bracket changes only after the arriving adult is in place

inputs.name: caption
inputs.description: Illustrative context for the example.
inputs.constraints: 1..48 characters

bindingExample.shortSourceText: A fictional school asks Colleague B to cover four learners while Teacher A rehearses an open question with Mentor C, then Teacher A returns.

distinction: The explanatory motion is adult coverage across two real learning spaces, with overlap at both handoffs. It is not a generic custody transfer, approval gate, or claim that a coaching session produces an educational improvement.
limits: Learner count is the learners array length; the three staff roles are separate adults and are never part of that denominator.
This is a staged staffing arrangement, not a recommended supervision ratio, a timetable optimizer, or evidence of professional-development impact.
The nearby alcove is schematic. Distance and transition duration do not claim physical proximity or actual session length.
Default participants, activity, and class are fictional.
verificationFocus: The covering colleague is in the classroom before the teacher leaves and remains until the teacher returns; learner count stays constant.

title: Bring the readers around the books
description: A fixed set of books moves from a classroom shelf to small reading circles. Learners gather around the same open pages, making the sharing arrangement visible without creating additional copies.
creativeDirection: Reveal the supplied books on a shelf and the learners at separate seats. Carry each book to its assigned shared table as seats pivot into the authored reading circles, preserving every learner identity. Open the books and turn one page within each circle. Hold reader counts against the class roster with the book inventory unchanged, then fade.
goodFor: Explain how existing classroom books are shared
Show reading-group organization around a limited material set
Distinguish the number of books from the number of learners using them
intent: Make a specific book-sharing arrangement concrete while preserving the material inventory.

inputs.name: learners
inputs.description: The full represented class, with stable identities as seats move.
inputs.constraints: 2..8 entries; unique IDs 1..20 characters; labels 1..16 characters

inputs.name: books
inputs.description: Physical book copies. Each entry appears once on the shelf and once at its assigned table.
inputs.constraints: 1..4 books; unique IDs 1..20 characters; labels 1..22 characters; page labels 1..28 characters; book count cannot exceed learner count

inputs.name: readingGroups
inputs.description: The explicit reader allocation for each physical book.
inputs.constraints: Exactly one group per book ID; 1..4 learner IDs per group; every learner ID occurs exactly once across all groups; no unknown IDs

inputs.name: startingShelf
inputs.description: The shelf position from which the existing copies move.
inputs.constraints: One of the declared values; no change to inventory or group membership

inputs.name: labels
inputs.description: Visible inventory and reader-denominator labels.
inputs.constraints: Each label 1..26 characters

inputs.name: showGroupCounts
inputs.description: Show each group size over the full learner array length and the separate physical book inventory.
inputs.constraints: boolean; counts derive only from supplied arrays

inputs.name: caption
inputs.description: Context identifying the illustrative sharing arrangement.
inputs.constraints: 1..48 characters

bindingExample.shortSourceText: In a fictional class of six learners, two existing story books are shared at two tables with three readers around each book.

distinction: Physical seats reorganize around a conserved set of open books and a shared page turn. This explains simultaneous access to one object, unlike shelf replenishment, source merging, or relabeling a collection of cards.
limits: One books entry is one physical copy. A page turn never creates another copy, and the inventory is constant across the animation.
Each learner belongs to one shown reading group. The default group count is 3 of 6 represented learners per book, while the class inventory is 2 books for 6 learners.
Grouping does not establish that all learners can see, read, or benefit from the material. The arrangement is not an adequacy threshold or an access-impact claim.
All books, passages, and learners are fictional schematic examples.
verificationFocus: Each book is assigned once, each learner belongs to one supplied reading group, and the final shelf/table inventory equals the initial books.

title: What reaches the lunch table
description: School lunch trays are assembled from an explicit list of planned components, with an unfilled component kept visible. The scene distinguishes a tray being served from a tray matching the stated plan.
creativeDirection: Reveal the supplied learners at a lunch table with their outlined planned trays. Serving utensils place only the authored components into the matching compartments; missing planned components retain their outlines. Bring trays to their places and hold the complete-plan numerator against every planned tray without marking a learner as deficient. Fade through the shared opaque ground.
goodFor: Explain the composition of a fictional school meal plan
Show a missing meal component without claiming nutritional adequacy
Distinguish meals planned, trays represented, and complete listed component sets
intent: Make the contents and omissions of a stated school meal plan visible.
family: Meal assembly at a learning setting

inputs.name: learners
inputs.description: The represented learners, each with one planned tray in this meal occasion.
inputs.constraints: 2..6 entries; unique IDs 1..20 characters; labels 1..16 characters

inputs.name: plannedComponents
inputs.description: The explicit component list required to count a tray as matching this authored plan.
inputs.constraints: 2..4 components; unique IDs 1..20 characters; labels 1..20 characters; symbols identify component type only, not a portion or nutrient amount

inputs.name: trays
inputs.description: The listed components placed on each learner's one planned tray.
inputs.constraints: Exactly one tray per learner ID; component IDs are a unique subset of plannedComponents IDs; empty subsets allowed; no unknown IDs or extra trays

inputs.name: labels
inputs.description: Visible labels for the meal occasion, tray-count numerator and denominator, and unfilled compartments.
inputs.constraints: Each label 1..26 characters

inputs.name: showComponentNames
inputs.description: Label the serving sources and the component outlines.
inputs.constraints: boolean; a legend with component names remains visible when direct labels are hidden

inputs.name: emphasizeMissingComponents
inputs.description: Use a short neutral outline emphasis on unfilled planned compartments.
inputs.constraints: boolean; no moral, medical, or learner-performance scoring

inputs.name: caption
inputs.default: Fictional meal plan, not nutrition guidance
inputs.description: Context for the illustrative meal composition.
inputs.constraints: 1..56 characters

bindingExample.shortSourceText: In a fictional school lunch for four learners, three of four planned trays contain grain, beans, and fruit; the fourth contains grain and beans.

inputBindings.caption: Fictional meal plan, not nutrition guidance

distinction: The hero action assembles physical meal components into separate tray compartments and preserves a planned-but-unfilled compartment. It is not a generic delivery handoff, shopping basket choice, or a population counter.
limits: The complete-plan numerator counts trays containing every supplied planned component. Its denominator is all trays, which is also the learner array length in this single meal occasion.
A component symbol means the component is listed as present. Its area does not encode calories, portion size, nutrient content, or actual consumption.
Matching the list does not establish a balanced diet, nutritional sufficiency, health improvement, or learning impact. Missing a component does not describe a learner's health.
The example covers one fictional meal occasion and cannot represent repeated meals or unique reach across days.
verificationFocus: Only supplied served components fill tray compartments; the complete-plan numerator counts trays with all planned components over all planned trays without assigning blame to learners.

title: Make space in the same classroom
description: A classroom rearranges its furniture and shared teaching surface so named learners can approach and participate in the same group. The room changes while the people remain themselves.
creativeDirection: Reveal a crowded row arrangement with the same learners waiting at its edge. Pull desks apart to make a clear schematic approach, rotate the shared table toward the group, and reveal the selected teaching-surface adaptations. Move every learner into the common activity space; retain the selected access cues during the hold. Do not transform bodies or separate one learner into a distant special zone. Fade out.
goodFor: Explain removal of a physical classroom participation barrier
Introduce a fictional room adaptation and a shared teaching activity
Show inclusive participation as an environmental design choice
intent: Show that changing the learning environment can address a stated participation barrier.

inputs.name: learners
inputs.description: The same represented learners before and after rearrangement. A mobility icon is an authored visual choice, not an inferred diagnosis.
inputs.constraints: 2..6 entries; unique IDs 1..20 characters; labels 1..16 characters; icons persist unchanged across all beats

inputs.name: adaptations
inputs.description: The explicitly selected environmental changes and their callout labels.
inputs.constraints: 1..3 entries; unique IDs 1..20 characters; unique kinds; labels 1..28 characters; clear-approach is required for a crowded-row opening; table and board changes are shown only when selected

inputs.name: activity
inputs.description: The common activity and teaching-surface text, available to the entire represented group.
inputs.constraints: Label 1..28 characters; board text 1..36 characters; no diagnostic or ability labels

inputs.name: resolvedLayout
inputs.description: The final common arrangement around the selected teaching surface.
inputs.constraints: One of the declared values; every learner remains inside the common activity area

inputs.name: showApproachTrace
inputs.description: Reveal a brief line through the newly cleared floor area to the common activity.
inputs.constraints: boolean; schematic path only, with no measurements or accessibility certification

inputs.name: phaseLabels
inputs.description: The two spatial arrangement labels.
inputs.constraints: Each label 1..28 characters

inputs.name: caption
inputs.description: Context preventing the room sketch from being read as a compliant building plan.
inputs.constraints: 1..56 characters

bindingExample.shortSourceText: A fictional classroom clears an approach, opens a shared table, and enlarges the example board text so four represented learners join the same shape activity.

distinction: Furniture and instructional surfaces physically change within one shared classroom while learner identities remain constant. Unlike a generic service-access gate, the scene explains the geometry and materials of participation rather than admission or referral.
limits: The learner array is the complete represented group. All are shown at the final activity; this is an authored staging choice, not an enrollment or inclusion rate.
No dimensions, turning-radius compliance, visual-acuity threshold, building standard, or universal accessibility claim is encoded.
A wheeled icon does not imply a diagnosis, dependence, or inability to learn. Adaptations alter the environment rather than a person.
The fictional schematic cannot establish that the selected changes meet any real learner's complete access requirements.
verificationFocus: The same learners join the common activity after furniture and surface adaptations; no person disappears or moves into a separate excluded zone.

title: Try the learned action in a new setting
description: A learner repeats an authored measuring-and-marking action first on a practice sheet and then on a workshop material. Both artifacts remain visible so the connection is concrete without implying a job outcome.
creativeDirection: Show one learner using a ruler to place a labeled measurement on a practice sheet at a classroom desk. Slide the surrounding furniture into a simple workshop arrangement while retaining the learner and the first marked sheet at the side. Repeat the same ruler placement and marking gesture on the chosen work material, then hold the two measured artifacts together. Fade to the shared background.
goodFor: Explain a school-to-practice skills transition
Show how one classroom action is tried on a work sample
Introduce hands-on vocational learning without promising employment
intent: Connect a specific practiced action to an application in a different physical setting.

inputs.name: learnerLabel
inputs.description: The persistent learner identity through both settings.
inputs.constraints: 1..20 characters

inputs.name: settingLabels
inputs.description: Labels for the two schematic environments.
inputs.constraints: Each label 1..26 characters

inputs.name: task
inputs.description: The shared authored measurement repeated on both artifacts.
inputs.constraints: Instruction 1..28 characters; value integer 1..10; unit 1..8 characters; the same value and unit appear on both artifacts; no conversion

inputs.name: workpieces
inputs.description: Labels and the target material whose visual surface changes between settings.
inputs.constraints: Each label 1..24 characters; material is one of the declared values; practice surface remains a sheet

inputs.name: showAlignmentGuides
inputs.description: Show the ruler zero point and the authored endpoint during each marking gesture.
inputs.constraints: boolean; guides derive from the same task value and a normalized diagram scale

inputs.name: showFirstArtifactAtHold
inputs.description: Retain the practice sheet next to the final application sample for visual correspondence.
inputs.constraints: boolean; retaining the sheet does not create a second learner or another completed qualification

inputs.name: caption
inputs.default: Fictional practice, not an employment outcome
inputs.description: Context for the staged skills example.
inputs.constraints: 1..56 characters

bindingExample.shortSourceText: In a fictional exercise, Learner A practices marking four centimeters on paper and then tries the same measuring action on a wooden workshop sample.

inputBindings.caption: Fictional practice, not an employment outcome

distinction: The same physical gesture is performed on different materials as the surrounding learning environment changes. Unlike field mapping or a sequence of workflow stages, the connection is demonstrated through tool use and preserved artifacts.
limits: One learner performs two authored attempts. Two artifacts are not two graduates, two skills certifications, or two employment outcomes.
The numeric label is an illustrative target measurement. SVG length is a normalized diagram representation, not a usable real-world measuring instrument.
Repeating a gesture does not prove competence, retention, successful transfer, workplace readiness, or a job placement.
This bounded motif supports measuring and marking only. Participants, materials, and setting names are fictional defaults.
verificationFocus: The same supplied measurement appears in both practice and work artifacts; transferring the setting does not imply qualification or change the measured value.

title: Predict together, then observe
description: Learners place separate predictions along a shared tabletop track before an experiment reveals one authored observation. Their different expectations remain visible beside the result.
creativeDirection: Reveal a tabletop ramp and a labeled distance track with the supplied learners around it. Each learner places a distinct labeled prediction flag before a single ball is released. The ball travels to the supplied observation position and stops; retain every prediction without scoring or ranking learners. Hold the observed marker and predicted positions together, then fade out before resetting.
goodFor: Introduce participatory learning through a shared experiment
Distinguish predictions from observations
Show different ideas being tested against the same authored demonstration
intent: Separate what participants expect from what is recorded in a shared demonstration.

inputs.name: learners
inputs.description: The participants and their explicitly authored prediction positions.
inputs.constraints: 2..4 entries; unique IDs 1..20 characters; labels 1..16 characters; finite predictionDistance values 0..track.maximum; coincident predictions stack labels without merging learners

inputs.name: observationDistance
inputs.description: The authored observed stopping position of the demonstration ball.
inputs.constraints: Finite number 0..track.maximum; interpreted in track.unit; supplied by the author, not computed from physical parameters

inputs.name: track
inputs.description: The common distance axis from a visible zero origin.
inputs.constraints: Maximum integer 10..100; unit 1..14 characters; all prediction and observation values use this unit and must fit the axis

inputs.name: labels
inputs.description: Visible experiment and marker roles.
inputs.constraints: Experiment label 1..32 characters; other labels 1..24 characters

inputs.name: showDistanceDifferences
inputs.description: Optionally bracket the absolute distance between each prediction and the observation, using the same axis unit.
inputs.constraints: boolean; differences are derived absolute distances, not scores, probabilities, or percentages

inputs.name: showPredictionValues
inputs.description: Display the authored numeric value beside each participant's prediction flag.
inputs.constraints: boolean; participant labels and the distinction between prediction and observation remain visible

inputs.name: caption
inputs.description: Context stating that the experiment result is supplied example content.
inputs.constraints: 1..56 characters

bindingExample.shortSourceText: In a fictional tabletop exercise, three learners predict stopping distances of 12, 20, and 28 example centimeters, then compare them with an authored observation of 18.

distinction: Participants physically commit separate predictions before one common test, and the final frame preserves disagreement alongside the observation. This differs from source merging, network signals, shared-fabric contributions, or a generic feedback revision loop.
limits: Each learner contributes exactly one prediction. The number of predictions equals the learner array length and is not a sample of measured scientific accuracy.
Distances use a shared zero and unit. Optional differences are absolute distances with the same unit; no denominator or success rate is implied.
The ball trajectory is illustrative motion toward an authored stopping point. It is not a physics simulation, measured experiment, or validation of a real hypothesis.
No learner is ranked or labeled correct by proximity. The fictional scene shows participation and comparison, not learning efficacy.
verificationFocus: All predictions appear before the observation and remain afterward; the ball stops at the supplied observed position without moving a prediction to match it.

title: Count where the layers meet
description: Two schematic geographic layers settle onto the same coordinate plane. Their intersection or difference isolates the supplied population records that satisfy the chosen spatial rule.
creativeDirection: Begin with offset translucent map sheets and stationary household markers. Register the sheets, hatch the resulting geometry, then lift only qualifying markers into a counting bracket while retaining their map positions. Hold the selected quantity over the full supplied denominator.
goodFor: Explain a GIS intersection query
Identify households inside two authored planning zones
Separate mapped exposure overlap from a health outcome
intent: Show how an explicit geometric rule selects records without establishing a causal relationship.

inputs.name: layers
inputs.description: The two schematic surfaces being combined.
inputs.constraints: Exactly 2 layers; unique IDs <= 12 characters; labels <= 28 characters; 3..8 vertices per simple polygon; coordinates 0..100.

inputs.name: households
inputs.description: Unique household locations and their supplied member counts.
inputs.constraints: 2..12 records; unique IDs <= 12 characters; labels <= 20 characters; coordinates 0..100; members integer 1..8; no location on a polygon boundary.

inputs.name: operation
inputs.description: Select locations in both layers or only in the first layer.
inputs.constraints: One listed value; layer array order defines first and second.

inputs.name: measure
inputs.description: Count unique household records or sum their supplied members.
inputs.constraints: One listed value; denominator uses all supplied households under the same measure.

inputs.name: copy
inputs.description: Visible geography qualifier, operation names, quantity labels and units.
inputs.constraints: All fields required; each <= 40 characters; context must identify fictional schematic geography.

inputs.name: showLayerOutlines
inputs.description: Retain original layer outlines during the result hold.
inputs.constraints: Boolean; result boundary and denominator remain visible.

bindingExample.shortSourceText: In the fictional overlay, three of eight supplied residents live inside both demo zones.

distinction: The hero transformation registers two geometric sheets and computes a spatial set before tallying records. It is neither field correspondence, a scope aperture, a cloud observation mask, nor a routing animation.
limits: Defaults represent fictional local geometry, not real exposure or epidemiological evidence.
Only supplied point locations are classified; household members share that location by explicit input convention.
Selected members divided by all supplied members is a record-based share, not population prevalence or an area-weighted estimate.
verificationFocus: For the default geometry, intersection selects one household and three members out of four households and eight members. Difference selects Home A only. Changing the measure changes counts without changing selected identities.

title: Coverage without counting twice
description: Authored service catchments join into one footprint around a fixed set of households. Overlap loses its duplicate shading while households outside every catchment remain visible as gaps.
creativeDirection: Draw the separate catchment outlines around stationary homes. Where catchments overlap, peel away the second tint and fuse the outer boundary. Finish with covered homes enclosed and uncovered homes ringed, alongside one unique covered share.
goodFor: Explain service catchment union
Show coverage gaps in a planning dataset
Prevent double counting overlapping service footprints
intent: Explain why overlapping service areas do not create additional people served.

inputs.name: catchments
inputs.description: Supplied coverage polygons, with no routing or travel-time calculation.
inputs.constraints: 1..4 catchments; unique IDs <= 12 characters; labels <= 28 characters; 3..8 vertices per simple polygon; coordinates 0..100.

inputs.name: households
inputs.description: The complete illustrated household denominator.
inputs.constraints: 2..12 unique households; IDs <= 12 characters; labels <= 20 characters; coordinates 0..100; members integer 1..8; no point on a catchment boundary.

inputs.name: measure
inputs.description: Choose the unit for the covered and uncovered shares.
inputs.constraints: One listed value; count each household once even inside several polygons.

inputs.name: gapEmphasis
inputs.description: How uncovered household markers receive final emphasis.
inputs.constraints: One listed value; do not shade unsupplied populations as known gaps.

inputs.name: copy
inputs.description: Visible labels and unit names.
inputs.constraints: All fields required; each <= 40 characters; context must identify fictional schematic geography.

inputs.name: showOriginalOutlines
inputs.description: Keep individual catchment edges after the union forms.
inputs.constraints: Boolean; the union and uncovered records remain visible.

bindingExample.shortSourceText: The fictional services cover three of four supplied households, including one household inside both footprints.

distinction: A geometric union removes overlapping coverage while preserving uncovered locations. Unlike household revisits, the duplicate comes from simultaneous polygon membership; unlike mobile-clinic relocation, no service or person travels.
limits: Catchments are authored schematic footprints, not inferred travel-time areas or proof of actual service use.
Covered plus uncovered equals the complete supplied denominator. Empty map space is not evidence of absent population.
No facility capacity, service quality, physical accessibility, or health outcome is inferred.
verificationFocus: The default union covers three of four homes and six of eight members, counting the overlapping home once. Removing a catchment recomputes the union and gaps without duplicating or deleting household records.

title: Locate the cluster in time
description: A supplied investigation group on a schematic map is linked to its recorded onset bins in an epidemic curve. The same selected case IDs remain highlighted in both views, including an explicit unknown-time compartment.
creativeDirection: Begin with all case pins and a complete histogram. An authored group receives a map bracket; thin identity guides lift its highlighted tokens into the corresponding histogram segments. A chosen time bin then outlines its matching map pins. Hold both views with selected and total case counts.
goodFor: Explain outbreak investigation cross-filtering
Relate a spatial case group to recorded onset time
Keep unknown onset dates visible during case review
intent: Connect place and recorded time for the same cases without inventing transmission links.

inputs.name: cases
inputs.description: One fictional case per marker and histogram unit.
inputs.constraints: 3..12 cases; unique IDs <= 12 characters; labels <= 20 characters; coordinates 0..100; onsetBinId references a time bin or is null.

inputs.name: timeBins
inputs.description: Ordered, equal-duration onset bins.
inputs.constraints: 3..6 bins in chronological order; unique IDs <= 12 characters; labels <= 16 characters; no independent bar counts.

inputs.name: investigationCaseIds
inputs.description: The explicitly authored investigation group, not a detected statistical cluster.
inputs.constraints: 1..8 unique IDs, all present in cases.

inputs.name: focusedBinId
inputs.description: Time bin whose cases receive the return highlight on the map.
inputs.constraints: Existing time-bin ID or null to omit the return highlight.

inputs.name: copy
inputs.description: All view titles, count labels and the unknown-time label.
inputs.constraints: All fields required; each <= 44 characters; context must identify fictional data and schematic geography.

inputs.name: showIdentityGuides
inputs.description: Show temporary guides between the two representations of a case.
inputs.constraints: Boolean; guides connect a case to its histogram position only, never case to case.

bindingExample.shortSourceText: Review three fictional nearby cases against the onset curve; one has no recorded onset day.

distinction: The same case identities drive a geographic selection and a binned epidemic curve. Unlike contact-window-overlap, no venue intervals intersect; unlike line-trace, the explanation is linked selection between two complete representations.
limits: The investigation group is supplied, not statistically detected. Proximity and timing do not establish a common source or transmission.
Histogram bars plus unknown-time cases equal the entire case array; highlights are subsets, not extra cases.
Counts describe supplied case records only. No population denominator, disease incidence, or clinical guidance is implied.
verificationFocus: The default investigation group contains three cases, including one unknown onset. Each case maps to exactly one histogram bin or the unknown compartment. Focusing a time bin highlights precisely its case IDs on the map.

title: Choose sites across the whole frame
description: A schematic sampling frame separates into named geographic strata. Authored sampling sites lift from each stratum while unsampled eligible sites remain visible underneath.
creativeDirection: Open on a complete field of eligible site markers. Thin boundaries divide the frame into supplied strata, then selected markers rise onto short sampling stems without leaving their coordinates. Hold each stratum's selected count over its eligible-site denominator.
goodFor: Explain a spatial sampling plan
Show selected versus eligible sites by stratum
Introduce field survey allocation without claiming representativeness
intent: Make the supplied selection and its geographic sampling frame visible together.

inputs.name: strata
inputs.description: Non-overlapping schematic sampling strata.
inputs.constraints: 2..4 strata; unique IDs <= 12 characters; labels <= 24 characters; 3..8 vertices per simple polygon; coordinates 0..100; interiors do not overlap.

inputs.name: sites
inputs.description: The complete illustrated eligible-site frame.
inputs.constraints: 4..12 unique sites; IDs <= 12 characters; labels <= 20 characters; stratumId must exist; coordinates strictly inside that stratum; every stratum has at least one site.

inputs.name: selectedSiteIds
inputs.description: Explicit sites selected for this plan.
inputs.constraints: 1..8 unique existing site IDs; selection may leave a stratum unsampled, which must remain visible.

inputs.name: copy
inputs.description: Visible qualifier, selection labels and counting unit.
inputs.constraints: All fields required; each <= 40 characters; context must identify a fictional schematic plan.

inputs.name: showUnselectedLabels
inputs.description: Show names as well as markers for unselected sites.
inputs.constraints: Boolean; unselected markers and denominators cannot be hidden.

bindingExample.shortSourceText: The fictional field plan selects one of three eligible western sites and one of two eastern sites.

distinction: The transformation is an explicit sample drawn from a retained, partitioned eligible frame. Unlike environmental-observation-gaps, it explains selection before observation and never adds measurements or fills missing geography.
limits: Selection is authored, not random. No sample weights, confidence intervals, or representativeness are calculated.
Each site counts once. Site fractions are not population fractions unless supplied through a different, explicit data contract.
Only schematic local geography is supported; boundaries do not describe real administrative areas.
verificationFocus: Default selected/eligible fractions are one of three in the west and one of two in the east. An authored empty selection in one stratum leaves its denominator and unsampled markers visible. Reject sites outside their referenced stratum.

title: Leave room around the site
description: Schematic parcels shrink inward by a supplied clearance distance to reveal their buildable envelopes. A chosen public-service structure seats inside one envelope with its surrounding space still visible.
creativeDirection: Start with parcel edges and dimension ticks. Slide an inner edge inward equally on every side, leaving the setback as a hatched perimeter band. Lower the authored structure footprint into the remaining envelope and hold the original parcel, clearance band and occupied footprint together.
goodFor: Explain geometric resource-siting constraints
Distinguish parcel area from a usable building envelope
Show an authored kiosk or service-post placement
intent: Show why the whole structure and its clearance must fit inside a site.

inputs.name: parcels
inputs.description: Rectangular parcels in a local schematic coordinate plane.
inputs.constraints: 1..3 parcels; unique IDs <= 12 characters; labels <= 20 characters; dimensions 5..80; non-overlapping rectangles fully inside 0..100.

inputs.name: setback
inputs.description: Uniform inward clearance in the same units as parcel geometry.
inputs.constraints: 0..15; collapse any exhausted envelope to an explicit empty result, never negative dimensions.

inputs.name: structure
inputs.description: The structure's complete rectangular ground footprint.
inputs.constraints: Label <= 28 characters; width and height 2..50; no rotation or automatic resizing.

inputs.name: placement
inputs.description: An authored placement inside the chosen parcel's inset envelope.
inputs.constraints: Existing parcelId; coordinates 0..100; the whole footprint must fit the inset envelope; invalid input must not render a successful placement.

inputs.name: copy
inputs.description: Visible geometric labels and coordinate unit.
inputs.constraints: All fields required; each <= 40 characters; context must identify fictional geometry rather than a planning standard.

inputs.name: showDimensions
inputs.description: Show parcel, inset and footprint dimension ticks.
inputs.constraints: Boolean; clearance band and original parcel outline remain visible.

bindingExample.shortSourceText: Fictional planners leave four schematic units around each plot before placing the service kiosk in Plot B.

distinction: The hero motion erodes parcel edges by a measured inset and fits an entire footprint. It neither relocates a service along a route nor exchanges rejected options; unlike layer intersection, the second geometry is derived from clearance rather than an independent map layer.
limits: This is rectangular schematic geometry, not a legal setback, construction recommendation, or optimized site choice.
Clearance is an authored illustration. Accessibility, utilities, terrain and operating capacity require separate evidence.
All dimensions share one coordinate unit; there is no implied geographic scale or population denominator.
verificationFocus: Inset every rectangular side by the supplied clearance. Default envelopes are 27 by 52 units. Reject a structure footprint extending beyond its chosen envelope; exhausted unchosen envelopes remain empty, never negative.

title: Put the denominator on the map
description: A fictional zone map changes from record counts to records per supplied population. Each zone exposes its numerator and denominator before its fill changes under the new labeled legend.
creativeDirection: Begin with count-colored polygons. Lift each polygon like a shallow lid to reveal a numerator-over-denominator fraction, then settle it with the recalculated population-normalized shade. Replace the legend explicitly and hold both raw fractions so the change remains accountable.
goodFor: Explain counts versus population-normalized measures
Discuss spatial inequity with explicit denominators
Prevent a large population from being mistaken for a high rate
intent: Show how population size changes the meaning of a mapped count.

inputs.name: zones
inputs.description: Stable zones with supplied record counts and population denominators.
inputs.constraints: 2..4 disjoint zones; unique IDs <= 12 characters; labels <= 24 characters; 3..8 simple-polygon vertices at 0..100; records integer 0..100; population integer 1..1000; records <= population for this unique-record contract.

inputs.name: rateBase
inputs.description: The population base used for records/population multiplied by this value.
inputs.constraints: 1, 10, 100 or 1000; use the same base for every zone.

inputs.name: colorDomains
inputs.description: Explicit zero-based color legend ranges before and after normalization.
inputs.constraints: Both > 0 and <= 100000; countMaximum covers every record count; normalizedMaximum covers every derived value; no clipping.

inputs.name: periodLabel
inputs.description: One common observation period retained across both maps.
inputs.constraints: 1..36 characters; no mismatched periods across zones.

inputs.name: copy
inputs.description: Visible measure names, geography qualifier and fraction labels.
inputs.constraints: All fields required; each <= 40 characters; normalized legend must make the changed measure explicit.

inputs.name: keepFractionsVisible
inputs.description: Retain each raw numerator and denominator in the resolved view.
inputs.constraints: Boolean; when false retain denominator labels beside each zone rather than hiding them entirely.

bindingExample.shortSourceText: Demo West has four records among forty residents; Demo East has three among ten, so their counts and population-normalized values tell different stories.

distinction: The polygon physically exposes its denominator before changing the mapped measure. Unlike chart-focus-edit, the numeric measure changes; unlike bar-race, no items reorder and both numerator and denominator remain inspectable.
limits: This displays arithmetic for supplied unique records, not disease incidence, individual risk, standardized rates, or causal inequity findings.
Population denominators must refer to the same geography, period and record universe. No uncertainty correction is inferred.
Separate labeled legends are mandatory because the two views use different units.
verificationFocus: Default raw counts are four and three; per-100 values are ten and thirty. Preserve both denominators while changing the legend and fill domain. Reject a domain that would clip a derived value.

title: Change the boundary, keep the people
description: The same small geographic cells regroup under two supplied zoning schemes. Zone totals and population-normalized values change while every underlying cell and the overall denominator stay fixed.
creativeDirection: Show the supplied fixed cells and the first grouping boundary. Lift only the outer grouping seams, redraw them in the second arrangement, and gather each zone's arithmetic along the new outline. Hold the unchanged underlying cell values and unchanged overall total beneath the new summaries.
goodFor: Explain sensitivity to aggregation boundaries
Compare reporting zones without implying population movement
Introduce the modifiable areal unit problem
intent: Show that a geographic summary can change when only the grouping boundaries change.

inputs.name: cells
inputs.description: Unchanging atomic geographic cells and their quantities.
inputs.constraints: 4..9 cells; unique IDs <= 12 characters and grid positions; labels <= 16 characters; row and column integers 0..2; records integer 0..100; population integer 1..1000; records <= population.

inputs.name: groupings
inputs.description: Two complete, mutually exclusive regroupings of the same cells.
inputs.constraints: Exactly 2 groupings; each has 2..3 contiguous zones; every cell appears exactly once per grouping; IDs <= 12 characters; all labels <= 24 characters.

inputs.name: measure
inputs.description: Display summed counts or the ratio of summed counts to summed populations.
inputs.constraints: One listed value; never average precomputed cell rates.

inputs.name: rateBase
inputs.description: The common multiplier for population-normalized summaries.
inputs.constraints: 1, 10, 100 or 1000; ignored for count display.

inputs.name: copy
inputs.description: Visible qualifier, unchanged-total caption and units.
inputs.constraints: All fields required; each <= 40 characters; context identifies fictional schematic geography.

inputs.name: showCellValues
inputs.description: Keep the underlying cell fractions visible after regrouping.
inputs.constraints: Boolean; the atomic cell boundaries and overall numerator/denominator always remain.

bindingExample.shortSourceText: With the same six fictional records and forty residents, west/east zones each show 15 per 100, while north/south zones show 20 and 10 per 100.

distinction: Only aggregation seams move; stable atomic cells produce different zone summaries. Unlike nested-drilldown-window, this replaces one complete partition with another rather than selecting a smaller subset.
limits: Square cells are schematic accounting units, not real neighborhoods.
Overall numerator and denominator must be identical across both groupings; no resident moves and no record is created.
The scene explains aggregation sensitivity, not individual risk, a preferred zoning plan, or a causal explanation for inequality.
verificationFocus: Both default partitions retain six records and forty residents. West/east per-100 summaries are fifteen/fifteen; north/south are twenty/ten. Derive rates from summed counts and populations rather than averaging cell rates.

title: New reports can change earlier days
description: A fictional surveillance histogram is updated between two reporting snapshots. Newly received records land in their earlier event-date bins instead of being added to the current day's event count.
creativeDirection: Begin with the histogram known at the first reporting snapshot. Advance the reporting-date tab while later receipts open above the chart; their tokens drop into the supplied earlier event bins. Hold the original bar outlines beneath the revised heights and retain both snapshot totals.
goodFor: Explain reporting delay and backfill
Distinguish event date from report date
Show why a historical surveillance count was revised
intent: Show that a later report can revise an earlier period without representing a new event today.

inputs.name: records
inputs.description: Unique records with an event bin and first visible reporting snapshot.
inputs.constraints: 3..12 records; unique IDs <= 12 characters; labels <= 20 characters; eventBinId exists; firstSnapshot is 0 or 1; at least one record per snapshot.

inputs.name: eventBins
inputs.description: Ordered equal-duration event-date bins; heights derive from records.
inputs.constraints: 3..5 bins; unique IDs <= 12 characters; labels <= 16 characters; every event predates its reporting snapshot.

inputs.name: snapshots
inputs.description: The two reporting cutoffs being compared.
inputs.constraints: Exactly 2 chronological snapshots; labels <= 32 characters; these are reporting cutoffs, not event-bin labels.

inputs.name: copy
inputs.description: Visible measure, snapshot and arrival labels.
inputs.constraints: All fields required; each <= 40 characters; context must identify fictional data.

inputs.name: showPriorOutline
inputs.description: Retain first-snapshot bar outlines inside revised bars.
inputs.constraints: Boolean; both snapshot totals and their cutoff labels always remain.

bindingExample.shortSourceText: Three reports received on fictional Day 5 revise the counts for Days 1 through 3; they are not three events on Day 5.

distinction: New records alter historical bins while reporting time advances independently. Unlike a trend trace or journal receipt, the hero action is retroactive event-date placement, not drawing a trend or acknowledging already stored records.
limits: Only supplied observations are shown. No nowcast, reporting completeness estimate, or unseen-event total is inferred.
Each record contributes once per snapshot after its first appearance; revised minus earlier total equals newly received records.
Histogram counts are record totals, not incidence rates. This does not assess an outbreak or offer medical guidance.
verificationFocus: Default first-snapshot bars are one, one, zero and revised bars are two, two, one. Each later record enters its event-date bin once. Revised minus initial total equals three newly received records.

title: A pin can straddle a boundary
description: A schematic location pin unfolds into its supplied positional-uncertainty footprint. A footprint spanning two districts remains unresolved for district assignment rather than being forced into the district under its center.
creativeDirection: Begin with district outlines and nominal location pins. Expand the focused pin into a translucent circle, letting its edge visibly cross the boundary. Lift the two possible district labels beside that footprint and move its accounting marker into an unresolved bracket. Hold definite and unresolved counts over all supplied records.
goodFor: Explain geocoding precision
Show boundary-sensitive location assignment
Keep ambiguous records out of false geographic certainty
intent: Show how uncertain position limits an otherwise simple geographic classification.

inputs.name: districts
inputs.description: Non-overlapping schematic assignment districts.
inputs.constraints: 2..4 districts; unique IDs <= 12 characters; labels <= 24 characters; 3..8 vertices per simple polygon; coordinates 0..100; interiors disjoint.

inputs.name: locations
inputs.description: Nominal locations and authored possible-position radii.
inputs.constraints: 2..6 records; unique IDs <= 12 characters; labels <= 20 characters; coordinates 0..100; radius 0..15; entire footprints inside map extent; radii are supplied bounds, not probability distributions.

inputs.name: focusedLocationId
inputs.description: The record whose uncertainty expansion receives the central explanation.
inputs.constraints: An existing location ID; all record footprints still participate in final assignment accounting.

inputs.name: copy
inputs.description: Visible uncertainty, assignment and denominator labels.
inputs.constraints: All fields required; each <= 40 characters; context identifies fictional schematic bounds.

inputs.name: showOtherFootprints
inputs.description: Display uncertainty circles for records other than the focused example.
inputs.constraints: Boolean; hiding their circles cannot change accounting or conceal unresolved markers.

bindingExample.shortSourceText: One of three fictional locations has a possible-position footprint crossing the west/east boundary, so its district assignment remains unresolved.

distinction: A point expands into a bounded possible-position area, changing the certainty of spatial membership. Unlike environmental-observation-gaps, evidence is present but imprecisely located; unlike a scope aperture, the uncertainty belongs to the record itself.
limits: A definite assignment requires the entire footprint strictly inside one district. Boundary-touching, crossing, or outside-district footprints remain unresolved.
No confidence level, probability, population exposure, or epidemiological relationship is inferred from a radius.
Definite plus unresolved records equal the location array length; ambiguous records are never counted once in each possible district.
verificationFocus: Default assignments are two definite and one unresolved. Crossing or touching a district boundary never yields a definite assignment, including a zero-radius pin on the boundary. The display toggle cannot alter accounting.

title: Capacity starts with usable floor area
description: A fictional shelter floor plan separates sleeping area from circulation, storage and closed space. Only the remaining area enters an explicitly authored area-per-place calculation, which is compared with registered people.
creativeDirection: Begin with one gross floor outline. Raise the non-sleeping tiles into shallow labeled cutaways, revealing the smaller sleeping-area footprint beneath. Unroll only that usable area into a measured strip, divide it by the supplied illustration benchmark, and hold the resulting place equivalents beside registered people and any shortfall.
goodFor: Explain gross versus usable shelter area
Make an area-only capacity assumption visible
Discuss displaced-population shelter planning without implying a safety standard
intent: Expose the space exclusions and assumed denominator behind an illustrative capacity figure.

inputs.name: floorTiles
inputs.description: Equal-area floor tiles with mutually exclusive uses.
inputs.constraints: 4..12 tiles; unique IDs <= 12 characters and grid positions; row integer 0..2; column integer 0..3; contiguous footprint; each tile has exactly one listed role.

inputs.name: areaPerTile
inputs.description: Area represented by each equal-sized tile.
inputs.constraints: 1..20, at most 2 decimal places; one common area unit for the whole scene.

inputs.name: illustrativeAreaPerPlace
inputs.description: Authored divisor for the area-only place-equivalent calculation.
inputs.constraints: 0.5..20, at most 2 decimal places; explicitly fictional, not a recommended minimum; capacity is floor(usable area / divisor).

inputs.name: registeredPeople
inputs.description: Supplied demand count compared with calculated place equivalents.
inputs.constraints: Integer 0..40; a single input owns this count; show shortfall max(people - equivalents, 0) and spare equivalents separately.

inputs.name: copy

default.context: Fictional area-only example, not a standard

inputs.description: All use labels, assumption labels and quantity units.
inputs.constraints: All fields required; each <= 48 characters; context must distinguish an illustration from a safety or shelter standard.

inputs.name: keepGrossOutline
inputs.description: Retain the original gross floor boundary around the cutaway.
inputs.constraints: Boolean; all excluded area quantities remain visible even if the outline is hidden.

bindingExample.shortSourceText: The fictional shelter has 24 square metres gross but 12 usable; its authored two-square-metre divisor gives six place equivalents against eight registered people.

copy.context: Fictional area-only example, not a standard

distinction: The hero action subtracts unusable floor geometry before dividing the remaining area by an explicit assumption. Unlike compute-capacity-consolidation, nothing is packed or migrated; unlike queue-relief, no service slots open or waiting people move.
limits: The floor plan is schematic and all default figures are fictional. The divisor is not a humanitarian, legal, health, or safety recommendation.
Sleeping, circulation, storage and closed areas must sum to gross area. Only sleeping tiles contribute to the illustrated numerator.
Area-only place equivalents are not operational shelter capacity; layout, safeguarding, access, household composition and other constraints are not modeled.
verificationFocus: Default gross area is 24, usable area is 12, place equivalents are six, and the demand shortfall is two. Excluded roles contribute zero sleeping area. Test zero usable tiles, spare equivalents and decimal divisors without double rounding.

title: Fit support around the person's week
description: A participant and caseworker arrange a support appointment around commitments the participant has already named. The participant moves the proposed appointment, while their existing commitments remain visible.
creativeDirection: Open on a tabletop weekly planner between two people, with existing commitments already occupying time cells. The worker places a proposed support appointment across an occupied cell; the participant lifts it into the explicitly agreed free cell. The worker follows the participant's placement with an agreement mark. Hold the unchanged commitments, moved appointment and participant's goal together before the shared exit envelope.
goodFor: Explaining a person-led case-planning meeting
Showing why caregiving commitments affect appointment design
Introducing an agreed support schedule without claiming attendance
intent: Show that support is scheduled around the person's stated commitments.
family: Human planning at a shared table

inputs.name: people
inputs.description: Name the two people at the planner.
inputs.constraints: Each label 1..24 characters; fictional defaults.

inputs.name: days
inputs.description: Set the visible planner columns.
inputs.constraints: 2..4 days; unique IDs <= 16 characters; labels <= 20 characters.

inputs.name: timeBands
inputs.description: Set the planner's discrete time bands.
inputs.constraints: 2..3 bands; unique IDs <= 16 characters; labels <= 16 characters; array order is display order.

inputs.name: commitments
inputs.description: Supply existing commitments and the appointment's authored move.
inputs.constraints: 2..5 commitments; unique IDs <= 16 characters; labels <= 22 characters; references must exist; exactly one support item; existing items retain positions; final cells cannot overlap. The support item must initially overlap an existing commitment, then move to a different, unoccupied agreed cell.

inputs.name: copy
inputs.description: Set the goal, agreement annotation and example label.
inputs.constraints: Goal <= 36 characters; other labels <= 30 characters.

inputs.name: showOriginalAppointment
inputs.description: Retain a dotted impression of the original proposed time.
inputs.constraints: Boolean; the original impression is a proposal, not a second booking.

bindingExample.shortSourceText: In this fictional case meeting, the participant moves a planning visit to Wednesday morning so Tuesday caregiving remains possible.

distinction: The participant physically revises a shared calendar around their existing responsibilities. Unlike schedule-buffer, there is no delayed sequence consuming reserve time; unlike priority-insertion, this is a negotiated appointment placement rather than precedence in a queue.
limits: All people, commitments and agreements are illustrative; agreement is not attendance or an outcome.
Each item occupies exactly one discrete planner cell; this is not a scheduling algorithm or a proportional duration chart.
No service is automatically withdrawn when a person proposes a different time.
verificationFocus: Keep every existing commitment fixed while moving only the support appointment to its authored agreed cell. Reject final overlaps and missing day/band references. The ghost appointment never counts as a second booking. Require an initial conflict and an actual move to a free cell.

title: Stop the next contact when consent changes
description: A participant withdraws permission for one planned referral contact. The worker sets that outgoing contact aside while an earlier sharing record remains visibly intact.
creativeDirection: Show the participant beside a worker's desk with the supplied destination-specific permission slips and prepared contact cards. The participant turns the withdrawn slips to their withdrawn faces. For each affected contact, the worker stops before reaching the phone and sets the card in a held tray. Any still-permitted contacts remain ready. Hold the changed permission scopes and, when supplied, dated prior-sharing receipts. Earlier records never reverse or disappear; omit the history region when none are supplied.
goodFor: Explaining prospective withdrawal of referral consent
Distinguishing a contact permission from a historical disclosure record
Showing different permission choices for different services
intent: Show that a changed permission stops the specified future contact without rewriting the past.

inputs.name: people
inputs.description: Label the people making and following the choice.
inputs.constraints: Each label <= 24 characters.

inputs.name: permissions
inputs.description: Set the separate recipient-and-purpose permissions.
inputs.constraints: 1..3 permissions; unique IDs <= 16 characters; recipient <= 24 characters; purpose <= 28 characters; at least one withdrawn permission.

inputs.name: plannedContacts
inputs.description: Bind prepared contacts to the permission that controls them.
inputs.constraints: 1..3 contacts; unique IDs <= 16 characters; permission references must exist; labels <= 26 characters; contacts are preparations, not completed events. At least one contact must reference a withdrawn permission.

inputs.name: priorRecords
inputs.description: Keep supplied historical sharing records separate from future permission.
inputs.constraints: 0..2 records; unique IDs <= 16 characters; recipient/date <= 24 characters; summary <= 30 characters; records never disappear as an effect of withdrawal.

inputs.name: labels
inputs.description: Set every permission, tray and record heading.
inputs.constraints: Each label <= 30 characters.

inputs.name: showPurpose
inputs.description: Display the purpose alongside each recipient.
inputs.constraints: Boolean; hiding the text does not broaden the permission scope.

bindingExample.shortSourceText: In a fictional referral discussion, the participant withdraws permission to contact the housing team, so the worker stops the prepared call while keeping the earlier sharing record.

distinction: The person actively changes a recipient-specific instruction while a worker interrupts a prepared real-world contact. Unlike expiring-lease, permission does not end because a timer runs out; unlike disclosure-aperture, this governs a future action after a prior disclosure has already occurred.
limits: This depicts an authored process, not a statement about legal rights or a product's security guarantees.
Revocation does not erase information already shared; the retained record must not animate backward.
No contact is portrayed as completed merely because permission remains active.
verificationFocus: Stop every prepared contact tied to a withdrawn permission while leaving permitted contacts only ready. Earlier sharing records remain visible. Reject dangling permission IDs and do not imply completed contact. Require an affected prepared contact; omit prior-record and permitted-contact beats when those arrays have no such entries.

title: Make room for a private conversation
description: A participant asks to continue part of a case meeting without a supporter present. The supporter steps into a waiting area, and the worker continues speaking directly with the participant.
creativeDirection: Begin with three people seated around one small consultation table. The participant displays the authored privacy request; the supporter acknowledges, stands and walks to a separate waiting seat. A door or screen closes between the two spaces while the participant and worker remain at the original table. Hold the participant's empty adjacent chair and the supporter's waiting position, without portraying abandonment or a completed assessment.
goodFor: Explaining an optional private segment of a case assessment
Showing that a participant controls a supporter's presence
Introducing confidential conversation arrangements in a social-service setting
intent: Show that the participant can choose who is present for a conversation.

inputs.name: people
inputs.description: Name the three distinct roles in the room.
inputs.constraints: Exactly 3 people, one per role; unique IDs <= 16 characters; labels <= 24 characters; no demographic inference from role.

inputs.name: requestLabel
inputs.description: Set the participant's privacy request.
inputs.constraints: 1..40 characters.

inputs.name: roomLabels
inputs.description: Label the two physical spaces.
inputs.constraints: Each label <= 26 characters; the floor plan is schematic, not a real facility.

inputs.name: partition
inputs.description: Choose the physical separator that closes after the supporter leaves.
inputs.constraints: One of door or screen; both preserve distinct meeting and waiting spaces.

inputs.name: showWaitingSupporter
inputs.description: Keep the supporter visible in the separate waiting area.
inputs.constraints: Boolean; false hides the waiting inset, never implies the person has been dismissed permanently.

inputs.name: copy
inputs.description: Set the acknowledgement and closing context.
inputs.constraints: Each string <= 38 characters.

bindingExample.shortSourceText: In this fictional assessment, the participant requests a private conversation and their chosen supporter waits nearby while the worker listens.

distinction: The explanatory change is a participant-requested alteration of who is physically present during an ongoing conversation. Unlike chosen-service-access, no barrier is removed to admit someone to a service; unlike scope-aperture, actual participants change rooms and the meeting continues.
limits: A room boundary illustrates an arrangement, not soundproofing, data security or legal confidentiality.
The supporter leaves by agreement; do not portray family or supporters as inherently unsafe.
The scene does not assert that a private conversation automatically produces disclosure or resolves a case.
verificationFocus: Keep participant and worker seated in the meeting while the supporter moves into a separate waiting space before the partition closes. Toggling the inset changes visibility only, not who remains in the meeting.

title: Count and correct a missing payment
description: A participant compares an assistance statement with the units actually received. A supplied correction fills some or all of the visible shortfall while any remainder stays open.
creativeDirection: Open an assistance statement next to the participant's receiving tray. Outline tokens show the stated amount; actual received tokens settle into matching positions, leaving empty outlines. The participant points to the gap and the worker adds only the authored correction tokens from a separate correction envelope. Hold the original payment, correction and still-empty positions with distinct patterns so the accounting remains inspectable.
goodFor: Explaining a reported assistance-payment discrepancy
Distinguishing an original payment from a later correction
Showing that a partial correction can leave an unresolved balance
intent: Show how a participant identifies and verifies a payment shortfall.

inputs.name: people
inputs.description: Label the person checking the payment and the worker responding.
