inputs.constraints: Each label <= 26 characters.

inputs.name: payments
inputs.description: Set stated, originally received and separately corrected quantities.
inputs.constraints: 1..2 payments; unique IDs <= 16 characters; labels <= 24 characters; all quantities integers 0..8; statedUnits >= 1; receivedUnits + correctionUnits <= statedUnits; at most 12 stated units overall; at least one original shortfall.

inputs.name: unitLabel
inputs.description: Define what each token represents.
inputs.constraints: 1..24 characters; each token equals exactly one displayed unit; no real currency implied.

inputs.name: labels
inputs.description: Name the quantities and their distinct visual patterns.
inputs.constraints: Each label <= 26 characters; arithmetic is derived from payment inputs.

inputs.name: showTotals
inputs.description: Show derived totals alongside the physical tokens.
inputs.constraints: Boolean; totals must equal the supplied units; no independent count input.

inputs.name: exampleLabel
inputs.description: Identify the scene as an illustrative case.
inputs.constraints: 1..32 characters.

bindingExample.shortSourceText: A fictional recipient expected five demo credits, received three, and verifies a later one-credit correction while one credit remains missing.

distinction: The participant aligns real received units against a separate statement and checks an additive correction, preserving the unpaid remainder. Unlike metric-counter, the argument is a physical reconciliation; unlike household-market-choice, there is no purchase or basket selection; unlike field-conflict-choice, neither amount is chosen as the single true value.
limits: These are fictional accounting units, not a determination of benefit eligibility or payment entitlement.
The stated amount and the received amount are different measures; their difference remains visible.
The scene covers underpayment only and never invents a successful remedy beyond the supplied correction.
verificationFocus: Default statement of five units reconciles three original units plus one correction plus one remaining gap. Reject over-correction. Sum multiple payments without losing per-payment shortfalls or duplicating tokens.

title: Let the person test the remedy
description: A participant reports a specific unusable object and tests it again after an authored repair. The repair action and the participant's acceptance remain separate events.
creativeDirection: Show a participant trying a locker latch that will not close, then placing a complaint marker beside it. A worker replaces the latch while the participant stays present. The participant, rather than the worker, operates the latch again; it closes only in the supplied functioning outcome. Hold the tested object and the participant's separately supplied accepted, not-accepted or pending response. Keep a non-functioning or unaccepted remedy visibly open.
goodFor: Explaining a community grievance remedy
Distinguishing work completed from a remedy accepted
Showing a complainant checking a tangible correction
intent: Show that a reported repair is checked by the person who raised the problem.

inputs.name: people
inputs.description: Label the person raising the issue and the person repairing it.
inputs.constraints: Each label <= 26 characters.

inputs.name: object
inputs.description: Choose the physical object and its concrete test action.
inputs.constraints: Kind selects close/open or switch/light choreography; label <= 24 characters.

inputs.name: testResults
inputs.description: Supply what the object's two tests visibly demonstrate.
inputs.constraints: Before is always not-functioning; after is explicitly authored; not-tested prevents the second operation.

inputs.name: participantResponse
inputs.description: Set the participant's reported response separately from the technical test.
inputs.constraints: One of the listed values; accepted is allowed only after functioning; a functioning test may still be not-accepted or pending.

inputs.name: labels
inputs.description: Set all complaint, repair, test and response text.
inputs.constraints: Each label <= 34 characters; issue and repair copy must match the selected object.

inputs.name: showComplaintMarker
inputs.description: Retain the original complaint marker alongside the tested object.
inputs.constraints: Boolean; hiding the marker does not close the complaint.

bindingExample.shortSourceText: In a fictional shelter, a resident reports a locker latch, tries the replacement themselves, and confirms whether the remedy addresses the complaint.

distinction: A material object is repaired and then physically operated by the affected person, with acceptance independent of the worker's action. Unlike feedback-refinement, the exchange does not edit a draft; unlike status-cycle, closure cannot be inferred merely from the repair step.
limits: Only a small visible object defect is represented; this is not a model for resolving violence, legal disputes or complex safeguarding concerns.
An operating object is not automatically an accepted remedy.
No measured satisfaction or program impact is implied.
verificationFocus: A repair alone never closes the complaint. Functioning and participant acceptance are separate supplied states; reject accepted with a nonfunctioning or untested result. An untested result skips the second operation.

title: Count residents' project ballots
description: Residents cast fictional project-choice ballots into a shared box. The same ballots unfold into an inspectable tally, while abstentions remain separate and no funding decision is inferred.
creativeDirection: Begin with a small row of anonymous residents and a project display. Each resident marks one paper behind a short screen, then places it in the ballot box or keeps an abstention slip. The box opens and the same papers unfold into stacks under their chosen project symbols. Hold every cast ballot, the abstention slips and derived totals. Do not transform votes into money or automatically crown a winner.
goodFor: Introducing a participatory-budget consultation
Showing how individual project ballots make a tally
Distinguishing ballots cast from residents who abstain
intent: Show how resident choices become a transparent project-preference tally.

inputs.name: projects
inputs.description: Define the project choices printed on the ballots.
inputs.constraints: 2..3 projects; unique IDs <= 16 characters; labels <= 26 characters; symbol must be one of the listed values.

inputs.name: ballots
inputs.description: Supply one authored choice or abstention for each anonymous resident shown.
inputs.constraints: 2..8 ballots; unique IDs <= 16 characters; non-null project IDs must exist; null means abstained, not invalid; resident count is derived from this array.

inputs.name: labels
inputs.description: Set the display, box, tally and abstention headings.
inputs.constraints: Each label <= 32 characters.

inputs.name: showTotals
inputs.description: Display per-project and abstention counts derived from the ballots.
inputs.constraints: Boolean; totals sum to the number of supplied ballots.

inputs.name: tallyArrangement
inputs.description: Choose the arrangement of unfolded paper ballots.
inputs.constraints: Stacks or rows; both retain one visible unit per ballot.

inputs.name: closingNote
inputs.default: Preferences are not a funding award
inputs.description: State the boundary between this count and later budget decisions.
inputs.constraints: 1..46 characters; must not imply an automatic funding allocation.

bindingExample.shortSourceText: In a fictional participatory-budget consultation, four residents produce two seating ballots, one reading ballot and one abstention.

inputBindings.closingNote: Preferences are not a funding award

distinction: The same privately marked paper ballots move from individual choice through a ballot box into an auditable tally. Unlike pooled-donor-allocation, the units are votes and never become funds; unlike bar-race, there is no animated rank change or automatic winner.
limits: This is an illustrative preference count, not a secure voting system or a complete electoral rule.
One ballot equals one anonymous illustrative resident; no population estimate is implied.
Ties, eligibility, quorum, invalid ballots and final funding decisions are outside the scene.
verificationFocus: Default totals are two bench ballots, one books ballot and one abstention, preserving all four ballot identities. Reject missing project IDs and never convert vote totals into funding or an inferred winner.

title: Measure the work against the promise
description: A community representative checks one supplied physical dimension of a public-work example against its published specification. A ruler exposes the authored difference without treating a visual inspection as a safety certification.
creativeDirection: Show a published specification beside a simple built wall or handrail. Two community observers extend a measuring tape along the actual structure, keeping its endpoints attached. A lighter promised-length outline remains behind the measured object; the tape's end stops at the supplied observed value. Hold the signed difference, the measurement source label and the two lengths on one scale.
goodFor: Explaining a community monitoring visit
Showing a public commitment checked against a supplied observation
Introducing a specific discrepancy for public accountability
intent: Make a public-work claim inspectable through one concrete measurement.

inputs.name: structure
inputs.description: Choose the physical structure being measured.
inputs.constraints: Low-wall or handrail; geometry is schematic and not a real site.

inputs.name: specification
inputs.description: Set the promised length and common measurement unit.
inputs.constraints: Label <= 28 characters; length finite 1..8; unit <= 18 characters; both lengths use this unit.

inputs.name: observation
inputs.description: Set the observed length and the supplied evidence label.
inputs.constraints: Label/source <= 30 characters; length finite 1..8; no measurement is inferred from a real image.

inputs.name: observers
inputs.description: Name the two people holding the tape endpoints.
inputs.constraints: Exactly 2 observers; unique IDs <= 16 characters; labels <= 24 characters.

inputs.name: showDifference
inputs.description: Label observed minus specified length in addition to the shared ruler.
inputs.constraints: Boolean; signed difference is derived and preserves over-delivery as well as shortfall.

inputs.name: labels
inputs.description: Set the measurement annotations and example caption.
inputs.constraints: Each label <= 32 characters.

bindingExample.shortSourceText: In a fictional social audit, residents compare a four-demo-metre published wall specification with a supplied three-demo-metre measurement.

distinction: Observers physically stretch a tape along a built object while the promised outline remains on the same spatial scale. Unlike capability-matrix or paired-contrast, the evidence is a concrete dimension checked through a measuring action; unlike chart-focus-edit, a measurement is introduced rather than a chart restyled.
limits: The authored measurement is an illustration, not evidence from a real project or an engineering assessment.
One length does not establish overall compliance, workmanship, accessibility or safety.
The layout is schematic and contains no real geography; scale applies only to the displayed measured dimension.
verificationFocus: Both lengths use a single spatial scale. Default observed-minus-promised difference is minus one, while a longer observation yields a positive difference. Measurement endpoints track the actual structure, not the promised outline.

title: Rehearse the new school routine
description: A learner practices a short routine in an unfamiliar school setting with a chosen companion. A supplied final step can be tried independently, while the scene remains explicitly a rehearsal.
creativeDirection: Open on a learner and companion beside a simple interior containing a locker and a classroom doorway. The learner consults a two-step practice strip, opens the named locker, then approaches the named room. The companion either stays alongside or deliberately stands back for the final step, according to the supplied choice. Hold the learner at the final practice stop with the rehearsal label visible, without changing it to enrolled or attended.
goodFor: Explaining a supported transition to a new school
Showing orientation as a concrete practice activity
Distinguishing a rehearsed routine from recorded school attendance
intent: Show how a learner can practice an unfamiliar school routine before it becomes a daily expectation.
family: Supported rehearsal in a physical setting

inputs.name: people
inputs.description: Label the learner and the person supporting the practice.
inputs.constraints: Each label <= 26 characters; roles do not imply an age, disability or family relationship.

inputs.name: stops
inputs.description: Set the small set of tangible stops and the learner's practice actions.
inputs.constraints: Exactly 2 stops, one locker then one classroom; unique IDs <= 16 characters; labels <= 24 characters; action labels <= 28 characters.

inputs.name: finalStepSupport
inputs.description: Show the learner's authored preference for the final practice step.
inputs.constraints: Alongside or stands-back; no automatic progression toward independence is inferred.

inputs.name: showPracticeStrip
inputs.description: Keep the two supplied practice actions visible as a small strip the learner holds.
inputs.constraints: Boolean; the strip is not an attendance record.

inputs.name: labels
inputs.description: Set the setting, rehearsal and learner-choice labels.
inputs.constraints: Each label <= 34 characters; choice copy must match finalStepSupport.

inputs.name: showFootprints
inputs.description: Retain faint footprints of the practiced route.
inputs.constraints: Boolean; footprints represent only this rehearsal, never attendance history or location tracking.

bindingExample.shortSourceText: During a fictional transition visit, a learner practices opening a locker and finding the new classroom, choosing to try the last step while their companion stands back.

distinction: The learner rehearses concrete object use and a short routine while choosing the companion's role. Unlike returning-learner-worktable, no prior learning artifact is carried back into a lesson; unlike chosen-service-access, the scene does not remove an admission barrier or claim successful service uptake.
limits: A practice visit is not enrollment, attendance, learning progress or a retention outcome.
The two-room interior is schematic and does not reproduce a real school layout.
Supported and independent practice are alternatives, not a hierarchy of participant worth or ability.

The author must make labels.choice agree with finalStepSupport. The renderer preserves supplied prose exactly and derives support geometry/state only from structured inputs. It does not infer natural-language meaning or rewrite the choice into canned English.
verificationFocus: Follow the authored locker and classroom routine in order. Alongside and stands-back alter the companion gesture while both remain labeled as practice. No attendance or enrollment result is introduced.

title: Agree who uses the shared machine when
description: Two or three livelihood participants resolve a supplied overlap in requests for one shared machine. Their agreed bookings become separate usage windows while the machine itself remains a single finite resource.
creativeDirection: Show one sewing machine beside a compact time ruler, with the supplied participant request strips overlapping above it. The participants slide only the authored changed strips into their agreed non-overlapping windows and place agreement tabs. A short physical turn at the same machine is shown for each booked participant in order, with the others' named strips remaining visible. Hold the one machine and the agreed schedule; unresolved requests stay above the ruler rather than masquerading as bookings.
goodFor: Explaining scheduling for a shared livelihood asset
Showing a negotiated solution to simultaneous equipment demand
Distinguishing a request from an agreed reservation
intent: Show how people share one productive asset by agreeing distinct times.

inputs.name: machine
inputs.description: Choose and label the single shared productive asset.
inputs.constraints: Kind selects the physical work gesture; label <= 28 characters; exactly one asset is shown.

inputs.name: timeSlots
inputs.description: Set the discrete reservable windows.
inputs.constraints: 2..5 slots; unique IDs <= 16 characters; labels <= 18 characters; each slot has equal schematic width, not an inferred real duration.

inputs.name: requests
inputs.description: Bind each participant's request to an authored booking or unresolved result.
inputs.constraints: 2..3 requests; unique IDs <= 16 characters; participant <= 24 characters; slot references must exist; non-null agreed slot IDs must be unique; at least two requested slots overlap.

inputs.name: labels
inputs.description: Set the request and booking annotations.
inputs.constraints: Each label <= 30 characters.

inputs.name: showOriginalRequests
inputs.description: Keep dotted original requests above the agreed bookings.
inputs.constraints: Boolean; dotted requests never count as additional machine usage.

inputs.name: showUsageTurns
inputs.description: Show a brief illustrative use gesture for each agreed participant.
inputs.constraints: Boolean; use gestures illustrate the schedule and do not claim completed production or income.

bindingExample.shortSourceText: Two fictional makers both request demo slot A for one sewing machine, then agree that maker A uses A and maker B uses B.

distinction: The participants negotiate contention over a physical machine that remains single, then occupy it at separate authored times. Unlike queue-relief, capacity never increases; unlike schedule-buffer, no deadline reserve absorbs a delay; unlike priority-insertion, the change is a mutually agreed reservation rather than imposed precedence.
limits: This is a small authored schedule, not an allocation algorithm or a demonstration of fair access at scale.
No revenue, employment or productivity outcome is implied by a booked or illustrated equipment turn.
A null agreed slot stays unresolved and never receives a use gesture.
verificationFocus: Resolve default overlapping requests into two distinct slots on one machine. A null agreed slot remains unresolved with no use gesture. Reject duplicate agreed slots and ensure ghost requests do not increase usage.

title: Keep the participant at the center of interpretation
description: A participant and worker exchange short statements through an interpreter while continuing to face each other. Each translated statement remains visibly attributed to its original speaker.
creativeDirection: Place the participant and worker across a small table, with the interpreter seated to one side. The first speaker's original bubble appears above them; the interpreter's corresponding supplied wording forms a smaller adjacent echo while the original speaker attribution stays anchored. Repeat once in the opposite direction, with a pause between turns. Hold both paired statements and direct participant-worker sightlines so the interpreter supports the conversation without replacing the participant's voice.
goodFor: Explaining language support during a case assessment
Showing turn-taking in an interpreted consultation
Distinguishing a participant's words from a worker's response
intent: Show interpretation enabling a direct conversation with the participant.

inputs.name: people
inputs.description: Label the three conversational roles.
inputs.constraints: Each label <= 24 characters; interpreter is distinct from participant and worker.

inputs.name: languages
inputs.description: Label the two authored language versions without generating a translation.
inputs.constraints: Each label <= 22 characters; defaults are explicitly fictional language labels.

inputs.name: turns
inputs.description: Supply the original and interpreted wording for each conversational turn.
inputs.constraints: Exactly 2 turns, participant then worker; unique IDs <= 16 characters; each text <= 48 characters; fictional defaults repeat English under demo language labels; real translations must be supplied and verified by the author.

inputs.name: labels
inputs.description: Set the attribution key and example caption.
inputs.constraints: Each label <= 38 characters.

inputs.name: showSightlines
inputs.description: Use subtle gaze guides to keep the participant and worker facing one another.
inputs.constraints: Boolean; guides depict conversational orientation, not surveillance or measured attention.

inputs.name: bubbleLayout
inputs.description: Arrange each original and interpreted wording while preserving speaker attribution.
inputs.constraints: Paired or stacked; the interpreter never becomes the attributed author of the participant's statement.

bindingExample.shortSourceText: In a fictional case conversation, an interpreter conveys the participant's preferred meeting time and the worker's reply while both continue addressing each other.

distinction: The scene maintains two-way human turn-taking, original-speaker attribution and direct participant-worker orientation while an interpreter adds a second wording. Unlike packet-stream or a data-pipeline, messages do not pass through anonymous processing stages; unlike word-reveal, the explanatory action is who speaks, who interprets and who is addressed.
limits: The animation does not translate text or certify the accuracy, confidentiality or quality of interpretation.
All supplied utterances must be brief enough for a six-second illustration; longer dialogue belongs in a longer scene.
The default English copies under fictional language labels demonstrate bindings only and must not be presented as an actual bilingual exchange.
verificationFocus: Render exactly the supplied participant then worker turns, retaining original-speaker attribution for both wordings. Paired/stacked layout and sightline toggles preserve that attribution and introduce no generated translation.

title: Save seed for the next planting
description: A household or cooperative chooses how much of its supplied harvest to retain as seed. The same seed lot crosses a fallow interval and returns to the same plot for sowing, with current use, recorded storage loss, and remaining seed kept visible.
creativeDirection: Frames 0-11 reveal a schematic plot, harvested crop on a mat, and its named cultivator. Frames 12-48 show the cultivator sliding a chosen portion into a seed jar while the current-use portion stays on the mat. Frames 49-100 close the jar and turn a seasonal backdrop from harvested stubble to fallow ground. Only a nonzero recorded storage loss triggers a temporary opening so that loss can leave into its separate visible tray; close smoothly after the complete loss portion clears and before the planting reopening at frame 101. With zero loss, retain the closed storage state without that opening pulse. Frames 101-144 reopen the same jar as the cultivator draws a furrow in the same plot and sows the supplied amount. Frames 145-167 hold the sown furrow, remaining seed, current-use portion, and loss tray together. No sprouts or next harvest appear. Frames 168-179 fade to the common opaque ground for the six-second seam.
goodFor: Explain a household's choice to retain seed from its own harvest
Show how a cooperative carries a seed lot between agricultural seasons
Distinguish seed reserved, seed actually sown, and seed remaining
intent: Explain how retaining part of a harvest connects one season's work to the next planting without promising a future yield.

inputs.name: crop
inputs.description: Names one crop and supplies all material quantities. Current use equals harvest minus reserved seed. Remaining seed equals reserved seed minus recorded storage loss minus sown seed. No future harvest is calculated.
inputs.constraints: label 1..24 characters; symbol grain or bean; unitLabel 1..12 characters; finite quantities 0..10000 with at most two decimal places in one common mass unit; harvestQuantity > 0; 0 <= reservedQuantity <= harvestQuantity; 0 <= storageLossQuantity <= reservedQuantity; 0 <= sownQuantity <= reservedQuantity - storageLossQuantity; reject inconsistent values rather than clamp; derived balances use exact decimal arithmetic

inputs.name: cultivator
inputs.description: Names the decision maker, selects a household or cooperative silhouette, and supplies the visible statement of its seed-retention choice.
inputs.constraints: label 1..28 characters; mode household or cooperative; choiceLabel 1..40 characters; any quantities stated in choiceLabel must agree with crop; silhouette count is decorative and does not represent membership

inputs.name: seasons
inputs.description: Labels the three temporal settings while the same plot and seed jar remain identifiable. These labels indicate order, not measured elapsed duration.
inputs.constraints: three required labels, each 1..28 characters; no inferred dates, climate, or season length

inputs.name: balanceLabels
inputs.description: Supplies all material-accounting labels on the mat, jar, loss tray, and furrow. The reserved label applies before sowing and the remaining label after sowing, so the reserved subtotal is never added to final destinations.
inputs.constraints: five required labels, each 1..28 characters; currentUse must describe the non-reserved portion without implying a sale or consumption event that is not shown

inputs.name: evidenceLabel
inputs.description: Keeps the example's factual status visible across the seasonal transition and resolved hold.
inputs.constraints: 1..56 characters; fictional defaults must retain an explicit fictional label; factual substitutions require supplied quantities and must not assert a predicted yield

inputs.name: showQuantities
inputs.description: Shows supplied and derived material quantities with their common unit. When false, the authored choice, destination labels, and evidence label remain visible and material proportions stay unchanged.
inputs.constraints: boolean; the visual quantity model remains identical in either setting

bindingExample.shortSourceText: In this fictional example, the Oak household keeps 4 kg from a 12 kg bean harvest for planting and sets 8 kg aside for current household use. Across the interval it records 1 kg of seed storage loss, later sows 2 kg back into the same plot, and retains 1 kg in the jar. No next-season yield is specified.

distinction: The same cultivator sets aside part of its own harvest and returns that physical seed to the same plot after a visible fallow interval. Its defining action is seasonal reuse as planting material, not donor allocation, replenishing retail shelves, a service handoff, or movement through pipeline boxes. Unlike battery-dispatch-balance, the material is placed into cultivated soil and the scene deliberately leaves biological outcomes unshown. No delivery, purchase, or new external stock restores the jar.
limits: One crop, one decision maker, one schematic plot, and one harvest-to-planting interval. No real geography, household demographics, or cooperative membership count is inferred.

All material quantities are supplied or exact balance differences. The final balance is harvest = current use + storage loss + sown seed + remaining seed. Reservation is an intermediate subtotal, not an extra destination.

The seed glyphs illustrate the material and are not individual seeds, yield units, or counts of plants. Material bands use one common mass scale across the mat, jar, tray, and furrow; labels provide precise quantities.

Zero reservation leaves the jar empty and suppresses sowing. Zero storage loss leaves a labeled empty loss tray. Zero sowing keeps usable seed in storage. These cases never receive invented motion suggesting use.

This is neither seed-storage advice nor a germination, food-security, income, or efficacy claim. Storage practices, viability, weather, harvest costs, and the next yield are outside the scene. The supplied storage loss is recorded, never estimated from duration.

Sowing concludes the narrative. The editorial loop fades out before returning to the earlier harvest and does not imply that the sown seed immediately produced that harvest. All visible text comes from the supplied inputs or formatted quantities.

The author must make cultivator.choiceLabel and evidenceLabel internally consistent with supplied quantities and factual status. Prose remains exact and is not parsed for quantities, translated or replaced with canned English. The renderer derives material quantities and stage state from structured fields.

A temporary storage-phase opening occurs only for nonzero recorded loss: loss clears the opening before a smooth closure, completed before the planting reopening begins at frame 101. Zero loss keeps the storage jar closed without an extraction-opening pulse. The initial post-reservation closure and explicit planting reopening remain distinct.
verificationFocus: Harvest portions remain conserved across immediate use, reserved seed, storage loss and planting; only reserved usable seed returns to the same plot, and the scene stops before germination or an inferred yield.

title: Add a field without inventing the past
description: A small table gains one new field while every earlier record keeps its identity and its uncollected value. A later record supplies a value under the expanded schema, leaving the older gaps visible.
creativeDirection: On a 960x600 React/SVG canvas, frames 0-11 reveal a compact table of earlier records. Frames 12-48 slide the existing columns left and unfold one new column from the header seam. Frames 49-92 place an explicit not-collected mark in that column for each earlier record without changing any original value. Frames 93-132 seat one later record in the same table, with its authored new-field value or missing mark. Frames 133-167 hold both generations under the new header and optional version captions. Frames 168-179 fade to the shared opaque palette ground, giving a deterministic six-second loop at 30fps.
goodFor: Explain an evolving collection form during a changing field program
Show why adding a question does not supply historical answers
Introduce a schema extension before discussing any backfill process
intent: Separate the addition of a field from the collection of a value for that field.

inputs.name: earlierRecords
inputs.description: Earlier rows whose recorded values remain unchanged throughout the extension.
inputs.constraints: 1..3 items; unique IDs 1..16 characters; labels 1..22 characters; recordedValue 1..18 characters; these rows have no supplied value for the new field

inputs.name: fields
inputs.description: The retained column, newly introduced column, and explicit meaning of earlier empty cells.
inputs.constraints: All keys required; labels 1..20 characters; missingLabel must mean not collected, never zero, false, or a negative finding

inputs.name: laterRecord
inputs.description: One later row created under the expanded schema. Null retains a missing mark rather than manufacturing an answer.
inputs.constraints: id 1..16 characters and absent from earlierRecords; label 1..22 characters; recordedValue 1..18 characters; addedValue null or 1..18 characters

inputs.name: phaseLabels
inputs.description: Labels the collection change and the later record without assigning real dates.
inputs.constraints: All keys required; each label 1..30 characters

inputs.name: showVersionLabels
inputs.description: Keeps the before and expanded captions beside the corresponding header outlines.
inputs.constraints: boolean; hiding captions cannot remove missing-value marks or the later-record distinction

inputs.name: evidenceLabel
inputs.description: Keeps the illustrative status and missing-data boundary visible.
inputs.constraints: 1..64 characters; fictional defaults retain an explicit fictional qualifier

bindingExample.shortSourceText: A fictional outreach form initially records a site. It later adds visit mode. Two earlier records retain not-collected visit modes, while a new East record supplies In person.

distinction: Unlike cell-normalization, this changes the available field structure without correcting existing values. Unlike schema-mapping, no fields are paired across two schemas. Unlike state-preserving-source-refresh, the visible change is a new collection question and its historical absence, not refreshing values from an existing source.
limits: One retained field, one added field, one later row, and at most three earlier rows fit the six-second explanation.
The ending record count is earlierRecords.length + 1. A new column does not create or remove earlier records.
The earlier records always retain missing marks in the added column. No default, imputation, migration, enrichment, or retrospectively inferred answer is shown.
The sequence is a conceptual collection example. It makes no claim about a particular database migration system or any shipped form-editing feature.
The editorial fade resets the illustration, not the stored records. All labels are supplied inputs.
verificationFocus: Each earlier record retains its ID and existing value, its added-field value stays not collected, and exactly one supplied later record enters. A null later value remains visibly missing.

sourceRefs.rationale: The history identifies rapidly changing collection schemas as a practical crisis-data problem.

sourceRefs.locator: page 5, Key Differentiators and Product Vision
sourceRefs.rationale: The strategy calls for configuration across changing domain needs; the proposal isolates one bounded schema extension.

title: Fit one new tool to existing data
description: An optional utility seats into a workspace only after an authored installation choice. Its category-count stencil then reads the retained records and reveals one derived tally, making added capability distinct from data replacement.
creativeDirection: Frames 0-11 reveal a work surface, a bounded record strip, and an empty tool socket on the 960x600 canvas. Frames 12-55 bring the named utility beside the socket and display the supplied decision. For install, frames 56-90 seat the utility and align its counting stencil with the unchanged category field. Frames 91-132 draw one tally mark per retained record into its category, resolving compact bars on a common integer scale. For defer, the utility stays beside the empty socket and no tally appears. Hold the retained records, decision, and resulting capability through frame 167, then use the shared opaque exit through frame 179. All movement is frame-driven React/SVG at 30fps.
goodFor: Explain an optional extension adding one task-specific capability
Show a team choosing a reusable utility without replacing its dataset
Introduce a plugin concept before a verified installation demonstration
intent: Show that a chosen extension adds an operation over retained data.

inputs.name: records
inputs.description: Small fictional records counted by the illustrated utility after installation.
inputs.constraints: 1..8 items; unique IDs 1..16 characters; categoryId must reference categories; each record contributes exactly one count

inputs.name: categories
inputs.description: Category labels and display order, including a category with no records if supplied.
inputs.constraints: 2..3 items; unique IDs 1..16 characters; labels 1..18 characters; zero-count categories remain labeled

inputs.name: utility
inputs.description: Names the optional utility and its fixed count-by-category operation.
inputs.constraints: All keys required; labels 1..26 characters; operationLabel must describe counting supplied records by category, not an arbitrary executable operation

inputs.name: installation
inputs.description: Authored human decision controlling whether the capability becomes available.
inputs.constraints: choice install or defer; decisionLabel 1..32 characters and consistent with choice; no automatic install

inputs.name: copy
inputs.description: Every workspace, status, result, and example caption.
inputs.constraints: All keys required; each string 1..36 characters; result must describe record counts

inputs.name: showRecordIds
inputs.description: Shows record IDs on the retained strip while each record becomes a tally mark.
inputs.constraints: boolean; each underlying record and category membership remains unchanged

bindingExample.shortSourceText: A fictional lending team chooses to install a category-count utility. The same four source records produce three Books counts and one Tools count. Deferring installation leaves the source records available and the tool slot empty.

distinction: Unlike dashboard-slot-assembly, a new operation becomes available before it acts on retained data. Unlike pipeline-step-splice, no processing chain is rewired. The socketed stencil visibly derives a result from the existing records rather than introducing a renamed card collection.
limits: One optional utility and one fixed tally operation. No executable code, external URLs, marketplace requests, dependency resolution, or security review occur.
The sum of category counts must equal records.length and each record is counted exactly once. Installation never adds, removes, or edits source records.
The default is fictional. This is not evidence of a shipped plugin system, one-click installation, compatibility with arbitrary data, or a particular installation time.
The defer outcome produces no result and no installed-state marker. Zero-count categories remain visible.
No medical prediction, automated risk assessment, or clinical decision is represented by the utility.
verificationFocus: The install choice seats exactly one utility and produces category totals from retained record IDs. Defer leaves the socket empty and produces no tally. Changing category membership changes only derived counts.

sourceRefs.rationale: The long-term strategy describes teams installing mission-specific utilities over a common platform; the proposal uses a non-clinical counting example.

title: Match the reference before comparing a charge
description: A fictional invoice line is laid over a separate price reference. Only matching procedure, provider, payer, period, and quantity windows permit the amounts to align on one scale; an unmatched context leaves the comparison unresolved.
creativeDirection: Frames 0-11 reveal a short invoice strip and a separate reference sheet on a 960x600 canvas. Frames 12-70 slide their context windows into vertical registration, retaining a visible notch at each mismatched key. When every key and quantity agrees, frames 71-125 extend the two total-amount rulers from the same zero and open a signed difference bracket. Otherwise the amounts stay separate without a difference bracket. Frames 126-167 hold the matched or unresolved context, source labels, and review caption. Exit to the shared opaque ground at frames 168-179. The six-second React/SVG sequence is deterministic at 30fps.
goodFor: Explain why published prices need the same billing context
Support a fictional price-transparency investigation
Show a discrepancy for review without implying a refund or legal entitlement
intent: Make the context required for a monetary comparison explicit before showing a difference.

inputs.name: invoice
inputs.description: One fictional billed line with an amount in the shared smallest monetary unit.
inputs.constraints: procedureCode 1..14 characters; providerKey and payerKey 1..22 characters; periodLabel 1..20 characters; quantity integer 1..5; unitPriceMinor integer 0..1000000; no real patient identifiers or real procedure codes in defaults

inputs.name: reference
inputs.description: A separately supplied reference with its own source label.
inputs.constraints: Key bounds match invoice; quantity integer 1..5; unitPriceMinor integer 0..1000000; sourceLabel 1..34 characters; comparison eligibility requires exact equality of all four context keys and quantity

inputs.name: money
inputs.description: Defines one common monetary unit for both lines and the signed difference.
inputs.constraints: currencyLabel 1..18 characters; minorUnitsPerUnit exactly 1 or 100; both lines use this same currency and unit scale; no exchange-rate conversion

inputs.name: copy
inputs.description: All visible context, outcome, and evidence labels.
inputs.constraints: All keys required. Source-role captions invoice and reference: 1..32 characters. Context-key labels procedure, provider, payer, period and quantity: 1..16 characters. Outcome captions matched, unmatched and difference: 1..32 characters. Review and example: 1..52 characters.

inputs.name: focus
inputs.description: Chooses whether the matched windows or the amount rulers receive the final emphasis.
inputs.constraints: keys or amounts; amount focus never hides unmatched context or creates a comparison

inputs.name: showDifference
inputs.description: Shows the signed total-amount difference only after complete context agreement.
inputs.constraints: boolean; totals are quantity times unitPriceMinor; difference equals invoice total minus reference total; mismatch suppresses both numeric difference and difference geometry

bindingExample.shortSourceText: A fictional billed line for DEMO-P1 at Demo clinic A under Demo plan Q in Demo period A is 84 demo credits for one unit. A separately supplied reference for the same context is 60 demo credits. The illustration exposes a 24-credit difference for review, without deciding what is owed.

distinction: Unlike benefit-shortfall-correction, no payment is corrected and no unpaid amount is treated as an entitlement. Unlike paired-contrast, exact context keys govern whether a numeric comparison is allowed. Unlike keyed-row-zipper, the records remain separate and open an amount ruler rather than becoming a joined dataset.
limits: This is a fictional one-line comparison. It is not a medical billing interpretation, legal determination, price guarantee, negotiation result, or refund claim.
Totals use exact integer arithmetic in the shared smallest unit. The signed difference may be negative, positive, or zero; no automatic favorable result is implied.
A mismatch in any context key or quantity leaves the comparison unresolved. Similar text is not treated as a match, and no real CPT or payer taxonomy is inferred.
The ruler uses a common zero and a domain derived from the larger supplied total. For two zero totals use a one-minor-unit display domain without changing either value.
Currency, quantities, source label, period, and fictional status stay visible at the resolved hold. Published reference prices can have qualifications outside this bounded example.
verificationFocus: Require all four context keys and quantity to match before showing a difference. Confirm exact signed arithmetic and common scale for zero, equal, larger, and smaller billed totals. A mismatched payer must never display a computed discrepancy.

sourceRefs.locator: pages 9-10, Early Results / healthcare cost comparison
sourceRefs.rationale: The plan describes comparing provider- and insurer-specific procedure prices with billed charges. The stock concept preserves matching context but does not repeat patient outcomes or legal assertions.

title: Make room without replacing the work
description: A bounded workspace retains its existing resources while additional requests wait outside its current allowance. An authored plan choice expands the available slots or leaves the requests pending, preserving both user agency and resource identity.
creativeDirection: Frames 0-11 reveal the current workspace as a shallow tray with its exact slot allowance on the 960x600 canvas. Frames 12-50 bring requested resource tabs alongside the filled tray while the existing tabs stay fixed. Frames 51-80 show the supplied choice. For expand, frames 81-125 extend the same tray along a hinged side, reveal the additional slots, and seat all requested tabs. For keep, retain the original boundary and pending tabs. Frames 126-167 hold the selected allowance, existing identities, and any pending requests. Fade to the common opaque ground at frames 168-179. Use deterministic frame-driven React/SVG at 30fps.
goodFor: Explain voluntary movement between capacity-limited software plans
Show a team retaining prior work while adding resources
Distinguish a pending need from an authorized plan change
intent: Show that an authorized capacity change creates room while the current work stays intact.

inputs.name: existingResources
inputs.description: The resources already inside the current workspace.
inputs.constraints: 1..6 items; unique IDs 1..16 characters across both resource collections; labels 1..20 characters; length cannot exceed allowances.currentAllowance.limit

inputs.name: requestedResources
inputs.description: Additional authored requests that remain pending unless the expanded allowance is chosen.
inputs.constraints: 1..3 items; unique IDs 1..16 characters across both resource collections; labels 1..20 characters; combined resource count must exceed allowances.currentAllowance.limit and not exceed allowances.expandedAllowance.limit

inputs.name: allowances
inputs.description: Two explicit resource-slot allowances. These are capacities, not independent claims about the number of connected datasets.
inputs.constraints: All keys required; labels 1..28 characters; integer limits 1..9; expanded limit strictly greater than current limit; actual resource counts derive only from the collections

inputs.name: choice
inputs.description: The human authorization controlling the boundary change.
inputs.constraints: decision expand or keep; label 1..36 characters and consistent with decision; no timer, usage threshold, or animation event authorizes an upgrade by itself

inputs.name: copy
inputs.description: All framing and evidence labels.
inputs.constraints: All keys required; each string 1..42 characters; example retains a fictional qualifier

inputs.name: showResourceLabels
inputs.description: Shows resource names on the persistent tabs.
inputs.constraints: boolean; hiding names does not change IDs, counts, pending status, or the selected allowance

bindingExample.shortSourceText: A fictional workspace has three resource slots and three existing resources. Its team requests two more, chooses a five-slot allowance, and keeps the original three while seating the two pending requests. Keeping the current allowance leaves both requests pending.

distinction: Unlike stagger-cards, the explanatory action changes a finite containing boundary after an explicit choice. Unlike queue-relief, resources occupy persistent workspace slots rather than leaving after service. Unlike dashboard-slot-assembly, no layout rearrangement or content reshaping makes the new capacity.
limits: One workspace, two allowance choices, and at most nine total resources. No actual billing, subscription entitlement, import, connection, or checkout is performed.

The combined collection lengths determine resource count. Capacity is supplied separately and must contain the final count when expansion is selected. Invalid combinations are rejected, not silently truncated.
Existing resource identity and content remain unchanged. Pending resources are not shown as already imported or connected.
No real plan names, prices, conversion rate, automatic charge, or guaranteed growth is illustrated.
A kept allowance is a valid outcome with visible pending demand. No celebratory failure mark or forced-upgrade message punishes that choice.
verificationFocus: The same existing resource IDs remain inside the same tray. Expand reveals exactly the supplied extra capacity and seats every requested resource; keep changes no allowance and leaves every request pending.

sourceRefs.locator: pages 11-13, Freemium and subscription value metrics
sourceRefs.rationale: The strategy links voluntary plan expansion to increased team and data needs after users have experienced value. The proposal isolates resource capacity without real pricing or adoption claims.

title: The same count can hold different amounts
description: Two equal-count collections begin with matching item marks. Each item unfolds into a strip proportional to its supplied byte size, revealing different total data volumes on one common ruler without changing the item count.
creativeDirection: Frames 0-11 reveal two labeled shelves containing the same number of authored items. Frames 12-48 align their count marks one for one. Frames 49-110 unfold each item horizontally into an adjacent byte-length strip while retaining its small identity tab; both shelves share one fixed zero and scale. Frames 111-145 show the derived collection totals beneath the unchanged count marks. Hold through frame 167 with the supplied measurement basis and proxy note, then fade to the shared opaque ground through frame 179. Use the same palette, 960x600 React/SVG canvas, deterministic 180-frame timing, and 30fps.
goodFor: Explain why dataset count is an imperfect storage proxy
Show why the same number of rows can occupy different byte sizes
Separate a simple allowance metric from a measured resource quantity
intent: Expose what an item count does not tell us about the amount of data.

inputs.name: groups
inputs.description: Two small collections with item-level byte quantities. Counts and totals derive exclusively from these items.
inputs.constraints: Exactly 2 groups; unique group IDs 1..16 characters; group labels 1..24 characters; each group has 1..3 items and both lengths are equal; all item IDs globally unique 1..16 characters; item labels 1..16 characters; bytes integers 0..10000000; group byte totals must differ

inputs.name: itemKind
inputs.description: Selects whether item marks stand for complete datasets or individual rows, without mixing the two grains.
inputs.constraints: datasets or rows; every item in both groups uses the chosen grain; no separate item-count prop

inputs.name: measure
inputs.description: Defines the common size basis, display conversion, and fixed ruler maximum for both shelves.
inputs.constraints: displayUnit B, KiB, or MiB uses divisors 1, 1024, or 1048576; basisLabel 1..36 characters; scaleMaximumBytes positive integer <= 60000000 and >= both group totals; both groups must share the same stored/uncompressed basis; formatted decimal values may round, geometry uses exact bytes

inputs.name: copy

default.proxyNote: Count alone does not determine size

inputs.description: Labels the two measures and preserves the limitation of the proxy.
inputs.constraints: All keys required; count, size, total 1..24 characters; proxyNote and example 1..52 characters

inputs.name: showItemSizes
inputs.description: Shows each item byte quantity beside its persistent ID tab.
inputs.constraints: boolean; both collection totals, item counts, unit, and basis remain visible

inputs.name: showCountGuides
inputs.description: Keeps the one-for-one count alignment visible while byte strips extend.
inputs.constraints: boolean; hiding guides never changes collection length or byte geometry

bindingExample.shortSourceText: Two fictional collections each contain three datasets. The first stores 100, 200, and 300 illustrative bytes; the second stores 500, 800, and 900. Their equal dataset counts coexist with totals of 600 and 2200 bytes on the same size scale.

copy.proxyNote: Count alone does not determine size

distinction: Unlike capability-matrix, this changes the represented measure from a discrete count to item-weighted size. Unlike bar-race, no rank changes over time and no data values evolve. Unlike population-normalized-map, no denominator division or geographic fill is used; the animation opens each counted object to expose its unequal weight.
limits: Exactly two equal-count groups and at most three items per group. Quantities are fictional measurement examples, not actual compression, transfer, memory, or storage benchmarks.
Every displayed total equals the sum of item bytes. Item count and byte volume remain distinct units; no conversion from count to bytes is inferred.
Both shelves use one zero, one scale, and one measurement basis. An empty-byte item keeps its count mark even though its size strip has zero length.
The selected datasets or rows grain applies to all items. A dataset and a row must never count as interchangeable units.
This does not assess whether a pricing policy is fair or predict actual costs. It illustrates a limitation of a proxy named in the strategy.
verificationFocus: Equal collection lengths remain fixed as each strip unfolds to bytes divided by scaleMaximumBytes. Verify exact byte totals, zero-byte items retained in counts, identical scale across groups, and the same measurement basis.

sourceRefs.rationale: The plan explicitly distinguishes simple dataset-count pricing from precise data-size usage measurement.
The plan describes row counts as approximations for byte-scale categories, supporting a generic warning about counting proxies.

title: Separate accounts preserve separate attribution

An account label is not proof of a real person, consent, authorization, legal signature, or secure identity. No credential or permission mechanism is modeled.
The source authors of the fictional choreography are known to the animation, but the shared-account ledger retains only the shared identity. Do not add individual attribution to earlier entries.

title: When a temporary share ends
description: Two equal-length fictional receipt periods expose the same operating outflow and a temporary distribution. After the authored term boundary, that distribution no longer leaves and the retained period cash increases by the exact amount, without forecasting growth or solvency.
creativeDirection: Frames 0-11 reveal two equal-sized period trays and one common monetary ruler on the 960x600 canvas. Frames 12-65 partition the first receipt strip into operating outflow, temporary distribution, and retained cash. Frames 66-95 turn the authored term marker between the trays and close only the temporary-distribution outlet. Frames 96-140 lay the second identical receipt strip into the second tray: operating outflow stays the same and the formerly distributed portion remains in retained cash. Frames 141-167 hold both periods and their exact reconciliation side by side. Exit to shared opaque ground at frames 168-179. Use frame-driven React/SVG at 30fps and no stochastic timing.

bindingExample.shortSourceText: Two fictional periods each receive 100 demo credits and spend 60 on operating outflow. A temporary distribution of 10 percent sends 10 credits out in period A and leaves 30 retained. The authored term has ended in period B, so no distribution leaves and 40 are retained. These are separate period flows, not an accumulated balance.

distinction: Unlike pooled-donor-allocation, the explanation compares two separate time-bounded receipt flows after a term changes. Unlike expiring-lease, no exclusive permission token returns to neutral custody. The expired outlet changes one conserved cash partition while equal receipts and operating outflow expose its exact effect.
limits: This is an illustrative arithmetic model, not financial advice, investment terms, a valuation, a profit statement, or a solvency projection. It uses no company financial figures.
Each period reconciles receipts = operating outflow + active distribution + retained period cash. The second retained amount exceeds the first by the first distribution, with all other inputs fixed.
Compute the active distribution using integer basis-point arithmetic. Reject fractional minor-unit distributions or negative retained amounts.
Both periods are separate flows over equal durations. Do not carry the first remainder into the second tray or display their sum as a company balance.

Operating outflow is a supplied composite. Taxes, financing transactions, accruals, other liabilities, ownership, and legal treatment are outside the model. No claim about employee compensation or investor rights follows from the illustration.
verificationFocus: Verify exact integer reconciliation in both periods, zero distribution after the term boundary, and a retained-flow difference equal to the first distribution. Swapping presentation layout cannot change amounts or scale.

goodFor: Explain the difference between a domain description and a proposed data model

distinction: Unlike schema-mapping, the starting material is a sentence rather than two field schemas. Unlike entity-spine-assembly, no source records are materialized and no unique-member set is calculated. The hero action preserves the origin of each authored concept as language becomes a proposed structure. Unlike prose-measurement-ledger, this proposes conceptual entity types and a relationship rather than extracting a subject's measurement, unit, reporting period, and qualifier. It defines a model, not an observation row.
limits: One short sentence, two entities, one relation, and at most one attribute fit the six-second loop. More complex domain modeling belongs in a longer explanation.

All mappings and labels are authored inputs, not generated model output. The scene does not implement description-logic reasoning, model training, natural-language parsing, or arbitrary-domain configuration.
No cardinality, uniqueness, datatype, relationship inference, or business rule may be added unless explicitly present in a future separately specified contract.
Pending review remains pending without a success marker. Accepted marks only the supplied owner decision, not objective model correctness or a deployed workspace.
The stock animation makes no claim that a particular product provides natural-language configuration or that a proposed model has been deployed.

Mapped-label validation trims surrounding whitespace and Unicode punctuation from both label and referenced source fragment, strips at most one leading English a/an/the case-insensitively only when followed by whitespace, then uses locale-independent lowercase. The nonempty normalized label must be a substring of the normalized source. This finite validation rule does not alter original sentence parts, labels, rendered content, controls, export or aria. It does not strip internal punctuation, normalize accents or Unicode compatibility, stem words, detect languages or infer meaning.
verificationFocus: Every draft item references the exact supplied source part, all entity references resolve, the original sentence remains unchanged, and pending review never receives an acceptance marker. Layout changes preserve relation direction.

title: Compare the observed result with its expectation
description: An expected-result sheet aligns over an observed-result sheet for each authored test. Matching wording registers exactly, mismatches separate into a visible gap, and unobserved results remain untested.

Unequal strings separate vertically and retain both complete values with a mismatch bracket. A null observation retains an empty lower slot and never receives a verdict. Frames 109..167 hold all tests, expected results, observations and derived states together. Use deterministic frame-driven React/SVG at 960x600, 180 frames and 30 fps, with the shared palette. Reveal during frames 0..11 and fade to the common opaque ground during frames 168..179.

goodFor: Explain ownership across a change of tool

title: Send the structure, run the question locally

inputs.description: Schema labels copied to the planner.

No real product screen, external fetch, supplied code execution, or measured performance claim. All text is authored; no JSX, functions or URLs in props.

Returned queries execute in the browser over locally resident relations.
Concrete values and user text have separately supported crossings, so an unconditional privacy claim would be false.

Freshness, authorization and source version changes are not modeled.
No real product screen, external fetch, supplied code execution, or measured performance claim. All text is authored; no JSX, functions or URLs in props.

Each exact raw columns[].cells[] value may be presented as at most two fixed 12px LiteralDataText lines, splitting after eight whole grapheme clusters within its 168px column. No stored newline, truncation, normalization, equality change or narrowing of the accepted <=16-character domain is introduced.
