inputs.description: Visible example and phase labels.
inputs.constraints: All fields required; each 1..38 characters.

bindingExample.shortSourceText: Refresh Site A to Site A North, leave Site B unchanged and flag Site C as missing from the source. Preserve each record ID, worker and human status.

distinction: Unlike field-conflict-choice, no human chooses a winner between competing fields. The update mask structurally excludes human state, and a missing source does not mean deleting a person or closing a case.
limits: This illustrates a chosen reconciliation algorithm, not a guarantee about a deployed sync service.
Source completeness is an authored assumption. Missing is a flag, not proof that an entity no longer exists.
No cross-page transaction or conflict-resolution guarantee is implied.
No real product screen, external fetch, supplied code execution, or measured performance claim. All text is authored; no JSX, functions or URLs in props.

All existing records begin with missing-from-source=false in this bounded example. Thus every source-absent record is newly flagged; repeated-refresh and reappearance cases require separate inputs and are not implied.
verificationFocus: Default changes only A label, leaves B entirely unchanged and flags C. Every id/status/assignee stays identical. With identical sourceRows, derived write count is 0.

sourceRefs.rationale: Narrow upserts preserve user state, skip no-ops and flag missing keys rather than deleting them.

title: Combine the grants that actually apply
description: Candidate grants line up on a role ladder. Ineligible grants fold away and the highest remaining role determines access; a restricted resource removes the default app grant without removing explicit shares.
creativeDirection: 960x600 React/SVG, shared palette, deterministic 180 frames at 30fps. Frames 0-12 reveal the scene. Frames 13-52 place each candidate on the none/view/edit/admin ladder. Frames 53-100 close gates for disabled conditions and for the app default when restriction applies. Frames 101-139 raise a result marker to the maximum eligible rank or leave it at none, then compare that marker visibly against a separate required-role notch to resolve allowed or denied. Hold the resolved meaning during frames 140-165. Frames 166-179 return to the same opaque ground for a six-second loop; reset is editorial.
goodFor: Explain maximum role across qualifying shares
Show why restriction removes defaults but leaves explicit grants
intent: Resolve eligible grants and compare the result with an action requirement.

inputs.name: grants
inputs.description: Candidate grants and explicit qualification.
inputs.constraints: 1..5 unique ids, each 1..12 characters; labels 1..20 characters; roles ordered viewer<editor<admin; eligibility must be supplied, not inferred.

inputs.name: restricted
inputs.description: Exclude app-default candidates while retaining qualifying explicit grants.
inputs.constraints: Boolean; does not by itself make a resource private.

inputs.name: requiredRole
inputs.description: Minimum role for the illustrated action.
inputs.constraints: Access iff maximum surviving role is at least requiredRole.

inputs.name: labels
inputs.description: All visible role and decision labels.
inputs.constraints: Each 1..26 characters.

inputs.name: showExcludedGrants
inputs.description: Keep excluded grants visible beside their closed gates.
inputs.constraints: Boolean; restrictions and final rank remain visible.

bindingExample.shortSourceText: A restricted report has an editor app default, an eligible viewer team share and an ineligible admin direct share. The effective role is viewer, so editing remains denied.

distinction: Unlike capability-matrix, this computes a maximum over eligible grants and explains why a candidate is excluded. It is neither first-match precedence nor a blanket role inheritance ladder.
limits: Bounded grant composition only. Owner/admin short circuits, public publication and extra row-selection policies are outside this simplified algorithm.
No permissions are actually granted by this graphic.
No real product screen, external fetch, supplied code execution, or measured performance claim. All text is authored; no JSX, functions or URLs in props.
This simplified grant calculation excludes independent read-visibility policies. Do not infer every operation from one effective-role result.
verificationFocus: Default effective role is viewer and edit denied. Unrestrict gives editor and allows edit. Enabling direct admin gives admin. Reordering grant array never changes result; no eligible candidates produces none.

sourceRefs.rationale: Qualifying candidates combine by max rank, while restriction removes app defaults and group shares may require app access.

title: Save the change and its delivery obligation together
description: A local edit and its matching outbound journal entry sit under one transaction latch. Both become durable together, or neither does, so an accepted edit cannot lose the obligation to synchronize it.
creativeDirection: 960x600 React/SVG, shared palette, deterministic 180 frames at 30fps. Frames 0-12 reveal the scene. Frames 13-55 write a local change and matching journal ticket on two halves of one sheet. Frames 56-110 close one shared commit latch. Frames 111-139 stamp both halves when committed, or withdraw both provisional halves when aborted. Hold the resolved meaning during frames 140-165. Frames 166-179 return to the same opaque ground for a six-second loop; reset is editorial.
goodFor: Explain transactional outbox crash safety
Show that local persistence and sync obligations commit together
intent: Bind a durable local change to its durable synchronization obligation.

inputs.name: change
inputs.description: One local mutation and its correlation identifier.
inputs.constraints: id 1..16 characters; recordLabel <=28; before/after <=24 and distinct.

inputs.name: outcome
inputs.description: One atomic outcome for both durable effects.
inputs.constraints: Only listed values; cannot configure record and journal outcomes independently.

inputs.name: labels
inputs.description: Boundary and outcome copy.
inputs.constraints: Each 1..26 characters.

inputs.name: showIdentifier
inputs.description: Show matching mutation ID on the journal and changed record.
inputs.constraints: Boolean; the two representations remain paired.

inputs.name: copy
inputs.description: Visible example and phase labels.
inputs.constraints: All fields required; each 1..38 characters.

bindingExample.shortSourceText: Change the stock note from Count 2 to Count 3 and create delivery ticket edit-a in the same commit. The pending ticket survives with the local edit.

distinction: Journal-receipts starts with an existing outbox and closes obligations after acknowledgment. This explains how the obligation is created atomically with the source mutation before any network activity.
limits: The shared transaction boundary is an authored protocol assumption.
Atomic local commit does not imply exactly-once remote delivery.
No network success is depicted. The committed journal entry remains pending.
No real product screen, external fetch, supplied code execution, or measured performance claim. All text is authored; no JSX, functions or URLs in props.
verificationFocus: Commit updates local after and creates exactly one matching pending ticket. Abort preserves before and creates zero durable tickets. There is no sampled frame with only one half committed.

sourceRefs.rationale: The data write and outbox append share one local transaction.
The roadmap explicitly describes the engine as unbuilt.

title: Continue after the acknowledged byte
description: A bounded file strip crosses in chunks. After an interruption, the sender resumes at the stored acknowledgment offset while the already confirmed prefix stays in place.
creativeDirection: 960x600 React/SVG, shared palette, deterministic 180 frames at 30fps. Frames 0-12 reveal the scene. Frames 13-55 transfer chunks to the acknowledged boundary. Frames 56-90 interrupt one unacknowledged segment without adding it to confirmed progress. Frames 91-139 restart at the confirmed offset and append the remaining chunks. Hold the resolved meaning during frames 140-165. Frames 166-179 return to the same opaque ground for a six-second loop; reset is editorial.
goodFor: Explain resumable file uploads by acknowledged offset
Distinguish confirmed bytes from in-flight bytes
intent: Distinguish confirmed progress from work that must be retransmitted.

inputs.name: file
inputs.description: File size and chunk scale.
inputs.constraints: sizeBytes integer 2..100000; chunkBytes integer 1..sizeBytes; ceil(sizeBytes/chunkBytes) 2..6. label 1..28 characters.

inputs.name: acknowledgedBytes
inputs.description: Durable offset at interruption.
inputs.constraints: Integer >=0 and <sizeBytes; must be a chunk boundary.

inputs.name: finalOutcome
inputs.description: Whether resumed transfer finishes in the example.
inputs.constraints: Still-pending stops after one resumed chunk and requires remaining bytes afterward.

inputs.name: labels
inputs.description: Transport and unit labels.
inputs.constraints: Each 1..24 characters; unit fixed semantic bytes.

inputs.name: showOffsets
inputs.description: Show cumulative byte boundaries.
inputs.constraints: Boolean; total and confirmed byte counts remain visible.

bindingExample.shortSourceText: A 1200-byte file uses 400-byte chunks. After 400 bytes are acknowledged, an interruption occurs. Resume at byte 400 and finish the remaining 800 bytes.

distinction: Retry-backoff repeats whole attempts. This retains a confirmed prefix and resumes by byte offset, so interruption does not restart the entire file.
limits: Confirmed means acknowledged in this authored protocol, not independently verified integrity.
No compression ratio, transfer speed or duration is measured.
Final short chunk uses exact remaining bytes.
No real product screen, external fetch, supplied code execution, or measured performance claim. All text is authored; no JSX, functions or URLs in props.
verificationFocus: Default sends 400-byte confirmed prefix once, resumes at 400 and ends at 1200. For size 1100, final chunk is 300. No confirmed byte counted twice; confirmed+remaining=size.

sourceRefs.rationale: Resumable transfers persist acknowledged byte progress so interrupted uploads can continue.

title: Recover cells from page geometry
description: Positioned text on a schematic document acquires row and column boundaries, then becomes a table while the original page remains visible. A selected structural signal stays named.
creativeDirection: 960x600 React/SVG, shared palette, frame-driven 180 frames at 30fps. Frames 0-12 reveal the scene. Frames 13-55 draw the selected evidence: tagged-cell outlines, ruling lines or whitespace corridors. Frames 56-105 register the supplied text items inside their cells. Frames 106-139 unfold an equal-sized grid beside the page with every cell still linked to its source position. Hold the resolved relationship at frames 140-165, then fade to the same opaque ground at 166-179. Reset is editorial.
goodFor: Explain table extraction from PDF ruling lines
Distinguish tagged, ruled and inferred page structure
intent: Reveal the geometric evidence behind an extracted table.

inputs.name: grid
inputs.description: Logical cell contents and order.
inputs.constraints: 2..4 columns and 2..4 data rows; each row same column length; labels 1..16 characters; cells <=18 characters.

inputs.name: signal
inputs.description: Structural evidence shown before extraction.
inputs.constraints: Listed values only; whitespace must retain an inferred-layout label, not high-confidence certainty.

inputs.name: evidenceLabel
inputs.default: Ruling lines define the cell grid
inputs.description: Authored explanation of the signal.
inputs.constraints: 1..48 characters; describe selected signal.

inputs.name: showSourceLinks
inputs.description: Retain a source-position guide for the focal row.
inputs.constraints: Boolean; page and extracted grid always coexist.

inputs.name: copy
inputs.description: Visible context and region headings.
inputs.constraints: Each required string 1..34 characters.

bindingExample.shortSourceText: The page has columns Site and Items, with West 12 and East 8. Ruling lines define the four data cells, which copy into the extracted table without changing order.

inputBindings.evidenceLabel: Ruling lines define the cell grid

distinction: Unlike schema-mapping, field names are not translated. Cell structure is recovered from two-dimensional page evidence before textual data becomes a grid.
limits: The preset depicts a bounded supplied grid, not a general PDF detector.
The evidence signal is supplied and may be incomplete or misleading in a real document.
No OCR or image-only reading is implied.
No JSX, functions, URLs or external fetch in props. The animation is an authored explanation, not actual document extraction or product evidence.
verificationFocus: Every supplied data cell appears exactly once at its original row and column. Switching evidence signal changes the evidence choreography without changing values. Whitespace mode shows inference qualifier.

sourceRefs.rationale: Three different page-structure signals recover cell organization; the later region spec keeps auto detection outstanding.
Automatic table detection remains a separate outstanding phase.

title: Review a number near two labels
description: A figure on a schematic page measures its distance to two possible labels. A close runner-up leaves the pairing flagged until an authored human choice identifies the intended label.
creativeDirection: 960x600 React/SVG, shared palette, frame-driven 180 frames at 30fps. Frames 0-12 reveal the scene. Frames 13-50 reveal one numeric token and two nearby label boxes. Frames 51-95 extend distance guides from the token to both boxes. Frames 96-139 show either the reviewer choosing one label or an unresolved bracket retaining both candidates; the extracted row carries the same source position. Hold the resolved relationship at frames 140-165, then fade to the same opaque ground at 166-179. Reset is editorial.
goodFor: Explain uncertain number-to-label matching on a PDF map
Show human review of ambiguous proximity pairs
intent: Keep uncertain document associations reviewable.

inputs.name: figure
inputs.description: One literal printed figure and its page position.
inputs.constraints: text 1..12 characters; x,y finite 5..95 in a normalized schematic page.

inputs.name: labels
inputs.description: Candidate label anchor positions.
inputs.constraints: Exactly 2 unique ids <=12; text 1..20; x,y 5..95; neither coincides with figure; distinct distances or explicit tie.

inputs.name: ambiguityThreshold
inputs.description: Flag when nearest distance / next-nearest distance is at least this value.
inputs.constraints: Finite 0.5..1; distance is Euclidean normalized-page units; this ratio is not a probability.

inputs.name: reviewedLabelId
inputs.description: Authored human resolution or unresolved state.
inputs.constraints: Null or a labels id; review overrides nearest suggestion but never rewrites source token.

inputs.name: showDistanceValues
inputs.description: Show both distances and their ratio.
inputs.constraints: Boolean; uncertainty flag remains visible.

inputs.name: copy
inputs.description: Visible context and region headings.
inputs.constraints: Each required string 1..34 characters.

bindingExample.shortSourceText: The printed figure 24 lies between West area and East area. Its nearest-to-next distance ratio exceeds 0.8, so flag it; a reviewer assigns it to West area.

distinction: Unlike keyed-row-zipper, labels are associated by spatial evidence rather than equal keys. Unlike location-uncertainty-boundary, uncertainty concerns document interpretation, not a position on Earth.
limits: Distance is an association heuristic, not evidence that a number truly belongs to a region.
No default association should silently become accepted when a close alternative exists.
Source text stays unchanged after review.
No JSX, functions, URLs or external fetch in props. The animation is an authored explanation, not actual document extraction or product evidence.
verificationFocus: Default ratio is above 0.8 and must flag ambiguity. Null reviewedLabelId leaves unresolved. An accepted farther label follows human choice, with the original two distances retained.

sourceRefs.locator: The proximity experiment; Shape 2; User flow
sourceRefs.rationale: Proximity pairing can silently misassociate labels; the design requires uncertainty flags and inspectable source positions.

title: Carry the unit and qualifier with the number
description: An authored sentence separates into subject, metric, value, unit and period strips that assemble into an observation row. Uncertainty qualifiers remain attached to the value.
creativeDirection: 960x600 React/SVG, shared palette, frame-driven 180 frames at 30fps. Frames 0-12 reveal the scene. Frames 13-55 underline the supplied sentence fragments with distinct patterns. Frames 56-110 move copies of those exact fragments into labeled observation slots. Frames 111-139 hold the original sentence above the structured row and keep the qualifier visible. Hold the resolved relationship at frames 140-165, then fade to the same opaque ground at 166-179. Reset is editorial.
goodFor: Explain extracting structured observations from prose
Preserve units, reporting periods and approximation qualifiers
intent: Preserve the context that gives a number meaning.

inputs.name: fragments
inputs.description: Sentence fragments in reading order with authored semantic spans; the extracted cell is text.slice(contentStart,contentEnd).trim().
inputs.constraints: 6..9 unique ids, each 1..12 characters; text 1..30 characters; total sentence <=110; exactly one subject,metric,value,unit,period,qualifier; optional connector fragments require contentStart=contentEnd=0. For semantic fragments, 0<=contentStart<contentEnd<=text.length, integer UTF-16 indices; resulting trimmed substring must be 1..20 characters. Value substring must match a finite plain decimal number, with optional leading minus, no exponent or thousands separators.

inputs.name: showSourceSpans
inputs.description: Keep underlines on the exact selected character spans in the source sentence.
inputs.constraints: Boolean; extracted values are always derived from these spans even when guides are hidden.

inputs.name: method
inputs.description: Visible extraction method, separate from review state.
inputs.constraints: Only listed values; method never determines confidence.

inputs.name: reviewState
inputs.description: Authored status of the structured observation.
inputs.constraints: Only listed values; needs-review remains labeled at final hold.

inputs.name: copy
inputs.description: Visible context and region headings.
inputs.constraints: Each required string 1..34 characters.

bindingExample.shortSourceText: West site reported about 12 crates received in week 2. Extract subject, metric, value, unit, period and About qualifier using rules, and keep the row flagged for review.

distinction: Unlike word-reveal, the action changes a sentence into an observation schema with explicit semantic roles, not merely typography. Value and unit cannot detach from period or qualifier.
limits: No automatic language understanding or verified factual extraction is performed.
One sentence and one observation only; multi-clause ambiguities require a longer scene.
Method and confidence are separate. A model-produced row is not inherently correct.
No JSX, functions, URLs or external fetch in props. The animation is an authored explanation, not actual document extraction or product evidence.

Every output field derives only from its corresponding role fragment by the specified substring and whitespace trim. Preserve casing; numeric value alone converts the exact selected plain-decimal substring with Number. No independent normalized-row prop may contradict the source.
verificationFocus: Derive subject West site, metric received, value 12, unit crates, period week 2 and qualifier about from the exact spans. Changing a span changes only that field. Switching extraction method does not alter review state, source text or extracted values. No output field can be independently supplied.

sourceRefs.locator: Shape 1; The observations schema; Model assistance
sourceRefs.rationale: Prose observations retain subject, unit, time and qualifier, while production method and confidence are independent.

title: Read the same fields across repeated sections
description: Repeated labeled paragraphs unfold into rows of one table. Shared run-in labels become columns, and an absent section stays missing instead of shifting neighboring text into its place.
creativeDirection: 960x600 React/SVG, shared palette, frame-driven 180 frames at 30fps. Frames 0-12 reveal the scene. Frames 13-55 reveal repeated heading blocks with their field labels. Frames 56-105 line up equal labels vertically and rotate the block organization into a compact row-based table. Frames 106-139 hold each block beside its row with an explicit missing cell. Hold the resolved relationship at frames 140-165, then fade to the same opaque ground at 166-179. Reset is editorial.
goodFor: Explain turning repeated labeled sections into a table
Preserve absent fields during document extraction
intent: Expose tabular structure inside repeated prose sections.

inputs.name: fields
inputs.description: Shared section labels become table columns.
inputs.constraints: 2..3 unique ids <=12; labels 1..18 characters.

inputs.name: blocks
inputs.description: Ordered sections and complete cell membership.
inputs.constraints: 2..3 unique blocks; heading 1..20; exactly one cell per field id in every block; text 1..26 characters or null. blocks[].id has a maximum of 12 characters, with no added minimum or normalization. Exact references inherit that target bound; an empty ID and matching empty reference remain valid subject to the existing uniqueness/reference rules.

inputs.name: missingLabel
inputs.description: Label for an absent field.
inputs.constraints: 1..20 characters; never replace missing with zero or empty-looking spacing.

inputs.name: showBlockNumbers
inputs.description: Add derived ordinal labels to sections and output rows.
inputs.constraints: Boolean; ordinals follow array order, not identity.

inputs.name: copy
inputs.description: Visible context and region headings.
inputs.constraints: Each required string 1..34 characters.

bindingExample.shortSourceText: Site West lists Action: Repair tap and Need: Spare seal. Site East lists Action: Check pump with no need stated. Make two rows and keep East Need missing.

distinction: Unlike schema-mapping, the field labels already match. The animation reveals a tabular structure concealed by repeated prose layout and preserves absent cells.
limits: Authored, exact field alignment only; no inference from headings.
Does not imply that the original document contained a printed table.
Multicolumn reading-order ambiguity is excluded from this compact example.
No JSX, functions, URLs or external fetch in props. The animation is an authored explanation, not actual document extraction or product evidence.
verificationFocus: Default yields two rows and two fields; East Need remains Not stated. Reorder fields and output columns follow without moving values to a different semantic field.

sourceRefs.rationale: Repeated headings with run-in labels can form a table even without a printed grid.

title: Turn each measurement into a row
description: A wide table unfolds each measure column into its own observation row while repeating the correct subject and preserving the measurement name and unit.
creativeDirection: 960x600 React/SVG, shared palette, frame-driven 180 frames at 30fps. Frames 0-12 reveal the scene. Frames 13-50 reveal a two-measure wide table. Frames 51-110 peel the measure columns into vertical strips, carrying a subject-key copy with each cell. Frames 111-139 stack the strips as a long observation ledger with explicit measure and unit columns. Hold the resolved relationship at frames 140-165, then fade to the same opaque ground at 166-179. Reset is editorial.
goodFor: Explain unpivoting wide measurements to a long table
Show how reshaping changes grain without creating measurements
intent: Explain a change in measurement grain while preserving values.

inputs.name: measures
inputs.description: Columns being unpivoted.
inputs.constraints: Exactly 2 unique measure ids <=12; labels 1..18; units 1..12 characters.

inputs.name: subjects
inputs.description: Source rows and exact measure values.
inputs.constraints: Exactly 2 unique subjects; label 1..18; exactly one value per measure id; finite -10000..10000 or null. subjects[].id has a maximum of 12 characters, with no added minimum or normalization. Exact references inherit that target bound; an empty ID and matching empty reference remain valid subject to the existing uniqueness/reference rules.

inputs.name: missingPolicy
inputs.description: Whether missing cells stay as rows or a visible omission count.
inputs.constraints: Missing never becomes zero; source measurement-cell count = output row count + omitted missing count.

inputs.name: showSourceGuides
inputs.description: Retain row/column guides to the original cells.
inputs.constraints: Boolean; subject/measure IDs remain semantically matched.

inputs.name: copy
inputs.description: Visible context and region headings.
inputs.constraints: Each required string 1..34 characters.

bindingExample.shortSourceText: Site A received 12 crates and used 8; Site B received 5 and has no used value. Produce one row per site and measure, retaining the missing cell.

distinction: Unlike source-merge, no datasets converge and no values are combined. Output grain changes from one row per subject to one row per subject-measure pair.
limits: A reshape is not a new observation or a recalculation.
Units may differ across measures and therefore must travel per row.
Duplicate subject labels remain distinct by ID.
No JSX, functions, URLs or external fetch in props. The animation is an authored explanation, not actual document extraction or product evidence.

Conservation counts only measurement cells: subjects.length*measures.length equals output measurement rows plus explicitly omitted missing measurement cells. Subject labels, headers and identifiers are not measurement cells.
verificationFocus: Defaults yield four output rows including one missing value. Omit-with-ledger yields three rows plus one omitted missing cell. Every output key pair is unique and traces to one source cell.

sourceRefs.rationale: A true table can be kept wide or reshaped to one row per number.
Different regions can normalize to a common observation schema with retained units and provenance.

title: Check that the saved region still points to the same content
description: A saved page region reopens at the same geometry, while its header and content fingerprint are compared with the new document. A mismatch holds the replacement for review rather than silently repointing by table number.
creativeDirection: 960x600 React/SVG, shared palette, frame-driven 180 frames at 30fps. Frames 0-12 reveal the scene. Frames 13-50 align saved and current page outlines at the same region coordinates. Frames 51-100 compare the header and fingerprint tags independently. Frames 101-139 either register a match or close a review latch when either tag differs. Hold the resolved relationship at frames 140-165, then fade to the same opaque ground at 166-179. Reset is editorial.
goodFor: Explain why PDF table ordinal numbers are unstable identifiers
Show a saved region fingerprint detecting source drift
intent: Detect changed source content without relying on unstable ordinal labels.

inputs.name: saved
inputs.description: Saved geometric source pointer and authored fingerprint.
inputs.constraints: page integer 1..20; box [left,top,right,bottom] with 0<=left<right<=100 and 0<=top<bottom<=100; header <=30; fingerprint 1..16.

inputs.name: current
inputs.description: Current region content and unrelated detector table number.
inputs.constraints: header <=30; fingerprint 1..16; ordinal integer 1..9; ordinal does not determine identity.

inputs.name: labels
inputs.description: Comparison and outcome labels.
inputs.constraints: Each 1..30 characters.

inputs.name: showDetectorOrdinal
inputs.description: Display that detector numbering may change independently.
inputs.constraints: Boolean; never use this ordinal to select a new region.

inputs.name: copy
inputs.description: Visible context and region headings.
inputs.constraints: Each required string 1..34 characters.

bindingExample.shortSourceText: Reopen page 2 at the saved region for Site | Items. The new detector calls it table 4, but its fingerprint changed from FP-A to FP-B, so hold replacement for review.

distinction: Unlike revision-restore, nothing rolls back. The saved geometric locator stays fixed while a content-identity test detects drift that table numbering alone cannot detect.
limits: Fingerprints are supplied opaque labels, not real cryptographic hashes generated by the renderer.
A matching fingerprint is only the illustrative comparator result, not authenticity or tamper-proofing.
Changing page layout may invalidate geometry and requires a separate review.
No JSX, functions, URLs or external fetch in props. The animation is an authored explanation, not actual document extraction or product evidence.

sourceRefs.locator: Data model / Why geometry rather than an ordinal index
sourceRefs.rationale: Table numbering can change with detector versions; persisted geometry plus fingerprint notices source drift.

title: Freeze the selected data for a published view

Frames 56-95 copy them into a separate snapshot frame with a revision label. Frames 96-139 alter only the authored live cell, preserving the frozen publication and its revision. Hold the resolved relationship at frames 140-165, then fade to the same opaque ground at 166-179. Reset is editorial.
goodFor: Explain immutable published snapshots of selected data
Show live-source edits diverging from a shared revision
intent: Separate live data from a bounded frozen publication.

inputs.name: table
inputs.description: Complete source table.
inputs.constraints: 2..4 unique columns and 2..4 unique rows; each cells length equals columns length; all text <=18 characters. The inclusive text maximum covers table.columns[].id and table.rows[].id, with no added minimum or normalization. Selection and liveEdit references inherit the 18-character bound through exact target membership.

inputs.name: selection
inputs.description: Exact rows and columns copied.
inputs.constraints: Unique nonempty subsets of table IDs; no inferred privacy review.

inputs.name: liveEdit
inputs.description: Source edit after snapshot creation.
inputs.constraints: IDs must reference table and selected slice; value <=18 characters and different from original.

inputs.name: publication
inputs.description: Frozen revision and explicit audience.
inputs.constraints: revision/label 1..24 characters; audience must be visible and is not inferred from selected fields.

inputs.name: showExcludedCells
inputs.description: Keep unselected source cells visible locally.
inputs.constraints: Boolean; excluded cells never appear in snapshot.

inputs.name: copy
inputs.description: Visible context and region headings.
inputs.constraints: Each required string 1..34 characters.

bindingExample.shortSourceText: Publish Site and Items for West 12 and East 8 to an internal Revision 1 snapshot. Exclude Internal note. A later West edit to 15 changes only the live table.

Selected data may still be sensitive; selection alone is no anonymization guarantee.
No JSX, functions, URLs or external fetch in props. The animation is an authored explanation, not actual document extraction or product evidence.

sourceRefs.rationale: Publishing materializes configured slices and loads published dependencies separately.
Published snapshot ownership is scoped to dashboard and revision.

Contrast filtered views with an unchanged all-records reference

inputs.name: metric

inputs.name: showExcludedRecords
inputs.description: Retain filtered-out rows as clearly excluded ghosts.
inputs.constraints: Boolean; excluded rows never count in subscribed results.

inputs.name: copy
inputs.description: Visible context and region headings.

inputs.name: locations
inputs.description: Original positions and deterministic authored offsets.
inputs.constraints: 1..3 unique ids; labels <=20; coordinates 10..90; offsets finite; displaced points 0..100; Euclidean offset <=radiusUnits. locations[].id has a maximum of 12 characters, with no added minimum or normalization. Exact references inherit that target bound; an empty ID and matching empty reference remain valid subject to the existing uniqueness/reference rules.

inputs.name: radiusUnits
inputs.description: Bound for the supplied displacement, in schematic grid units.
inputs.constraints: Finite >0 and <=20; no metre or uncertainty claim.

inputs.name: labels
inputs.description: Distinct precision and disclosure labels.
inputs.constraints: Each 1..30 characters.

inputs.name: showLocalOriginal
inputs.description: Show original position only inside the local inset.
inputs.constraints: Boolean; never reveal original coordinates on display-copy map.

inputs.name: copy
inputs.description: Visible geography and phase qualifiers.
inputs.constraints: All required; each 1..40 characters; context must identify schematic illustration.

bindingExample.shortSourceText: Displace Location A by (6,4) and Location B by (-5,3), both within a ten-unit bound. Retain original positions locally and label display copies approximate.

distinction: Location-uncertainty-boundary depicts uncertainty already present in evidence. This intentionally changes a display copy under a supplied disclosure policy and labels the difference.
limits: Displacement does not guarantee anonymity, safety, k-anonymity or differential privacy.
The bound is displacement from the source, not confidence radius around the true position.
No fresh randomness; offsets are supplied and deterministic.
No live geography, online routing, JSX, functions, URLs, private records or external requests. Maps are schematic local plans; no real-world inference follows.
verificationFocus: Every displacement length<=radiusUnits. Public copy never labels original x/y. Zero offset is allowed but still labeled approximate policy; invalid bound rejects configuration. Before disclosure the public display is empty. For every location, the first and every subsequent public position equals only (x+offsetX,y+offsetY). No trail connects the display marker to its source coordinate.

sourceRefs.rationale: Sensitivity policy includes jitter/centroid displacement separately from aggregate-only release.

title: A smooth surface depends on its radius
description: Each supplied point contributes a bounded kernel to a schematic grid. The kernels add into one intensity field, then a second radius changes the smoothing without creating or deleting any point observations.
creativeDirection: 960x600 React/SVG with shared palette, deterministic 180 frames at 30fps. Reveal at frames 0-12. Frames 13-55 raise a small cone over each point. Frames 56-105 add cone heights into a sampled grid intensity. Frames 106-139 widen or narrow every cone to the second radius and recompute the grid while point markers stay fixed. Hold the resolved state at 140-165; fade to the same opaque ground at 166-179. Reset is editorial.
goodFor: Explain how a heatmap radius changes smoothing
Distinguish modeled intensity from observed cell counts
intent: Expose smoothing assumptions without presenting intensity as observed counts.

inputs.name: points
inputs.description: Weighted fictional observations.
inputs.constraints: 2..5 unique ids 1..12 characters; x,y finite 0..100; weight finite >0..5.

inputs.name: radii
inputs.description: Two smoothing radii in normalized grid units.
inputs.constraints: Both finite 5..40 and distinct; kernel at cell center=max(0,1-distance/radius)*weight.

inputs.name: gridSize
inputs.description: Number of sample cells per grid axis.
inputs.constraints: Integer 6..12; intensity sampled at exact cell centers; no count conservation claim for summed cell intensities.

inputs.name: legendMaximum
inputs.description: Fixed intensity legend ceiling for both states.
inputs.constraints: Finite >=sum(points.weight) and <=25; no automatic rescaling.

inputs.name: labels
inputs.description: Explicit smoothing and non-count units.
inputs.constraints: Each 1..28 characters.

inputs.name: showKernels
inputs.description: Retain faint kernel boundaries after combination.
inputs.constraints: Boolean; original point markers stay visible.

bindingExample.shortSourceText: Spread three unit-weight points using cone kernels. Increase radius from 15 to 30 grid units while keeping the same points and fixed intensity legend maximum 5.

distinction: Spatial-grid-binning assigns each point once to an exact count cell. This spreads each contribution across neighboring cells and makes radius a visible modeling choice.
limits: This specified cone kernel is an instructional design, not a claim about a mapping library kernel.
Intensity is neither case count, population, probability nor risk. Grid cell intensities do not sum to point count.
A smooth field does not fill gaps in actual observations or establish conditions between points.
No external requests, URLs, JSX or functions in props. Supplied examples are fictional.
verificationFocus: Every sampled cell equals sum(weight*max(0,1-distance/radius)). Radius change preserves point count and legend scale. A cell beyond all radii has zero modeled intensity, explicitly not observed zero population.

sourceRefs.rationale: Heatmap symbology has a weight, radius and ramp, distinct from clustering and binning.

title: A buffer is a distance rule
description: A schematic point emits an equal-distance envelope. Nearby supplied locations are classified by the explicit straight-line radius, while a distance ruler shows that the envelope is not a travel-time boundary.
creativeDirection: 960x600 React/SVG with shared palette, deterministic 180 frames at 30fps. Reveal at frames 0-12. Frames 13-50 anchor the center and radius ruler. Frames 51-105 sweep a compass arm to draw the distance circle. Frames 106-139 compare each location distance with the radius and collect only qualifying IDs in a separate ledger. Hold the resolved state at 140-165; fade to the same opaque ground at 166-179. Reset is editorial.
goodFor: Explain straight-line distance buffers
Distinguish distance inclusion from actual service access
intent: Define straight-line spatial inclusion without implying travel access.

inputs.name: origin
inputs.description: The buffer center in a local schematic plane.
inputs.constraints: label 1..24 characters; x,y 20..80.

inputs.name: locations
inputs.description: The complete illustrated classification set.
inputs.constraints: 2..6 unique ids 1..12; labels <=20; x,y 0..100.

inputs.name: radiusUnits
inputs.description: Euclidean distance threshold.
inputs.constraints: Finite >0..40; origin plus envelope must fit inside 0..100 in both axes; distance<=radius includes boundary.

inputs.name: labels
inputs.description: Distance units and scope qualifier.
inputs.constraints: Each 1..44 characters; qualifier must remain visible.

inputs.name: showDistances
inputs.description: Show origin-to-location rulers and values.
inputs.constraints: Boolean; threshold remains labeled.

inputs.name: copy
inputs.description: Visible source and example qualifiers.
inputs.constraints: Each required string 1..36 characters.

bindingExample.shortSourceText: Draw a radius-30 envelope around (50,50). Locations at (60,50) and (70,70) lie within it; (90,50) lies beyond it. This is distance, not travel time.

distinction: Catchment-union-gaps combines supplied coverage polygons. This derives a buffer from a distance rule and classifies points without inferring service use or routes.
limits: No real ground-distance projection or travel network is used.
Inside a distance buffer does not imply access, safety, capacity or service coverage.
Only the supplied locations form the denominator.
No external requests, URLs, JSX or functions in props. Supplied examples are fictional.
verificationFocus: Default distances A=10,B=sqrt(800),C=40; radius30 includes A and B. A location exactly on boundary is included once. Radius change never moves origin or locations.

sourceRefs.rationale: Buffer and distance analysis are explicit geometric operations, distinct from travel-time isochrones.

title: Keep the late value that changes the column
description: A column initially appears numeric. A later text value widens the proposed type to text while every original cell stays intact, showing why a short initial sample must not silently discard contrary evidence.
creativeDirection: 960x600 React/SVG with shared palette, deterministic 180 frames at 30fps. Reveal at frames 0-12. Frames 13-55 reveal the initial numeric-looking rows under a provisional numeric type label. Frames 56-100 append the authored text row and open a type-review bracket. Frames 101-139 widen the column type to text or hold the import for review according to policy, preserving all input values. Hold the resolved state at 140-165; fade to the same opaque ground at 166-179. Reset is editorial.
goodFor: Explain import inference challenged by a late text value
Show why all source rows must survive schema review
intent: Preserve contrary late evidence during column-type inference.

inputs.name: values
inputs.description: Complete source strings in order.
inputs.constraints: 3..6 strings 1..16 characters; first 2..5 must be finite decimal numeric strings; final must be nonnumeric; no null ambiguity in this preset.

inputs.name: policy
inputs.description: Explicit response to late contradictory evidence.
inputs.constraints: Neither policy may drop, coerce to null or truncate the late value.

inputs.name: labels
inputs.description: Type and import-state labels.
inputs.constraints: Each 1..30 characters.

inputs.name: showOriginalStrings
inputs.description: Retain exact original lexical forms beside output.
inputs.constraints: Boolean; visible final cell contents still preserve all strings.

inputs.name: copy
inputs.description: Visible source and example qualifiers.
inputs.constraints: Each required string 1..36 characters.

bindingExample.shortSourceText: A column begins 12, 8 and 4, then contains Pending. Widen the proposed numeric type to text while preserving all four original strings.

distinction: Cell-normalization edits explicitly supplied characters. This changes a proposed column type in response to late evidence while refusing to change or discard any cell.
limits: The widening rule is illustrative, not a claim that all import engines infer types this way.
Text preservation does not make the column ready for numeric aggregation.
One column and one contradictory value are shown; general type lattices and date inference are outside scope.
No external requests, URLs, JSX or functions in props. Supplied examples are fictional.
verificationFocus: Default output retains 12,8,4,Pending in original order. Widen yields text type; hold yields no completed import. Both retain four rows and cannot replace Pending with null.

sourceRefs.rationale: The fixture tests a late prose value after numeric rows to prevent aborted imports or dropped rows.
